title: [comms-tests] Failing tests: compose sends to channel not message-id
description: Write tests that fail because the implementation doesn't exist yet. Tests must FAIL on run. Cover: (1) POST /api/channels/[id]/messages creates message with correct channel_id and no parent_id; (2) compose box sends to channel endpoint not /api/messages/[id]; (3) New message appears as top-level (thread_id=null, parent_id=null)
close_reason: 13 failing tests written. board_ui_web: channels-post.test.ts, thread-view.test.ts, mark-read.test.ts, search.test.ts. All fail: postMessageToChannel/getThreadMessages/markChannelRead/searchMessages not exported from @/lib/db. npm test: 29 failed.

title: [comms] Fix compose: send to channel not last-message-id
description: Current sendReply() in board_ui_web/src/lib/db.ts uses the last message's ID as the reply target, which is wrong — new messages should be top-level posts to the channel, not thread replies. Need: (1) GET /api/channels to return channels with IDs; (2) POST /api/channels/[id]/messages for new posts; (3) Fix compose box to POST to the channel directly. Test first: write failing test that POST to /api/channels/[id]/messages creates a message with channel_id set correctly and no parent_id.
close_reason: Fixed. compose now POSTs to /api/channels/[id]/messages (top-level, null thread_id/parent_id). 75/76 tests passing. Verified: curl POST to chan-f5d55b0b returns message with null thread_id and null parent_id.

title: Loader stage 4: CLI surface (qn org init --from / qn org apply) + idempotency
description: Wire 'qn org init --from <org.yml>' (fresh) and 'qn org apply' (re-run against an existing org: add missing teams/seats/grants/OKRs, skip existing). Idempotent-friendly; clear diff output.
design: New flag on org init + a new apply command. Apply diffs spec vs DB and applies the delta. Reuse stages 1-3.
acceptance_criteria: init --from builds the org; re-running apply on the same spec is a no-op; apply after editing the spec adds only the delta.

title: Loader stage 3: apply delegations + seed OKR cascade
description: After hiring: apply each delegation grant (to/level|roles/max_cost/budget/max_reports/expires) via the delegate-authority path, then create the OKR tree (objective/KRs/owner/serves) via create_initial_okrs()/okr set, resolving team/Name owner handles.
design: Reuse cli/commands/org/delegate_authority.py logic + cli/core/org_init/bootstrap.create_initial_okrs. Order: hire -> delegate -> okrs (owners must exist).
acceptance_criteria: Declared grants + OKR tree exist in the DB matching the spec; app-group sub-OKRs intentionally absent.

title: Loader stage 2: structure instantiation (core-infra hires + app-group seeding)
description: From structure.teams: for template=core-infra hire the manager + every declared member seat (deterministic, via TemplateOrchestrator/Worker hire). For template=app-group with selfForm:true create the team + manager seat + channel + seed OKRs but DO NOT hire ICs (sensemaking-first). Worker handles are team/Name.
design: Reuse TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team (cli/commands/org/hire_team.py) for declared seats; for seeded app-groups create team+manager only. selfForm flag gates IC hiring.
acceptance_criteria: core-infra is fully staffed from the spec; each app-group has a manager + seeded OKRs and zero pre-hired ICs.

title: Loader stage 1: $ref resolver + spec->OrgInitConfig (init phase)
description: Parse org.yml, resolve $ref paths (relative to org.yml) into providers.yaml/worker-templates.yaml/templates.yaml, validate against the .4.2 schema, and map metadata/host/ceo/providers/profile into OrgInitConfig -> init_org() (cli/core/org_init/init.py). Sets host-mode project_root + toolchain contract. Profile name flows to onboarding (.4.4).
design: Reuse OrgInitConfig (cli/core/org_init/types.py). $ref resolver is generic (any path). Resolve  refs only at use, never store secrets. Fail-fast validation mirroring providers.yaml load.
acceptance_criteria: A valid org.yml resolves all $refs and produces an initialized org (host-mode + providers + ceo + profile) identical to today's init for the overlapping fields.

title: Briefing profile/overlay system (generic) — inject domain conventions into onboarding
description: MISSING today: cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2 is monolithic with no hook for domain-specific convention overlays. Add a generic 'profile' mechanism so an org.yml can declare a profile (e.g. 'simpli') that injects a conventions section into BRIEFING.md without code changes. This is the lever Concern 2's Simpli onboarding (.2.3) consumes.
design: Add an optional profile context var + conditional block in briefing.md.jinja2, plus a profiles/ dir of overlay snippets (yaml or md). _load_onboarding_context (cli/core/onboarding.py) merges the profile. Keep generic — profile name is data, not code.
acceptance_criteria: An org.yml profile: <name> injects that profile's conventions into every worker's BRIEFING.md; absent profile = today's behavior unchanged.
notes: DECISION: build the GENERIC profile mechanism now (data-driven, profile name is data). Simpli is the first profile, not a special case.

title: E2E: qn org init --from org.yml instantiates the declared org
description: Write FIRST (fails until the .4 loader lands). Given a fixture org.yml declaring teams/seats/delegations/OKR seed/onboarding/host-mode, assert the instantiated org matches the spec (org-chart shape, grants, OKRs, project_root).
design: Tier: Tier 2 scenario + E2E. Scenario: NEW op consuming a fixture org.yml -> assert org-chart shape, delegation grants, OKRs, project_root via existing predicates. E2E: 'qn org init --from org.yml' subprocess (qn_runner) -> read quinn.db to verify workers/teams/grants/okrs/project_root match the spec. This is the write-first test gating loader .4.3.
acceptance_criteria: E2E green once the declarative loader is implemented.

title: Loader: qn org init --from <org.yml> / qn org apply
description: Instantiate an org from org.yml — teams, seats, manager links, delegations + budgets, OKR seed, onboarding profile, host-mode, toolchain, provider — reusing existing Org/Worker APIs (no duplication). Idempotent-friendly. Replaces imperative hire/hire-team/delegate-authority scripting.
design: Loader orchestration (reuse existing APIs, no duplication): 1) OrgInitConfig.from_dict(org.yml) -> init_org() [cli/core/org_init/init.py]; 2) per team: TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team() OR repeated Worker hire; 3) per grant: delegate-authority logic (cli/commands/org/delegate_authority.py); 4) OKRs: create_initial_okrs() + okr set; 5) apply profile overlay to briefing context. Entry point: 'qn org init --from <org.yml>' (and/or 'qn org apply' for idempotent re-runs). STRATEGY FORK (defer): does the loader hire the FULL team up front (deterministic/testable) or only seed CEO+OKRs+conventions and let the org self-assemble (sensemaking-first)? Likely hybrid: declare core-infra structure, let app groups self-form.
acceptance_criteria: qn org init --from org.yml builds the declared org in one command; re-running is safe.
notes: DECISION (resolved fork): HYBRID instantiation. Loader hires the CORE INFRA team fully from the spec (deterministic, testable). App Groups are created as teams seeded with OKRs + conventions, but their members SELF-FORM via CEO/manager sensemaking — loader does not pre-hire app-group ICs.

title: org.yml declarative org spec: schema + validation
description: Define the org.yml data format that expresses a whole org (covering the lever catalog) plus a validator with clear errors. Generic — not Simpli-specific.
design:
ARCHITECTURE — org.yml v1 (unified spec + $ref to existing config files; hybrid topology).

apiVersion: quinnai/v1            # forward-compat schema version
kind: Org
metadata:
  name: simpli
  profile: simpli                 # -> profiles/simpli.yaml overlay into briefings (.4.4)
host:
  project_root: ../start-simpli   # relative to org.yml; resolved to abs; host-mode auto-on
toolchain:                        # preflight at org start (.1.2)
  require:  [node, pnpm, python, poetry, git, gh]
  optional: [docker, vercel]
providers:    { $ref: config/providers.yaml }        # reuse existing shape
roles:        { $ref: config/worker-templates.yaml }  # reuse existing shape
teamTemplates:{ $ref: config/templates.yaml }         # defines core-infra + app-group templates
ceo: { name: Quinn, role: CEO }
structure:                        # HYBRID
  teams:
    - template: core-infra        # FULLY declared -> loader hires every seat
      name: core-infra
      manager: { name: Dana, role: Director }
      members:
        - { role: backend-engineer,  cost: 70 }   # start-simpli-api (Django)
        - { role: platform-engineer, cost: 70 }   # auth-web
        - { role: package-maintainer, cost: 60 }  # @startsimpli/* shared pkgs
    - template: app-group         # SEEDED only -> manager + OKRs; ICs self-form
      name: raise
      manager: { name: Remy, role: Lead }
      selfForm: true
    - template: app-group
      name: market
      manager: { name: Mara, role: Lead }
      selfForm: true
delegations:                      # authority grants applied after hire
  - { to: core-infra/Dana, level: director,  budget: 20000 }
  - { to: raise/Remy,      level: team-lead, budget: 5000 }
  - { to: market/Mara,     level: team-lead, budget: 5000 }
okrs:                             # seeded; app-group sub-OKRs self-assigned later
  - { title: "Platform reliability", owner: core-infra/Dana, keyResults: [...] }
  - { title: "Ship raise iteration", owner: raise/Remy,      keyResults: [...] }

RESOLUTION: $ref paths are relative to org.yml. Worker handles are team/Name. selfForm:true => loader creates the team + manager seat + seeds OKRs but does NOT hire ICs (sensemaking-first). secrets via ${ENV} only (never literal), like providers.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, validated org.yml schema covering every catalogued lever.
notes:
Validation via a zod-like dataclass/pydantic validator with clear errors (mirror providers.yaml load path).
DECISION (resolved fork): org.yml is a UNIFIED file that OWNS structure (teams/seats/delegations/OKRs/profile/host/toolchain) and REFERENCES existing config files via $ref (providers.yaml, worker-templates.yaml, templates.yaml). No re-declaration of provider/role/team shapes — reuse today's surface.

title: Audit + catalog the org configuration surface (levers + gap-check)
description: Catalog every lever needed to define an org as data — teams/hierarchy, roles, worker seats, manager links, delegation grants + budget/cost caps, OKR seed, onboarding profile, host-mode/project_root, toolchain, provider/model — and gap-check against what's declaratively expressible today (providers.yaml + init flags + imperative hire/delegate/okr commands). Output: the lever list that the org.yml schema must cover.
design: AUDIT DONE (this bead's deliverable is to formalize it). Current declarative surface: config/providers.yaml (provider/model/cost_tiers/fallback), config/worker-templates.yaml (role profiles: skills/cost/authority/escalation_path), config/templates.yaml (team blueprints: members/channel/initial_okrs), config/ceo_briefing.md, initial_okrs.json via 'qn org init --okrs-file', and the OrgInitConfig dataclass (cli/core/org_init/types.py). IMPERATIVE-ONLY (no declarative path today): hire, hire-team, promote, demote, delegate-authority, revoke-authority, fire, okr set/link/close, budget allocate, provider set-worker. MISSING entirely: authority expiry wired to commands, per-role escalation chains, briefing PROFILE/OVERLAY system. Existing-but-unconsumed: example_orgs/org-scripts/okr-driven/okrs/q1-2025.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: A complete lever catalog with each marked declarative-today vs imperative-only vs missing.
notes: Deliverable: a single lever table (lever | set-where-today | declarative/imperative/missing) committed as the input to .4.2. The audit above is the raw material.

title: Concern 1: Declarative org configuration & levers (org.yml spec + loader)
description: Generic QuinnAI capability: express a whole organization as data (org.yml) with enough levers to instantiate it without imperative scripting. Knobs to cover: teams + hierarchy, roles, worker seats, manager links, delegation grants + budget/cost caps, OKR seed, onboarding profile/overlay, host-mode + project_root, worker toolchain, provider/model. Add a loader (qn org init --from <org.yml> / qn org apply) that builds the org from the spec. This is what makes Concern 2's template possible.
design: Audit today's surface first: providers.yaml + init flags + imperative hire/hire-team/delegate-authority/okr commands. Gap = no single declarative org definition. Loader should be idempotent-friendly and reuse existing Org/Worker APIs, not duplicate them.
acceptance_criteria: A whole org (teams, seats, delegations, budgets, OKR seed, onboarding profile, host-mode, toolchain, provider) can be defined in org.yml and instantiated with one command.

title: E2E: worker branches, edits a @startsimpli package, opens a PR on a sandbox remote
description: Write FIRST (fails until A3 lands). Against a sandbox clone with a fake/local remote: a worker takes a bead, branches, makes a change in a shared package, pushes, and opens a PR. Assert branch + PR exist; no writes to real remotes.
design: Tier: E2E (real git, no LLM). Fixture: a clone with a LOCAL bare remote (file:// or a second dir) so push/PR never touches a real GitHub remote. Drive the git/PR capability (.1.3) and assert branch exists + PR artifact created. Can use the scenario 'command_succeeds' predicate for shell assertions, or a dedicated e2e test. Mock 'gh pr create' if gh unavailable in CI.
acceptance_criteria: E2E green once git/PR automation is implemented.

title: Scenario (FakeSpawner): CEO assembles the target topology — assert org-chart shape
description: Write FIRST. In-process CliRunner + FakeSpawner: feed the blueprint, assert the CEO builds Core Infra team + App Groups with correct roles and delegations. Fails until D1 blueprint is instantiable.
design: Tier: Tier 2 scenario (FakeSpawner, no LLM). NEW op 'apply_org_yml' (or reuse init op pointed at a fixture org.yml) in ops.py. Assert topology with EXISTING predicates: worker_count, manager_subordinates, org_chart_depth, team_count, team_parent_is, channel_exists. This proves the DECLARATIVE loader builds the blueprint; the LIVE CEO building it is covered by the canary .3.5.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario asserts the expected org-chart shape and delegation grants.

title: E2E: qn org init --host against a start-simpli fixture (host detect + per-app .beads + toolchain preflight)
description: Write FIRST (must fail until A1/A2 land). Against a throwaway start-simpli fixture/clone: assert host mode detected, project_root set, per-app .beads discovered, and toolchain preflight behaves (fails fast when CLIs missing). Never mutate the real repo.
design: Tier: E2E + unit. Extend cli/tests/test_org_init_host_mode.py (unit: initialize_org(host_mode=True)) and cli/tests/test_host_mode_integration.py (real bd via CliRunner). Build a FIXTURE monorepo: pnpm-workspace.yaml root + apps/<app>/.beads + packages/ + a meta .beads + .git, so the test exercises per-app .beads discovery. Assert: host detected, org_state.project_root set, .quinnai/ created, per-app .beads resolved, real repo untouched (hash-check). Toolchain preflight asserted via monkeypatched PATH (missing CLI -> fail fast).
acceptance_criteria: E2E green once host-mode monorepo hardening + toolchain preflight are implemented.

title: OKR cascade design for the Simpli org
description: Design the OKR tree: top-level objectives -> Core Infra KRs (auth/API/shared-package health, reliability) + per-App-Group KRs (ship/iterate a customer app). Encode that App Groups self-assign sub-OKRs AFTER sensemaking rather than being pre-filed (per sensemaking-first feedback).
acceptance_criteria: An OKR seed the org can start from, with clear core-infra vs app-group split and room for self-assigned sub-OKRs.
notes: DECISION: OKR cascade seeds top objectives + Core Infra KRs + per-App-Group objectives, but leaves App-Group sub-OKRs for self-assignment after sensemaking (consistent with hybrid topology).

title: Team topology blueprint: Core Infra team + App Groups
description: Define the org shape: CEO -> Core Infra team (owns auth-web, start-simpli-api/Django, shared @startsimpli/* packages) + N App Groups (each owns one customer-facing app: raise/market/vault/trade/etc., leverages foundries + shared packages). Specify roles, default headcount, manager/IC split, and delegation + budget caps per group.
acceptance_criteria: A documented topology a CEO can instantiate via hire/hire-team + delegate-authority.
notes: DECISION: HYBRID topology. Declare Core Infra team (auth-web, Django API, shared @startsimpli/* packages) explicitly in org.yml; App Groups are seeded (OKRs + conventions + a manager seat) and self-assemble their ICs. Use a 'core-infra' team template + an 'app-group' team template referenced by $ref.

title: Git workflow integration: branch-per-bead -> commit -> push -> PR (gh) across submodule remotes
description: Currently MISSING. Give workers a sanctioned flow to create a branch tied to a bead, commit, push to the correct submodule remote, and open a PR via gh. Trust-bounded so it can't push to arbitrary remotes.
design: GREENFIELD capability (nothing today). Workers can run git from cwd in host mode but there's no sanctioned branch/PR flow. Build: branch-per-bead naming, commit, push to the CORRECT submodule remote (apps/<app> have distinct remotes), open PR via gh. Trust-bound (can't push to arbitrary remotes) — extend the .quinnai/bin shim pattern (scaffolding.install_bd_shim). Consider a 'qn wrkr' subcommand or a shim binary. Test via .3.3 (local bare remote).
acceptance_criteria: A worker can take a bead, branch, commit a change in the right app/package, and open a PR on that submodule's remote.

title: Worker toolchain contract + preflight (node/pnpm/python+poetry/docker/gh/vercel/MCP)
description: Define and verify the toolchain a Simpli worker session needs. Add a preflight check at org start/worker spawn that confirms required CLIs are on PATH and fails fast with a clear message if missing. Document the contract.
design: Add a preflight at org start / worker spawn (org_start_controller.py spawn path ~320-397). Define a toolchain contract (node/pnpm, python+poetry, docker, gh, vercel, MCP browser-verify) — likely declared in org.yml (.4.2) and checked via shutil.which. Fail fast with a precise message naming the missing CLI. Mirror the existing skip-config-validation pattern so tests can bypass.
acceptance_criteria: Spawning a worker against start-simpli fails fast with a precise error if pnpm/node/poetry/gh/vercel are absent; passes when present.

title: Host-mode hardening for a pnpm-workspace + git-submodule monorepo
description: Make host mode work against start-simpli's shape: pnpm-workspace root, apps/* as git submodules (each own remote + .beads), packages/@startsimpli/* shared, start-simpli-api Django. Discover and route per-app .beads vs the meta-repo .beads; ensure worker cwd + relative paths resolve correctly inside the workspace; handle submodule presence/absence gracefully.
design: Touch points: cli/core/host_mode.py (is_host_mode/get_project_root/find_org_root), cli/core/onboarding.py:get_worker_session_working_directory (627-663) + get_worker_env_vars (730-785), cli/core/org_init/ (init.py, scaffolding.py). Host mode ALREADY sets cwd=project_root + project_root in org_state. ADD: pnpm-workspace + git-submodule awareness and PER-APP .beads routing — start-simpli has apps/<app>/.beads (own remotes) + a meta .beads. Decide which .beads a given worker's qn-bd shim targets based on the app subtree it's working in. Handle submodule present/absent gracefully.
acceptance_criteria: qn org init --host on a start-simpli checkout detects host mode, sets project_root, and worker sessions resolve per-app .beads correctly.

title: Testing (TDD-first): prove QuinnAI can drive start-simpli via canaries + E2E
description: Test-first validation of the whole capability. Each implementation task in the Architecture/Design epics is gated on a test written first that FAILS until the capability lands (per QuinnAI's test-driven-bug-fixing commandment). Tiers: E2E (real qn + real bd against a fixture/sandbox start-simpli checkout), scenario (FakeSpawner, in-process CliRunner) for org-topology assertions, and a paid live-LLM canary for the real end-to-end. All foundry/AWS interactions run in dry-run/mock — no real provisioning.
design: Extend tests/e2e/, tests/scenarios/specs/, tests/canary/specs/. Use a throwaway clone or fixture of start-simpli so tests never mutate the real repo. Canary gated/opt-in (paid). Mock the foundry orchestrator + AWS calls.
notes:
TEST STRATEGY (from infra audit): map each capability to its cheapest sufficient tier.
- Tier 2 SCENARIO (FakeSpawner, YAML ops/predicates, ~60s, FREE) = workhorse for topology + org.yml loader. Author specs in tests/scenarios/specs/NN_*.yml; register new ops in shared/testing/scenarios/ops.py and predicates in predicates.py. Existing useful predicates: worker_count, manager_subordinates, org_chart_depth, team_count, team_parent_is, channel_exists, okr_owner.
- E2E (qn_runner subprocess + REAL bd, ~3m, FREE) = host-mode init + git/PR CLI. Extend tests/e2e/ and cli/tests/test_host_mode_integration.py.
- Tier 3 CANARY (live LLM, gated QUINNAI_RUN_CANARY=1, BudgetGuard via QUINNAI_CANARY_BUDGET_USD/SECONDS, default sonnet-4-6) = the live capstone only. Author in tests/canary/specs/.
All foundry/AWS = mocked. New tests are WRITTEN FIRST (impl beads are blocked-by them).

title: Concern 2: the quinn-ai-start-simpli-org template — config, org.yml, layout & briefings agents build off of
description: Author the concrete, runnable org template for quinn-ai-start-simpli-org: the config + org.yml + directory layout + onboarding briefings that the org's agents build off of so they know WHAT to do and HOW things work. Encodes the Core Infra team (auth-web, start-simpli-api/Django, shared @startsimpli/* packages) + App Groups (each owns a customer-facing app, leverages foundries + shared packages). This is the SPECIFIC instantiation; it CONSUMES the generic declarative-config levers from epic .4. Respect sensemaking-first: the template seeds topology + OKR scaffolding + conventions, but the live org self-assigns its execution sub-OKRs after discovery.
design: Respect sensemaking-first: blueprint + template are platform artifacts; the live org self-assigns its Simpli execution sub-OKRs after discovery. Onboarding additions go in cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2 (already has a host-mode section). Example org lives under example_orgs/.

title: Architecture: QuinnAI host-mode operation against the start-simpli monorepo + foundry toolchain
description: Architectural capability so a QuinnAI org can reliably build/maintain start-simpli. Covers: host-mode hardening for a pnpm workspace with git submodules and per-app .beads; a worker toolchain contract (node/pnpm/python+poetry/docker/gh/vercel + MCP browser-verify); git -> branch-per-bead -> commit -> push -> PR automation across submodule remotes; a sanctioned, trust-bounded path for app-group workers to invoke foundry provisioning; the org-chart -> Simpli-architecture mapping and the secrets/credentials boundary.
design: Builds on cli/core/host_mode.py, cli/core/onboarding.py:get_worker_session_working_directory, org_state.project_root. start-simpli specifics: pnpm-workspace.yaml root, apps/* are git submodules each with own remote + .beads, packages/@startsimpli/* shared, start-simpli-api is Django. Reuse existing API-key stripping in claude_code adapter for the secrets boundary.

title: QuinnAI ⇄ start-simpli: AI org that builds Simpli core infra + ships customer apps via foundries
description:
Two distinct concerns, tracked together because Concern 2 consumes Concern 1.

CONCERN 1 — QuinnAI PLATFORM CODE (generic, benefits every org):
  (a) Runtime capability to run/operate an org against an external monorepo + foundries — host-mode hardening, worker toolchain, git->PR, foundry-aware tooling.  [epic .1]
  (b) Configuration levers: express a WHOLE org declaratively (org.yml) with enough knobs to do what we want — teams, roles, seats, manager links, delegation/budgets, OKR seed, onboarding profile, host-mode/project_root, toolchain, provider/model — instead of imperative hire/delegate scripting.  [epic .4]

CONCERN 2 — the quinn-ai-start-simpli-org TEMPLATE (specific instantiation):
  The actual config + org.yml + layout + briefings that the org's agents BUILD OFF OF, so members know what to do and how things work. Encodes: Core Infra team (auth-web, Django API, shared @startsimpli/* packages) + App Groups that leverage foundries to ship customer apps. CONSUMES the levers from Concern 1(b).  [epic .2]

CROSS-CUTTING: Testing (TDD-first) proves both concerns.  [epic .3]

start-simpli is the forcing function; Concern 1 must stay generic.
design: Today QuinnAI host mode (qn org init --host) points workers' cwd at an external repo (project_root in org_state, auto-detects .git/.beads). Gaps vs start-simpli: no pnpm-workspace/git-submodule + per-app .beads handling, no worker toolchain contract (pnpm/node/poetry/gh/vercel/MCP), no git→branch→PR automation, no foundry-aware worker tooling, no non-toy example org. start-simpli foundry = control plane (apps/foundry + start-simpli-api/backend/apps/foundry/orchestrator.py) that provisions isolated central-auth-federated tenant stacks from tenant-starter/ + frontend-starter/.
acceptance_criteria: qn org init --host against a start-simpli checkout boots an org whose CEO assembles the core-infra + app-group topology, a worker can land a PR in a Simpli package, and an app-group worker can exercise foundry provisioning in dry-run — all covered by passing E2E/canary tests.

title: [GUARDRAILS] Tests: failing unit + integration tests for tool guard
description: Write failing tests: qn-tool-guard exits 1 when Bash command matches ABSOLUTE rule, exits 0 for allowed commands, hook config written to correct path at spawn, shell.bash action evaluates correctly in rule engine. All must fail before implementation.
close_reason: 17 tests written, all failing. Covers: evaluate_tool_call, GuardResult, hook config generation, default_rules shell.bash action, engine evaluation on shell.bash.

title: [GUARDRAILS] Extend default_rules.yaml ABSOLUTE rules to include shell.bash action
description: Add shell.bash to the actions list of the 4 ABSOLUTE rules (no-rm-rf-storage, no-force-push-main, no-drop-database, no-secret-commit) so they fire when a worker attempts these via a direct Bash tool call, not just via qn-bd. This is the rule-side change; the hook-side change is in the hook injection bead.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 18036ac. 17 tests passing. Workers shipped it.

title: [GUARDRAILS] Hook injection: write PreToolUse hook config at worker spawn
description: At prepare_worker_onboarding() or spawn_worker_session(), write a .claude/settings.json into the worker's working directory containing a PreToolUse hook that calls qn-tool-guard. Hook receives tool_name + tool_input JSON via stdin. Worker's ORG_PATH + WORKER_ID env vars are already set so the guard can find the rule engine. Files: cli/core/session/tool_guard.py (hook generator), cli/core/onboarding.py or session spawn.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 18036ac. 17 tests passing. Workers shipped it.

title: [GUARDRAILS] qn-tool-guard CLI: evaluate tool calls against rule engine
description: New CLI entrypoint called by Claude Code's PreToolUse hook. Reads tool name + input JSON from stdin (Claude Code hook protocol), maps to a rule action (shell.bash, session.write, session.edit), calls the rule engine, exits 0 to allow or 1+message to block. Files: cli/commands/qn_tool_guard.py, registered as console_scripts qn-tool-guard.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 18036ac. 17 tests passing. Workers shipped it.

title: Board OS: User Requirements
description: Define what 'full operating system' means for the Board UI. Key areas: (1) interactivity — pop in/out of worker tmux sessions from the UI, send directives without leaving the board; (2) worker detail panel — per-worker context showing tools, slash commands, storage layout, active beads, recent messages, briefing summary; (3) visual design — what does 'full OS feel' look like in a Textual TUI; (4) session control — attach, detach, monitor multiple sessions simultaneously; (5) non-goals — what stays in CLI vs moves to UI.
notes:
User: Quinn. Vision: Board UI as the primary OS for managing AI orgs — not a passive monitor, but an interactive control plane.

Three pillars:
1. WORKER DETAIL PANEL — select any worker in TeamView → right-side panel shows: available CLI tools (from tools.yaml + worker tools), storage directory tree, active beads, recent channel messages, briefing excerpt, current task. Replaces hunting through CLI commands for worker context.

2. SESSION ATTACH/DETACH — from Board UI, press Enter/a on a selected worker → suspend Textual, tmux attach-session into that worker's session, work directly, prefix+d to detach → Textual resumes. 'Pop in and out' without leaving the board.

3. VISUAL/UX — split-pane layout (worker list left, detail right), OS-like navigation (arrow keys to move between workers, panel updates live), direct directive sending from board without modals.

Acceptance: can run an org entirely from the Board UI — monitor, drill into any worker, attach to their session, give directives, detach back — without touching separate terminal tabs or CLI commands.

Non-goals: not a full terminal emulator, not replacing tmux, not rebuilding the CLI. Board UI calls CLI via existing OrgConnection/OrgCommander patterns.
close_reason: Closed

title: Board UI Messages: detail pane empty due to RowKey-vs-str comparison
description:
## Problem
Selecting any message in the messages table leaves the right-hand detail pane empty. User-visible symptom: 'right side that's supposed to show the actual content of the back and forth shows nothing'.

This was the actual underlying bug in qc1a. The earlier qc1a fix addressed default-channel selection and stale Select.Changed events, plus added a 'positive control' test for the row-selection path — but that test mocked event.row_key as a string. In real Textual, event.row_key is a RowKey object.

## Root cause
board_ui/views/messages.py:416 (pre-fix):

    self._selected_message = next(
        (m for m in self._messages if m.id == row_key), None
    )

m.id is a str, row_key is textual.widgets.DataTable.RowKey. The == always returns False, so _selected_message stays None and the function returns at the 'Could not find message' guard. Header, body, reply controls — all stay in their initial empty state.

team.py at line 256 already uses .value: 'worker_id = event.cell_key.row_key.value'. Messages view didn't.

## Fix
Extract row_key.value before comparison (with hasattr fallback for backward compat). Verified by code inspection that the messages flow is the only board_ui callsite missing this.

## Repro
1. qn board ui (against any org with messages)
2. Tab to messages panel, click a message row
3. Right pane stays blank; debug log shows 'No message found for row_key'

## Discovered while
User pushed back: 'still cant see anything in messages — the right side that's supposed to show the actual content of the back and forth shows fucking nothing'.
notes:
REOPENED — fix was a no-op. RowKey.__eq__ already returns True for string comparison (verified: 'msg-board-channel-0' == RowKey('msg-board-channel-0') is True). My patch (row_key.value extraction) is harmless but didn't fix the user's actual problem.

A new Pilot test that simulates focus+Enter on the messages table renders the message body correctly (tests/board_ui/test_e2e_real_clicks.py). So under that interaction model, detail-rendering works.

The user's actual symptom remains unclear. Need from user:
- Are they tabbing to the messages-table specifically, or hitting Enter while focus is on the channel selector?
- Do they see the row highlight change as they arrow up/down?
- Was the screenshot they showed (with content) from 'qn board messages' (CLI text dump) or 'qn board ui' (Textual TUI)?

Repeatable check: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/board_ui/test_e2e_real_clicks.py
close_reason:
ACTUAL FIX (previous close was a no-op).

Root cause: Textual DataTable fires DIFFERENT events on click vs Enter:
- Mouse click → RowHighlighted only
- Enter on focused row → RowSelected

Verified empirically: see the inline 4-event diagnostic in this session.

The messages view only handled RowSelected, so mouse clicks left detail pane on its placeholder ('Click on a message in the list...'). The user's symptom: right pane stays blank when clicking. Pressing Enter after selecting WAS already working.

Fix in board_ui/views/messages.py: extracted _select_message_by_row_key helper and added on_data_table_row_highlighted handler that calls it. RowHighlighted also fires on arrow-key navigation, giving an inbox-style preview UX (matches Mail.app, Outlook, etc.).

Repeatable verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/board_ui/test_e2e_real_clicks.py::TestMessagesPanel
  - test_row_selection_via_keyboard_populates_detail (Enter path)
  - test_row_selection_via_mouse_click_populates_detail (click path)
Both pass with fix; the mouse-click test FAILS without it (proven by reverting and re-running).

Earlier 'fix' (row_key.value extraction) was harmless but not the root cause — RowKey.__eq__ already accepts string compare.

title: Board UI Team panel: NoActiveWorker crash when clicking action cells
description:
## Problem
Clicking the [Actions ▸] cell on a non-CEO worker in the Team panel crashes the board UI:

    NoActiveWorker: push_screen must be run from a worker when wait_for_dismiss is True

at board_ui/views/team.py:263 → _show_worker_actions_menu → push_screen_wait(WorkerActionsModal(...)).

Same crash class on the [+ Hire Worker] button (board_ui/views/team.py:243 → _hire_worker → push_screen_wait(HireWorkerModal())).

## Root cause
Textual 0.x+ requires push_screen_wait to run inside a Worker context (so the dismiss callback has somewhere to suspend). _show_worker_actions_menu and _hire_worker are async helpers called from message handlers (on_data_table_cell_selected, on_button_pressed) — message handlers are NOT workers by default.

## Fix
Decorate _show_worker_actions_menu and _hire_worker with @work (textual.work). Change call sites in handlers to fire-and-forget (drop the await). Downstream methods that also use push_screen_wait (_fire_worker, _promote_worker, _demote_worker) are reached only via _show_worker_actions_menu, so they inherit its worker context.

## Repro
1. qn board ui (in any org)
2. Tab to team panel
3. Click [Actions ▸] on any non-CEO worker
4. Crash with NoActiveWorker traceback

## Discovered while
Operating ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise board UI right after the qc1a/176s fixes landed.
close_reason:
Fixed in board_ui/views/team.py:
- Imported textual.work
- Decorated _show_worker_actions_menu and _hire_worker with @work so push_screen_wait inside them has a worker context.
- Changed call sites in on_data_table_cell_selected and on_button_pressed to fire-and-forget (no await on @work-decorated methods).

Downstream methods (_fire_worker, _promote_worker, _demote_worker) reach push_screen_wait only via _show_worker_actions_menu, so they inherit its worker context — no separate fix needed.

Now back to the messages-panel question that surfaced this: the panel showing only the Sasha DM is by design (qc1a default-channel pick is 'channel with most unread'). #general has 8 messages but they may all be marked read in whatever read-state table the messages panel queries. Will investigate separately if user reports the # of channels visible is wrong.

title: Board UI data sync is broken across panels (OKRs, messages, health) — needs systemic audit
description:
## Problem
Multiple Board UI panels are out of sync with the underlying data, suggesting a class of bugs (not isolated incidents). Captured during ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise bring-up:

1. **OKR panel**: shows 'No OKRs found' despite bd having an open OKR epic (see sibling bug for OKR specifics)
2. **Messages panel**: list doesn't render usable entries; right-pane detail view stays blank on selection
3. **Health panel**: surfaces 'no_okrs' warnings for every worker even when the parent OKR is assigned to one of them — likely lookup-by-name vs lookup-by-id mismatch (assignee=Cleo vs assignee=wrkr-e47c8976)

## Hypothesis
The board reads from a mix of (a) qn's SQLite mirror (which qn org okr never populates on dolt orgs — see quinn-ai-k9ff), (b) bd directly (broken via run_bd --db= override), and (c) some local cache. When any of those is stale/empty/wrong, the UI shows zeros instead of querying alternative sources or surfacing an error.

## Suggested approach
Don't fix one panel at a time. Audit board data flow end-to-end:
- For each panel, list: source-of-truth → query path → renderer
- Identify where source-of-truth diverges from what panel queries
- Fix the read path to point at bd's actual data (with dolt support), or fix qn's mirror-population so the mirror IS authoritative

## Impact
Quote from operator: 'board ui sucks dick at syncing with the data ... functionally useless'. Operators can't trust the dashboard, which means they can't supervise orgs without dropping into CLI/tmux directly.
notes: Two of three leaves closed (176s OKR-panel, qc1a messages-panel). uk9v (health-panel name-vs-id mismatch) remains in progress with another agent. Once uk9v lands, nu51 can be closed.
close_reason:
Umbrella resolved by closures of children:
- quinn-ai-176s: OKR panel now reads from bd as fallback when SQLite mirror is empty (board_ui/services/readers/okrs.py)
- quinn-ai-qc1a: Messages panel default-channel + stale-event handling fixed (board_ui/views/messages.py)
- quinn-ai-uk9v: assignee resolved to worker_id at OKR creation (cli/commands/org/okr/_helpers.py)

Architectural finding (worth keeping in mind for future board work): board_ui readers all query the SQLite mirror at <org>/live/quinn.db. That's correct for messages/channels (SQLite is canonical) but wrong for OKRs (bd is canonical, mirror is denormalized and empty for dolt orgs). The 176s fix layers a bd fallback into OKRReader; if other panels start showing similar staleness, same pattern applies.

Tests: tests/board_ui/test_view_panel_data_sync.py (3 new tests, all pass). 45/45 panel tests pass. 320/321 broader board_ui suite (1 pre-existing skip).

title: Board UI: OKR panel shows 'No OKRs found' even when org has OKRs
description:
## Problem
The QuinnAI Board UI OKR panel renders 'No OKRs found. Create OKRs to track organizational objectives.' even when the org's beads has open epics labeled `okr`.

Example: ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise has `debugg-fundraise-6is` (P0 epic, --label okr, OPEN, assignee Cleo). `bd show debugg-fundraise-6is` from inside the org returns it correctly. The board UI lists zero.

## Likely root cause
The board UI's OKR query mirrors the broken path in qn org okr (see quinn-ai-k9ff): it uses `run_bd` with --db=beads.db override that doesn't work against dolt-mode beads. Fix that wrapper and the board likely starts seeing OKRs.

May also be that the board queries OKRs via the SQLite mirror that `qn org okr set` would have populated — but since qn org okr set is broken on dolt orgs, the mirror is empty even when bd-side epics exist.

## Repro
1. From a dolt-mode org: `bd create --type epic --label okr --title T --description ...`
2. Open board UI → OKR panel says 'No OKRs found'
3. `bd list --label okr` from inside org → shows the epic

## Impact
Board UI is the primary human surface; if it doesn't reflect OKRs, operators can't tell at-a-glance whether the org has objectives. Currently functionally useless for OKR oversight.
notes: k9ff fix likely resolves this in CLI ('qn org okr list' now surfaces dolt-org OKRs). Board UI not directly verified yet — needs someone to launch the board UI and confirm the OKR panel populates. If it does, close. If not, the board UI may have its own query path that needs the same dolt-aware fix.
close_reason: Fixed by adding bd-fallback to board_ui/services/readers/okrs.py:OKRReader.get_okrs(). When the SQLite okrs mirror is empty (common for dolt-mode orgs whose qn org okr set was broken pre-k9ff), the reader now also queries bd for OKR-labeled epics and synthesizes OKRInfo entries. Regression test: tests/board_ui/test_view_panel_data_sync.py::test_okr_panel_shows_bd_okrs_when_mirror_is_empty. Dep on nu51 was reversed (umbrella) — bypassed with --force.

title: qn org start Phase 5 silently fails to deliver kickoff prompt to CEO session
description:
## Problem
`qn org start` reports:

    Phase 5: Sending initial prompt to CEO...
    Creating initial task instructions...
    ✓ Initial task instructions delivered; CEO session is processing

But the prompt never lands in the CEO's claude TUI. Cleo's tmux pane shows an empty `❯` prompt and the team-view says `Status: Working... [auto]` while she's actually idle.

## Repro
1. qn --org-path <new-org> org init --ceo-name X --skip-okrs
2. qn --org-path <new-org> org start --wait
3. tmux capture-pane -t qn-wrkr-<ceo-id> -p → empty input

Expected: kickoff prompt visible/submitted in CEO's claude session. Actual: nothing delivered, status reports false-positive 'delivered'.

## Workaround
Manually inject via `tmux send-keys -t qn-wrkr-<id> '<prompt>' Enter Enter` (note: needs TWO Enters — first lands the text in the multiline buffer, second submits).

## Likely root cause
Whatever stdin/tmux send-keys mechanism Phase 5 uses either (a) sends to wrong target, (b) doesn't submit (no trailing Enter), or (c) silently swallows errors. The 'Working... [auto]' status seems to be set by Phase 5 regardless of actual delivery.

## Impact
Every new org launch requires manual intervention — defeats the point of `qn org start --wait`. Discovered launching ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise.
close_reason:
Two-part fix in cli/core/org_start_controller.py:

1. **Honest verification** (_pane_shows_prompt_landed helper): replaced 'any pane diff = success' with content-aware check. Now requires either the cat command text to be visible in the pane OR a claude processing indicator (⏺/✻/⎿/Crunching/Reading/Thinking). Old check false-positived on TUI redraws (cursor blink, status bar).

2. **Reliable submit**: added a second Enter after a 0.5s gap. Claude-code TUI empirically requires this — first Enter on long pasted text is sometimes interpreted as newline-in-input rather than submit. Verified by manual repro against Cleo's live session: first Enter left text in input box, second Enter submitted.

title: qn org okr commands fail on dolt-mode beads (--db=beads.db override)
description:
## Problem
`qn org okr set` (and likely other okr subcommands routed through run_bd) fail on orgs whose .beads/ was scaffolded in dolt-embedded mode — the default for orgs created by `qn org init`. Error:

    Error: Failed to create OKR: database not initialized: issue_prefix config is missing

## Root cause
`cli/core/bd_wrapper.py:run_bd` (~line 664) builds:

    cmd = [bd_path, '--sandbox', f'--db={beads_db}'] + args

with `beads_db = beads_dir / 'beads.db'`. In dolt mode the actual db lives in `<org>/.beads/embeddeddolt/` (metadata.json: backend=dolt, dolt_mode=embedded). The sqlite-style beads.db file exists but lacks issue_prefix config, so bd refuses writes via that --db override.

Direct `bd` from inside the org dir works — bd auto-discovers the dolt backend from .beads/metadata.json. The breakage is specific to run_bd's --db= override.

## Repro
1. qn --org-path /tmp/foo org init --ceo-name X --skip-okrs
2. qn --org-path /tmp/foo org okr set --title T --description ... --kr m:1:u
3. issue_prefix error.

## Suggested fix
run_bd should read .beads/metadata.json: when backend == 'dolt', drop the --db= override and rely on BEADS_DIR + cwd for bd's auto-discovery. Or pass dolt connection params explicitly.

## Workaround
bd create --type epic --label okr from inside the org dir. Loses validation that 'qn org okr set' provides (KR format etc.).

## Discovered while
Setting up ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise. OKR debugg-fundraise-6is was created via the workaround.
close_reason:
Fixed in cli/core/bd_wrapper.py.

Two changes:
1. is_dolt_backend(beads_dir) helper: reads .beads/metadata.json's 'backend' field, returns True for dolt-mode orgs.
2. run_bd(): when dolt mode detected, skips --db= override AND BEADS_DB env var (both pointed at empty .beads/beads.db). Also added prefer_system param to get_bundled_bd_path() — bundled bd 0.43.x doesn't fully support dolt --sandbox; system bd 1.x+ does.

Tests: 3 new tests in TestDoltModeBackend (cli/tests/test_bd_wrapper.py) — all 29 bd_wrapper tests pass. Pre-existing 3 failures in test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py are unrelated (filed as quinn-ai-oj39).

Integration verified: 'qn org okr set' against ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise (a real dolt-mode org) creates OKRs successfully. 'qn org okr list' surfaces them. Confirmed against real Cleo org while she was running.

title: [BUG] CEO interprets kickstart prompt as 'documentation about another worker' instead of self-direction
description:
Live observation, StartSimpli canary v2 2026-04-29 09:25.

After fixing quinn-ai-ltvl (cat path), the CEO successfully read INITIAL_TASK.md but FAILED to recognize the prompt was addressed to themselves. They responded:

  'This is the onboarding script for a StartSimpli-CEO worker spawned by qn org start. It's not addressed to me as your assistant — it's the initial autonomous-mode prompt for that worker process.'

The actual prompt starts with 'You are StartSimpli-CEO, the CEO of this organization. You've just been onboarded.' — first-person, no ambiguity. But the CEO claude session interpreted the cat'd file as DOCUMENTATION ABOUT another worker, not as direction for itself.

This is meta-cognitive dissociation: claude's training to recognize 'you are X' as a system-prompt pattern made it conclude the file content was a *configuration document* for the CEO role rather than the runtime prompt FOR the CEO it's currently embodied as.

Net effect: CEO sits idle just like the original ltvl bug — same outcome (no hires, no msgr send), different cause.

Hypotheses for a fix:
  1. Send prompt content directly via tmux send-keys (paste into the input box) instead of via 'cat <file>' which makes it look like content being read for review.
  2. Add an explicit framing prefix: 'PROMPT FOR YOU TO EXECUTE NOW — do not summarize, do not describe, just begin.'
  3. Change the file name from INITIAL_TASK.md to FIRST_ACTION_INSTRUCTIONS.md or similar, and have the cat output prefixed with 'BEGIN AUTONOMOUS EXECUTION:' so it's read as a directive.
  4. Use 'echo' to write the prompt directly to claude's stdin instead of cat-ing a file.

Recommend (1) — directly paste the prompt into claude's input via tmux send-keys with the prompt text inline. That way claude sees it as a user message in the chat, not as a file being read.

Filed in addition to ltvl (cat path) because this is a separate failure mode that emerges only after ltvl is fixed.
close_reason: Shipped in c8e7d80. Prepended '=== EXECUTE THIS NOW ===' framing block to _INITIAL_PROMPT_TEMPLATE explicitly disambiguating that the reader IS the worker (not analyzing it), forbidding summarization, and countering the exact 'script for another worker' phrasing the canary CEO produced. Regression test test_kickstart_initial_task_has_unambiguous_framing pins the framing in place. Verification still pending: needs a fresh StartSimpli canary to confirm the CEO actually starts hiring + messaging instead of dissociating.

title: [BUG] host-mode kickstart 'cat INITIAL_TASK.md' fails — cwd is project_root but file is in storage dir
description:
Host-mode-init regression. resolve_session_cwd returns project_root for host-mode workers (so they can edit project files directly), but _send_initial_prompt_to_ceo writes INITIAL_TASK.md to <worker_dir>/INITIAL_TASK.md and then sends 'cat INITIAL_TASK.md' via tmux send-keys.

In greenfield mode, cwd == worker_dir, so the relative cat works. In host-mode, cwd == project_root, so the cat fails ('INITIAL_TASK.md does not exist'). The CEO never sees their kickstart prompt → never reads BRIEFING.md → never hires → org silent for the entire session.

Verified on a fresh canary 2026-04-29 09:02 against /Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli: 30 min wall, 0 hires, 0 messages beyond the system welcome, CEO pane shows literally 'INITIAL_TASK.md does not exist at /Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli/INITIAL_TASK.md'.

Same issue affects the prompt template's followup steps:
  - 'Read your BRIEFING.md file: cat BRIEFING.md' (also fails — BRIEFING.md is in storage)
  - All other relative file refs in the kickstart

Fix: change kickstart cat invocation to use $WORKER_STORAGE (already in env_vars):
  cmd = 'cat "$WORKER_STORAGE/INITIAL_TASK.md"'
Same pattern in the prompt template:
  cat "$WORKER_STORAGE/BRIEFING.md"

Or alternative: write INITIAL_TASK.md to project_root in host-mode (gross — pollutes user's repo).
close_reason: Shipped in c628a30: kickstart now uses absolute path 'cat {instructions_file}' so it works in both greenfield (cwd=worker_dir) and host-mode (cwd=project_root). Prompt template's followup 'cat BRIEFING.md' updated to use $WORKER_STORAGE/BRIEFING.md. Verified: fresh CEO spawn now reads the prompt successfully (uncovered a follow-on issue with the CEO meta-cognating themselves out of the role — filed separately as the CEO-dissociation bead).

design:
# BOARD-TPL Phase 3 — Architecture & Interface Design

Builds on quinn-ai-iabn (system design) and quinn-ai-cutg (strategy). Pins module boundaries, dependency injection, integration with existing primitives.

## 1. Module map

```
cli/core/templates/
├── __init__.py        # public API re-exports (Template, TemplateRegistry, TemplateOrchestrator, validate_parent_reference, HireTeamResult)
├── types.py           # dataclasses (Template, TemplateMember, ChannelSpec, InitialOKR, TemplateRegistry, HireTeamResult)
├── loader.py          # load_templates(org_path: Path) -> TemplateRegistry
├── composition.py     # validate_parent_reference(template, parent_team_name, db) -> str | None
└── orchestrator.py    # TemplateOrchestrator class
```

`cli/commands/org/`:
- `hire_team.py` — Click command + `hire_team_cmd` entry-point.
- `templates.py` — Click subgroup with `list`, `show`, `validate`.

## 2. Public API surface

Re-exported from `cli.core.templates`:
- Dataclasses: `Template`, `TemplateMember`, `ChannelSpec`, `InitialOKR`, `TemplateRegistry`, `HireTeamResult`
- Functions: `load_templates`, `validate_parent_reference`
- Class: `TemplateOrchestrator`

Internal: nothing. The 5-file module is small enough that the public surface = the module surface.

## 3. Dependency injection

`TemplateOrchestrator.__init__(ctx, db, registry)`:
- `ctx`: Click context (carries logger, env, optional rules engine when BOARD-RULES lands).
- `db`: Database instance (existing).
- `registry`: TemplateRegistry (loaded once per `qn org` invocation).

The orchestrator is instantiated inside `hire_team_cmd`:
```python
@click.command("hire-team")
@click.option("--template", required=True)
# ... options ...
@pass_context
def hire_team_cmd(ctx, template, name, manager, ...):
    registry = load_templates(ctx.obj.org_path)
    orch = TemplateOrchestrator(ctx, ctx.obj.db, registry)
    result = orch.hire_team(template, name, manager, ...)
    _print_result(result)
```

Tests inject fake `ctx`/`db`/`registry` directly into `TemplateOrchestrator.__init__`, no decorator-context machinery.

## 4. Reuse map (existing primitives the orchestrator wraps)

| Step in iabn §D                | Existing API the orchestrator calls                                                       |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Create team record              | `cli.core.queries.team:create_team(db, name, parent_team_id, lead_id, auto_create_channel=False)` |
| Create channel                  | `cli.core.queries.channel:create_channel(db, name, channel_type="team", team_id)`         |
| Hire worker                     | `cli.core.worker.hiring:hire_worker(db, ctx, name, role, manager_id, cost)` (NEW — extracted in Phase 4 from hire_cmd body) |
| Fire worker (rollback)          | `cli.core.worker.firing:fire_worker(db, ctx, worker_id, reason, terminate_immediately)` (NEW — extracted from fire_cmd) |
| Add team member                 | `cli.core.queries.team:add_team_member(db, team_id, worker_id, role)`                     |
| Update team lead                | Direct SQL in orchestrator: `UPDATE teams SET lead_id = ? WHERE id = ?`                   |
| Subscribe channel members       | `cli.core.queries.channel:subscribe_worker_to_channel(db, worker_id, channel_id)` (verify existence; create if not present) |
| File initial OKR                | `cli.core.queries.okr:create_okr(db, ctx, ...)` (NEW — extracted from okr.manage body)    |

## 5. Schema migration shape

New file: `cli/core/db/migrations/<n>_add_team_template_fields.py`. Idempotent.

```python
def upgrade(conn):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("ALTER TABLE teams ADD COLUMN template_type TEXT DEFAULT NULL")
    cur.execute("ALTER TABLE teams ADD COLUMN ttl_hours INTEGER DEFAULT NULL")
    cur.execute("ALTER TABLE teams ADD COLUMN ttl_started_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NULL")
    cur.execute("ALTER TABLE teams ADD COLUMN status TEXT DEFAULT 'active'")  # if not already present
    conn.commit()
```

Note: `status` column may already exist for the broader teams lifecycle. Migration checks first via `PRAGMA table_info(teams)`.

## 9. Exception hierarchy additions (`shared/exceptions.py`)

```python
class TemplateError(Exception):
    """Base for template-system errors."""

class TemplateNotFound(TemplateError):
    """Named template not in registry."""

class TemplateMissingParent(TemplateError):
    """Template requires a parent but no --under was passed."""

class TemplateWrongParentType(TemplateError):
    """--under references a team whose template_type doesn't match required."""

class TemplateParentTerminated(TemplateError):
    """--under references a team that's no longer active."""

class HireTeamRollbackFailed(TemplateError):
    """Rollback itself failed; org is in partial state — operator intervention needed."""
    def __init__(self, original: Exception, rollback_errors: list[Exception]):
        self.original = original
        self.rollback_errors = rollback_errors

class ChannelNameCollision(TemplateError):
    """Auto-derived channel name already exists."""
```

## 10. Backward compatibility

- Legacy teams (created pre-template-fields migration) have NULL `template_type`. They cannot be referenced as `--under` parents — `validate_parent_reference` rejects them with `TemplateWrongParentType` and a message like "Team 'mobile-app' predates the templates feature; retag it via `qn org templates retag` (out of scope for v0)".

- The default-templates YAML file ships in the package; orgs created before this lands get the catalog automatically on next `qn org templates list` invocation.

## 11. Test ergonomics

The orchestrator is the hardest thing to test because it touches DB, channel, worker hire, OKR set, and rollback. Phase-2 integration tests (7xu5) use:

- Real `create_team` / `create_channel` / `add_team_member` (these are pure DB ops, no LLM).

This gives end-to-end coverage of the orchestrator's sequencing + rollback logic without spinning up real worker sessions.

design:
# BOARD-TPL Phase 3 — Technical Strategy

Builds on quinn-ai-iabn (system design). Resolves implementation strategy for the orchestrator, rollback path, default-template shipping, and TTL enforcement.

## 1. Programmatic hire/fire helpers (extraction strategy)

The orchestrator (TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team) cannot call `hire_cmd` and `fire_cmd` directly — those are click-bound entry points expecting a Click context. Calling them programmatically requires either constructing a fake click context (fragile) or extracting the business logic into a callable.

**Decision: extract.** Phase 4 lifts the business logic out of:
- `cli/commands/org/hire.py:hire_cmd` → `cli/core/worker/hiring.py:hire_worker(db, ctx, name, role, manager_id, cost) -> Worker`
- `cli/commands/org/fire.py:fire_cmd` → `cli/core/worker/firing.py:fire_worker(db, ctx, worker_id, reason, terminate_immediately) -> None`

The Click commands become thin wrappers that:
1. Parse click params.
2. Build a minimal context dict.
3. Call the programmatic helper.
4. Print the human-readable result.

The orchestrator (and tests) call the programmatic helpers. The Click layer is just I/O.

## 2. Rollback strategy

Synchronous, in-process, stack-based. Pseudo-code:

```python
def hire_team(...) -> HireTeamResult:
    rollback_stack: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
    try:
        # 1-4 (validation, no DB writes) — failures here just raise, no rollback needed
        team = create_team(db, ..., auto_create_channel=False)
        rollback_stack.append(lambda: db.execute("DELETE FROM teams WHERE id=?", (team.id,)))

        if template.channel:
            channel = create_channel(db, ...)
            rollback_stack.append(lambda: db.execute("DELETE FROM channels WHERE id=?", (channel.id,)))

        for member_spec in expanded_members:
            worker = hire_worker(db, ctx, ...)
            rollback_stack.append(lambda w=worker: fire_worker(db, ctx, w.id, "hire-team rollback", terminate_immediately=True))
            add_team_member(db, team.id, worker.id, member_spec.role)

        for okr_spec in template.initial_okrs:
            okr = okr_set(db, ...)  # programmatic helper, similar extraction needed for okr.manage
            rollback_stack.append(lambda o=okr: okr_close(db, o.id, status="cancelled", reason="hire-team rollback"))

        # commit succeeds — no rollback
        db.connection.commit()
        return HireTeamResult(rolled_back=False, ...)
    except Exception as e:
        # iterate rollback_stack in reverse; collect any rollback exceptions
        rollback_errors: list[Exception] = []
        for fn in reversed(rollback_stack):
            try:
                fn()
            except Exception as re:
                rollback_errors.append(re)
        db.connection.commit()
        if rollback_errors:
            raise HireTeamRollbackFailed(original=e, rollback_errors=rollback_errors) from e
        return HireTeamResult(rolled_back=True, failure_reason=str(e), ...)
```

**Why stack-based + lambda closures:** each rollback step knows exactly which entity to undo. No need for a "transaction journal" abstraction. ~50 LOC.

**Rollback-of-rollback:** if a rollback step itself throws, we collect the exception and continue with the rest. Final raise of `HireTeamRollbackFailed` requires operator intervention. Logged loudly to stderr.

## 3. Default-template shipping

`cli/config/default_team_templates.yaml` ships with the package (5 templates).

`load_templates(org_path)`:
- If `org_path/config/templates.yaml` exists: parse it. The default catalog is NOT merged — operator's file is canonical.
- If absent: parse the default catalog, return as-is. One-time stderr warning: "No org/config/templates.yaml found. Using default catalog. Run `qn org templates init --copy-defaults` to customize."

`qn org templates init --copy-defaults`: copies the default file to `org/config/templates.yaml` so operator can edit. No-op if the file already exists.

**Why no merge:** merging defaults with operator-defined templates creates ambiguity ("did I delete that template or did I just override it"). Explicit copy keeps the source-of-truth single.

## 4. Sequential vs parallel hires

**Decision: sequential.** Session-spawn races (per-worker session adapter setup, msgr subscription updates, org-chart writes) are real and concurrent hires would require fine-grained locking. Sequential is slow but correct. Phase 4 measures the actual cost — if hire_team takes >60s for a 5-worker product_team, revisit.

## 5. TTL enforcement (incident_response_squad)

**Decision: passive.** No background daemon. Two surfaces:
- `qn org status` shows team's `ttl_remaining` if non-null.
- `qn org templates expire-ttl` (operator command, optionally cron-driven) finds teams with `ttl_started_at + ttl_hours < NOW()`, fires all members, and closes the team.

**Active enforcement** (auto-fire on TTL expiry without operator action) is rejected for v0 because (a) the audit story is messier ("workers were fired by a clock"), (b) the operator might want to extend the TTL last-minute, (c) cron is the right tool for "do X every N minutes".

## 6. Implementation order (Phase 4)

Sequential:
1. `cli/core/templates/types.py` — dataclasses.
2. Schema migration: add `template_type`, `ttl_hours`, `ttl_started_at` to `teams` table.
3. `cli/core/templates/loader.py` — `load_templates(org_path)`.
4. `cli/config/default_team_templates.yaml` — 5 default templates.
5. Extract `hire_worker(...)` and `fire_worker(...)` programmatic helpers.
6. Extract `okr_set(...)` and `okr_close(...)` programmatic helpers.
7. `cli/core/templates/composition.py` — `validate_parent_reference`. Make 61hp green.
8. `cli/core/templates/orchestrator.py` — `TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team` (without OKR or rollback). Make 7xu5's first half green.
9. Add rollback. Make 7xu5 fully green.
10. `cli/commands/org/hire_team.py` + `cli/commands/org/templates.py` — Click wiring.
11. Role briefings (`cli/config/templates/role_briefings/<role>.md.jinja2` × 11).
12. Briefing-template integration (Team Membership section).
13. Live-LLM canary 12 (l2wl) green.

## 7. Cross-epic coordination

Per the cross-epic dep `quinn-ai-1ttp ← quinn-ai-l9uc`: the orchestrator must call the rules-aware `hire_worker` (i.e. the programmatic helper that respects rules), not bypass it. Concretely: when BOARD-RULES Phase 4 lands `requires_rule_check` on hire/fire, the same enforcement is automatically inherited by the orchestrator since it calls the same helpers.

If BOARD-RULES Phase 4 hasn't landed when BOARD-TPL Phase 4 starts, the orchestrator works fine (rules just don't fire). The cross-epic dep ensures BOARD-TPL doesn't ship hire-team into production until rules are wired — but development can proceed in parallel.

## 8. Risks + mitigations

| Risk                                                              | Mitigation                                                                                            |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Programmatic-helper extraction is invasive, may break canaries 01-11 | Phase 5 explicitly validates canaries against pre/post; commit the extraction in its own PR for easy revert |
| 5-worker hire_team takes >60s, operator thinks it hung            | Print progress lines per worker hire (`Hiring engineer-mobile-app-1...`)                              |
| Rollback writes get committed mid-iteration if helpers commit eagerly | Wrap helpers in a savepoint pattern (`SAVEPOINT hire_team_<uuid>`); rollback releases the savepoint |
| Default-template YAML format drifts from schema validator         | Add a Phase-2 test that loads the bundled defaults file and asserts schema-valid                      |
| TTL enforcement forgotten by operator → stale incident squads     | `qn org status` shows expired teams in red; `qn doctor` flags them                                    |

## 9. Open Phase-4 questions

- Should `hire_team` take a `--manager` argument that's the team-MANAGER, vs. the new team's manager-of-manager (the worker the team manager reports to)? iabn §D step 10 says `manager_id` param is the org-chart parent. **Phase 4 should NOT change this — keep `manager_id` as "parent in org chart" and call the in-template manager "team lead" to disambiguate.**
- Should `--worker-names` be a JSON or comma-separated list? **JSON for v0** (`'{"engineer": ["bob","alice"], "qa": ["charlie"]}'`) — simpler parsing, less ambiguity than comma-separated.

design:
# BOARD-RULES Phase 3 — Architecture & Interface Design

Builds on quinn-ai-t2zb (system design) and quinn-ai-p286 (strategy). This bead pins module boundaries, dependency injection, and the public-vs-internal API surface.

## 1. Module map

```
cli/core/rules/
├── __init__.py        # public API re-exports (Severity, Rule, RuleEngine, requires_rule_check, AuditLogger)
├── types.py           # dataclasses + enums (NO logic)
├── loader.py          # load_rules(org_path: Path) -> RuleSet
├── audit.py           # AuditLogger (write-only; reads handled outside)
├── engine.py          # RuleEngine + evaluate_or_raise helper
├── decorators.py      # requires_rule_check Click decorator
└── cli.py             # qn org rules {add, list, disable, test, validate}
```

Internal modules (loader, audit) are NOT re-exported from `__init__.py`. Command modules import only what they need from the public surface. Tests can reach internals directly via full path.

## 2. Public API surface

Re-exported from `cli.core.rules`:
- Enums: `Severity`, `DecisionKind`
- Dataclasses: `Rule`, `RuleSet`, `Pattern`, `Scope`, `Decision`
- Engine: `RuleEngine`, `evaluate_or_raise`
- Decorator: `requires_rule_check`
- Logger: `AuditLogger`

Everything else (helpers, internal validators, side-caches) is private.

## 3. Dependency injection

`ctx.obj` (Click context object) carries:
- `db: Database` — already there.
- `rules: RuleEngine` — new. Initialized in `cli/main.py`'s org-context loader after `db` is built.
- `rules_audit: AuditLogger` — new. Initialized alongside `rules`.

The init code:
```python
# cli/main.py (sketch)
ruleset = load_rules(ctx.obj.org_path)
ctx.obj.rules_audit = AuditLogger(ctx.obj.org_path / "live" / RULES_AUDIT_FILENAME)
ctx.obj.rules = RuleEngine(ruleset, ctx.obj.db, ctx.obj.rules_audit)
```

If `QUINNAI_RULES_DISABLED=1`, `RuleEngine` is replaced with `DisabledRuleEngine` (same interface, always returns ALLOW with kill-switch flag). This is a strategy-pattern swap, not a conditional inside `evaluate()` — keeps the hot path branch-free.

## 4. Pattern: mirror requires_permission

Existing pattern at `cli/core/permissions/access_control.py:525`:
```python
def requires_permission(channel_param, permission_level):
    def decorator(f):
        @functools.wraps(f)
        @click.pass_context
        def wrapper(ctx, *args, **kwargs):
            # ... permission check ...
            return f(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper
    return decorator
```

`requires_rule_check` follows the same shape:
```python
def requires_rule_check(action: str):
    def decorator(f):
        @functools.wraps(f)
        @click.pass_context
        def wrapper(ctx, *args, **kwargs):
            context = _build_action_context(ctx, action, args, kwargs)
            justify = kwargs.pop("justify", None)
            override = kwargs.pop("override", None)
            evaluate_or_raise(ctx, action, context, justify_bead_id=justify, override_bead_id=override)
            return f(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper
    return decorator
```

Two click options must be added to every rule-aware command: `--justify <bead-id>` and `--override <bead-id>`. The decorator pops them from kwargs before calling the wrapped function so the command body doesn't need to know about them.

## 5. Decorator stacking order

For commands that already have `@requires_permission`:
```python
@click.command()
@click.argument("worker")
@click.option("--justify")        # new
@click.option("--override")       # new
@requires_permission(...)          # outer (auth gate)
@requires_rule_check("qn-org.fire") # inner (rule gate)
@pass_context
def fire_cmd(ctx, worker, justify, override): ...
```

Reasoning: rule check assumes the worker is authenticated. Permission check fires first (outer); rule check fires second (inner). If permission denies, no rule eval happens — saves audit-log noise on unauthorized attempts.

## 6. Schema for action_name strings

Format: `<binary>.<command>` for top-level, `<binary>-<group>.<sub>` for nested. Strict format enforced by a regex at load time on `rules.yaml` `actions[]` values. Consistent with what each Click decorator passes to the rules engine. Examples in t2zb §F.

## 7. AuditLogger interface

```python
class AuditLogger:
    def __init__(self, path: Path): ...

    def record(self, *,
        worker_id: str | None,
        action: str,
        rule_id: str | None,
        decision: DecisionKind,
        justify_bead: str | None = None,
        override_bead: str | None = None,
        context_summary: dict | None = None,
        kill_switch_used: bool = False,
    ) -> None: ...
```

Single method, kwargs-only, no overloads. Synchronous append; one line per call; no batching. Matches t2zb §E contract exactly.

## 8. Open click param ergonomics

Adding `--justify` / `--override` to 12 commands is repetitive. Two options:
- (a) Each command opts in via two `@click.option` decorators above the `@requires_rule_check` line. Boilerplate but explicit.
- (b) The `requires_rule_check` decorator itself attaches the click options programmatically.

**Decision: (b).** Click supports decorator-attached options. Reduces 24 lines (2 per command) of boilerplate, keeps the rule-check contract self-contained.

## 9. Backward-compat & schema migration

- `orgs` table gains a `rule_engine_loaded_at` column (TIMESTAMP NULL). Set on every `qn org` start to `NOW()`. NULL on legacy rows; populated forward.
- A migration file at `cli/core/db/migrations/<n>_add_rule_engine_loaded_at.py` is idempotent.
- Loader handles missing `rules.yaml` gracefully (default catalog + one-time stderr warning per t2zb §I).

## 10. Constants required

In `cli/core/constants/`:
- `RULES_AUDIT_FILENAME = "rules-audit.jsonl"`
- `DEFAULT_RULES_TEMPLATE_PATH = cli/config/templates/default-rules.yaml` (Path)
- `RULE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3` (int)
- `KILL_SWITCH_ENV_VAR = "QUINNAI_RULES_DISABLED"`
- Action-name string constants for the 12 v0 surfaces (e.g. `ACTION_QN_ORG_HIRE = "qn-org.hire"`)

## 11. Exception hierarchy additions (`shared/exceptions.py`)

```python
class RuleEngineError(Exception):
    """Base for all rules-engine errors."""

class RuleViolation(RuleEngineError):
    """Raised when evaluate_or_raise hits a BLOCK-class decision."""
    def __init__(self, decision: Decision):
        self.decision = decision

class RuleSetLoadError(RuleEngineError):
    """Loader failed (YAML parse, schema validation, regex compile)."""

class RuleEvalTimeout(RuleEngineError):
    """signal.alarm fired during evaluate(). Engine fail-closed."""
```

Specific exceptions, not generic `Exception` — per CLAUDE.md error-handling rule.
acceptance_criteria: design doc lists exact file paths for new modules, exact dataclass fields, exact CLI arg shapes. Reviewer can write tests against it without ambiguity.
close_reason: Architecture captured in --design. 6-module map (types/loader/audit/engine/decorators/cli); ctx.obj DI for rules + rules_audit; DisabledRuleEngine swap for kill-switch (branch-free hot path); decorator attaches --justify/--override click options programmatically; permissions decorator OUTSIDE rule-check decorator; rule_engine_loaded_at column on orgs table; specific exception hierarchy (RuleEngineError/RuleViolation/RuleSetLoadError/RuleEvalTimeout).
