design:
# Org Templates — System Design (translated from quinn-ai-56yh requirements)

> Note: bead description's original wording — "topological sort over template.requires" and "TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team(template_name, team_name, manager_id, ctx)" — is partially stale per the user's batch-3 decision (reference-existing semantics, no DAG sort). This document supersedes that wording. Composition resolution is a one-call validator, not a topological sort.

## A. YAML schema — `org/config/templates.yaml`

### Top-level
```yaml
version: 1                       # required, integer
templates:                       # required, list, may be empty
  - name: product_team           # required, kebab/snake_case, unique within file
    description: "Standard product team — PM-led, ships features."  # required
    members:                     # required, non-empty list
      - role: pm                 # required, free-form string
        count: 1                 # required, positive int
        is_manager: true         # optional, bool, default false; exactly ONE manager per template
        cost: 60                 # required, int 0-100, passed to existing `qn org hire --cost`
      - role: engineer
        count: 2
        cost: 50
    channel:                     # optional; if absent, no channel created at hire-team time
      auto_create: true          # default true if `channel:` present
      name_template: "product-{team_name}"  # `{team_name}` substituted at hire-time
    requires: [product_team]     # optional, list of template names; reference-existing parent dep
    initial_okrs: []             # optional, list of OKR specs (see §A.3); default []
    ttl_hours: null              # optional, positive int or null; non-null = time-bounded
```

### A.1 Required fields per template
- `name`, `description`, `members` (with each member having `role`, `count`, `cost`).

### A.2 `is_manager` validation
- Exactly one member with `is_manager: true` per template. Loader fails closed with a clear error if zero or more than one.

### A.3 `initial_okrs` shape
```yaml
initial_okrs:
  - title: "Resolve incident within {ttl_hours}h"
    description: "..."
    key_results:
      - metric: "incident.resolved"
        target: 1
        unit: "boolean"
```
Substitution variables in `title`/`description`: `{team_name}`, `{ttl_hours}` (only meaningful for time-bounded templates).

### A.4 Defaults file
- `cli/config/default_team_templates.yaml` ships with the 5 v0 templates from 56yh §1.
- `qn org init` copies it to `org/config/templates.yaml` if no templates.yaml exists. Operator edits in place; no merge logic.
- File location chosen to avoid name collision with existing `cli/config/templates/` (Jinja briefing templates).

## B. In-memory data model — `cli/core/templates/types.py`

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateMember:
    role: str
    count: int
    cost: int                    # 0-100
    is_manager: bool = False

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChannelSpec:
    auto_create: bool
    name_template: str           # uses `{team_name}` placeholder

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InitialOKR:
    title: str
    description: str
    key_results: tuple[dict, ...]  # each dict has metric, target, unit

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Template:
    name: str
    description: str
    members: tuple[TemplateMember, ...]
    channel: Optional[ChannelSpec] = None
    requires: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    initial_okrs: tuple[InitialOKR, ...] = ()
    ttl_hours: Optional[int] = None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateRegistry:
    version: int
    templates: tuple[Template, ...]
    source_path: str             # absolute path to templates.yaml

    def get(self, name: str) -> Template:
        """Returns the Template with the given name. Raises TemplateNotFound if absent."""
```

## C. Public Python API

### C.1 Loader — `cli/core/templates/loader.py`
```python
def load_templates(org_path: Path) -> TemplateRegistry:
    """Read org/config/templates.yaml. If missing, fall back to default_team_templates.yaml.
    Fails closed on YAML parse errors or schema-validation errors with a clear path-citing message."""
```

### C.2 Composition validator — `cli/core/templates/composition.py`
```python
def validate_parent_reference(
    template: Template,
    parent_team_name: Optional[str],
    db: Database,
) -> Optional[str]:
    """If template.requires is non-empty, verify parent_team_name resolves to an existing
    active team whose `template_type` matches one of template.requires.
    Returns the parent team's lead_id (the manager the new team's manager reports to).
    Raises TemplateMissingParent / TemplateWrongParentType / TemplateParentTerminated.
    NO topological sort, NO cycle detection — single-edge validation only."""
```

### C.3 Orchestrator — `cli/core/templates/orchestrator.py`
```python
class TemplateOrchestrator:
    def __init__(self, ctx: Context, db: Database, registry: TemplateRegistry): ...

    def hire_team(
        self,
        template_name: str,
        team_name: str,
        manager_id: str,         # the existing worker who will be this team's manager's reports-to
        *,
        parent_team_name: Optional[str] = None,
        size_overrides: dict[str, int] = {},      # {"engineer": 3}
        cost_overrides: dict[str, int] = {},      # {"engineer": 70}
        worker_names: dict[str, list[str]] = {},  # {"engineer": ["bob", "alice"]}
        dry_run: bool = False,
    ) -> HireTeamResult:
        """Atomic hire-team operation. Sequence in §D. Rolls back on partial failure."""

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HireTeamResult:
    team_id: str
    channel_id: Optional[str]
    worker_ids: tuple[str, ...]    # in hire order
    okr_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    rolled_back: bool = False
    failure_reason: Optional[str] = None
```

## D. Orchestration sequence (atomic with rollback)

For `hire_team(template_name, team_name, manager_id, parent_team_name=...)`:

1. **Load + validate.** `template = registry.get(template_name)`. Validate `is_manager` count == 1 (defensive; loader should already have caught this). Apply `size_overrides` and `cost_overrides`.
2. **Validate parent reference** (§C.2) — fail before touching DB.
3. **Validate manager exists** — `db.get_worker(manager_id)` non-None and active.
4. **Pre-validate channel collision** — if `template.channel.auto_create`, derive channel name and check no existing channel uses it. Fail loud if collision.
5. **Reserve team_id** — `team_id = generate_id("team")`. No DB write yet.
6. **Begin transaction.** All subsequent steps are tracked in a local rollback stack.
7. **Create team record** — `create_team(db, name=team_name, parent_team_id=<resolved>, lead_id=<TBD>, auto_create_channel=False)`. Push `team` to rollback stack.
8. **Create channel** (if specified) — `create_channel(db, name=<derived>, channel_type="team", team_id=team_id)`. Push channel to rollback stack. Update team record with channel_id.
9. **Hire each member.** Iterate members: manager first, then others in YAML order. For each member, for each instance up to count:
   - Determine name (from `worker_names[role]` if provided, else auto-generate `<role>-<team_name>-<index>`).
   - Call programmatic hire path (NOT the click command — extract a `hire_worker(db, name, role, manager_id, cost) -> Worker` helper from `cli.commands.org.hire:hire_cmd`'s body during impl). Push each new worker to rollback stack.
   - Call `add_team_member(db, team_id, worker_id, role)`.
   - If member.is_manager, store this worker_id as the team's `lead_id`.
10. **Update team's lead_id** — `db.execute("UPDATE teams SET lead_id = ? WHERE id = ?", (manager_worker_id, team_id))`. The manager-of-this-team is the worker we just hired with is_manager=true. The `manager_id` parameter to hire_team is the worker that THIS new manager will report to in the org chart (i.e. the org-chart parent of the team manager, not the parent_team_id which is the team-level dep).
11. **Subscribe channel members** — for each new worker, subscribe to channel.
12. **File initial OKRs** — for each `initial_okr`, call `qn org okr set` programmatic path. Push each OKR to rollback stack. (Will hit BOARD-RULES rule #10 once that ships.)
13. **Set template_type and ttl** — `db.execute("UPDATE teams SET template_type = ?, ttl_hours = ?, ttl_started_at = ? WHERE id = ?", (template_name, template.ttl_hours, now if template.ttl_hours else None, team_id))`.
14. **Commit transaction.** Return `HireTeamResult(rolled_back=False)`.

### D.1 Rollback strategy
On any exception at step 7+, iterate the rollback stack in reverse:
- For each new OKR: close with status=cancelled, reason="hire-team rollback".
- For each new worker: call programmatic fire path with reason="hire-team rollback", `terminate_immediately=True`.
- Drop the channel.
- Delete the team row.
- Commit the rollback. Return `HireTeamResult(rolled_back=True, failure_reason=<exception summary>)`.

If rollback itself fails (which would leave the org in a partial state), raise `HireTeamRollbackFailed` with both the original exception and the rollback exception. Operator must hand-inspect.

### D.2 Dry-run
`dry_run=True` runs steps 1-4 (validation only), returns a synthetic `HireTeamResult` with the IDs that *would* be assigned (`team_id="dry:product_team"`, etc.) so the operator can preview without touching DB.

## E. Schema migrations

Add columns to existing `teams` table:
- `template_type TEXT NULL` — name of the template that produced this team (NULL for teams created before this lands).
- `ttl_hours INTEGER NULL` — non-null only for time-bounded templates.
- `ttl_started_at TIMESTAMP NULL` — set on team creation if ttl_hours is non-null.

A migration file ships at `cli/core/db/migrations/<n>_add_team_template_fields.py`. Runs idempotently on next `qn org` start.

## F. CLI surface

### F.1 New commands
- `qn org hire-team` — registered under existing `org` group; click decorator adds `@requires_rule_check("qn-org.hire-team")` for BOARD-RULES integration.
- `qn org templates list` — lists templates from the org's templates.yaml + the defaults.
- `qn org templates show <name>` — prints the template's full spec.
- `qn org templates validate` — runs the loader against templates.yaml; non-zero exit on schema errors.

### F.2 Wire-up
- `cli/commands/org/hire_team.py` — new file. Click command + entry-point function `hire_team_cmd`. Reads click params, builds `size_overrides` and `cost_overrides` dicts from `--override` repeated flag, calls `TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team()`, prints `HireTeamResult` summary.
- `cli/commands/org/templates.py` — new file. Click subgroup `templates` with `list`, `show`, `validate`.
- `cli/commands/org/__init__.py` — register both new groups.

## G. Briefing template integration (per A.4.7 of the epic)

Workers hired via hire-team get an additional briefing variable:
- `team_template`: the template name (`product_team`, etc.) — None for workers hired the standard way.
- `team_name`: the human-friendly team name.
- `team_member_count`: total worker count in this team.
- `team_role`: the role this worker holds within the template.

`cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2` gets a new "Team Membership" section that renders only when `team_template is not None`. Shows the operator-readable description and a link to the template spec ("Run `qn org templates show <name>` for the full template definition").

## H. Role-specific briefings (per 56yh §3)

`cli/config/templates/role_briefings/<role>.md.jinja2` — one file per well-known role (`pm`, `engineer`, `designer`, `qa`, `data-eng`, `sre`, `ml-eng`, `analyst`, `research-lead`, `tech-lead`, `incident-commander`).

The briefing-render path (`cli/core/onboarding.py`) gets a hook: if a worker's role matches a well-known name AND `team_template is not None`, the role-specific briefing is rendered as an "Additional Role Guidance" section appended to the main briefing. Unknown roles → no append, generic briefing only.

## I. File layout

New files:
- `cli/core/templates/__init__.py` — re-exports public API.
- `cli/core/templates/types.py` — dataclasses (§B).
- `cli/core/templates/loader.py` — `load_templates(org_path)` (§C.1).
- `cli/core/templates/composition.py` — `validate_parent_reference()` (§C.2).
- `cli/core/templates/orchestrator.py` — `TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team()` (§C.3).
- `cli/commands/org/hire_team.py` — Click command (§F.2).
- `cli/commands/org/templates.py` — Click subgroup (§F.2).
- `cli/config/default_team_templates.yaml` — 5 default templates.
- `cli/config/templates/role_briefings/<role>.md.jinja2` — 11 role briefings (§H).
- `cli/core/db/migrations/<n>_add_team_template_fields.py` — schema migration.

Modified files:
- `cli/commands/org/__init__.py` — register `hire-team` and `templates` groups.
- `cli/commands/org/hire.py` — extract `hire_worker(db, ...)` programmatic helper from `hire_cmd` body so the orchestrator can call it without going through click. (Keep `hire_cmd` as the click wrapper.)
- `cli/commands/org/fire.py` — extract `fire_worker(db, ...)` programmatic helper (for rollback).
- `cli/core/onboarding.py` — wire role-briefing append (§H).
- `cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2` — Team Membership section (§G).
- `cli/core/queries/team.py` — extend Team dataclass with `template_type`, `ttl_hours`, `ttl_started_at` fields; update `create_team` to accept these.
- `shared/exceptions.py` — add `TemplateNotFound`, `TemplateMissingParent`, `TemplateWrongParentType`, `TemplateParentTerminated`, `HireTeamRollbackFailed`, `ChannelNameCollision`.
- `cli/core/constants/__init__.py` — add `DEFAULT_TEAM_TEMPLATES_PATH`, role-name constants for the well-known registry.

## J. Performance budget

- `load_templates()` target: <50ms cold (YAML parse for ≤20 templates).
- `validate_parent_reference()` target: <5ms (single DB lookup).
- `hire_team()` end-to-end is dominated by per-worker session-spawn cost (existing constraint, ~5-30s per worker depending on provider). Templates add no measurable overhead.

## K. Backward compatibility

- Orgs without `templates.yaml` get the default catalog (5 templates) on first `qn org templates list` invocation. One-time stderr warning. Operator runs `qn org templates validate` to surface any local-edit issues.
- Existing teams (created before template_type column existed) have NULL `template_type`. They cannot be referenced as `--under` parents because the validator requires `template_type` to match one of `template.requires`. Operator can manually set it via `qn org templates retag <team> <template_name>` (out of scope for v0; flag for v1 if needed).
- Canaries 01–11 still pass with templates wired in (verification step in Phase 5).

## L. Open Phase-3 strategy items
- Whether `hire_team()` runs as one click invocation or spawns worker hires sequentially (parallel hiring would be faster but session-spawn race conditions are real). Default: sequential.
- Whether the rollback path is fully synchronous or kicks off async cleanup. Default: synchronous.
- Whether `ttl_hours` enforcement (auto-fire of incident_response_squad after TTL expires) is an active monitor or a passive check. Default: passive — surfaces in `qn org status` and operator runs `qn org templates expire-ttl` to fire stale teams.
acceptance_criteria: docs/board-templates-system-design.md exists with full schema, orchestrator API, rollback strategy, and the integration points named.
close_reason: System design captured in --design (option-b). Includes: full templates.yaml schema with required fields and is_manager constraint; in-memory data model (TemplateMember/Template/TemplateRegistry); loader with default-fallback; composition validator (NOT topological sort — reference-existing only); TemplateOrchestrator.hire_team() with 14-step atomic sequence + full rollback strategy; dry-run; schema migration for template_type/ttl_hours; CLI surface (qn org hire-team + qn org templates list/show/validate); briefing template integration with role-specific overlays for well-known roles (11 well-known roles); file layout; backward compat; open Phase-3 strategy items flagged. Reuses existing primitives: cli/core/queries/team.create_team, cli/core/queries/channel.create_channel, programmatic hire/fire helpers (to be extracted), qn org okr set.

title: [BOARD-TPL] Capture user requirements for org templates
description: Why: pin down what 'template' means in this org — fixed sizes? size ranges? dynamic role names? — before specifying schema. Without this we'll re-litigate semantics during impl. What: produce docs/board-templates-requirements.md covering: (a) the use cases (product team, data team, launch pod, incident-response squad, >=5 examples), (b) what each template specifies (members with role+count+cost, manager structure within the team, default budgets, default channels, optional initial OKRs), (c) composition semantics (does launch_pod 'require' a product_team or 'reference' an existing one?), (d) how the CEO triggers a template (single CLI call vs. multi-step wizard?), (e) what happens when a template includes another template (recursive expansion vs. dep-graph), (f) explicit non-goals for v0 (e.g. dynamic team-size based on org-wide load? not yet).
design:
# Org Templates — User Requirements (final)

## 1. v0 catalog (5 templates)

| Template                  | Composition                       | Notes                                                                  |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| product_team              | standalone                        | 1 PM (manager), 2 engineers, 1 UI/UX, 1 QA. 5 workers.                 |
| data_team                 | standalone                        | 1 lead data eng (manager), 1 data eng, 1 analyst, 1 ML eng. 4 workers. |
| launch_pod                | requires: [product_team]          | 1 tech lead (manager), 1 engineer, 1 designer, 1 QA. 4 workers. References an existing product_team via `--under`. |
| incident_response_squad   | standalone, time-bounded          | 1 incident commander (manager), 2 SREs, 1 comms lead. 4 workers. Auto-fires after `ttl_hours` (default 72h) unless extended. |
| research_pod              | standalone                        | 1 research lead (manager), 2 researchers, 1 prototype eng. 4 workers.  |

### 1a. Out of scope for v0
- `oncall_rotation` — rotations cycle workers on a schedule; doesn't fit the "hire a team" model.

## 2. Sizing
Fixed sizes per template. Per-instantiation override at hire-time via `--override <role>:<count>` (or `--override <role>:cost=<n>` for cost).

## 3. Roles
Free-form role strings. Well-known role registry: `engineer`, `pm`, `designer`, `qa`, `data-eng`, `sre`, `ml-eng`, `analyst`, `research-lead`, `tech-lead`, `incident-commander`. Well-known roles get tailored briefings at `cli/config/templates/role_briefings/<role>.md.jinja2`. Unknown roles fall back to generic.

## 4. Costs — DO NOT REINVENT
Costs are LLM-tier values (existing 0-100 scale). Templates carry a default `cost` per role member that hire-team passes through to the existing `qn org hire --cost <n>` flow. Existing `cli/core/budget/{enforcer,service}` enforces budget at the per-hire boundary. Templates do NOT introduce a new budget model.

## 5. Channels (Q4=a)
hire-team auto-creates a channel named per `name_template` (e.g. `product-{team_name}`) and subscribes all new workers + the manager. Fail-loud on collision: operator picks a different `--name`.

## 6. Initial OKRs (Q5)
Optional `initial_okrs` per template. Most templates ship with `[]`. `incident_response_squad` ships with a default OKR ("resolve incident within ttl_hours"). Filed via existing `qn org okr set` — automatically traverses BOARD-RULES rule #10 (`okr-set-mid-quarter`).

## 7. Composition (Q8 decided: reference-existing only)
Templates with non-empty `requires` MUST be invoked with `--under <existing-team-name>`. hire-team validates the parent team exists and matches the required template type. **No recursive auto-creation.** **No topological sort, no cycle detection** — the dep graph is trivially shallow (one edge in v0). lnwg's bead description gets simplified accordingly (see §Bead-corrections).

Cascade-fire behavior (parent firing while child team exists): refuse to fire the parent until children are fired. Implementation detail flagged for Phase 3 strategy bead, not user-facing capability for v0.

## 8. Hire-time UX (single CLI call, no wizard)
```
qn org hire-team \
  --template=<name> \
  --name=<team-name> \
  --manager=<existing-worker> \
  [--under=<parent-team-name>]                # required iff template.requires non-empty
  [--override <role>:<count>] [...]            # repeatable; size override
  [--override <role>:cost=<n>] [...]           # repeatable; per-role LLM-cost override
  [--worker-names "<role>:<name>,..."]         # optional explicit names; default auto-generated
  [--dry-run]                                  # preview without executing
```

Auto-naming default: `<role>-<team_name>-<index>` (e.g. `engineer-mobile-app-1`, `engineer-mobile-app-2`).

Rollback: hire-team is transactional. If any single hire fails mid-sequence, prior hires from this invocation are reversed (fired) and a clear error is reported with the failure point. Audit trail: a single hire-team-run record links all the per-worker hires and the rollback if any.

## 9. YAML schema for `org/config/templates.yaml`
```yaml
version: 1
templates:
  - name: product_team
    description: "Standard product team — PM-led, ships features."
    members:
      - role: pm
        count: 1
        is_manager: true        # exactly one per template
        cost: 60                # 0-100, passed to existing hire system
      - role: engineer
        count: 2
        cost: 50
      - role: designer
        count: 1
        cost: 45
      - role: qa
        count: 1
        cost: 40
    channel:
      auto_create: true
      name_template: "product-{team_name}"
    requires: []
    initial_okrs: []
    ttl_hours: null             # only meaningful for time-bounded templates
```

## 10. Non-goals (v0)
1. No recursive auto-creation of dependency templates (Q8).
2. No topological sort / cycle detection (consequence of #1).
3. No template inheritance — templates are flat, no `extends`.
4. No conditional/dynamic template content — no "if env=prod, add an SRE".
5. No team-size auto-scaling — sizes fixed; operator overrides per-instantiation or hires/fires individuals.
6. No template-driven offboarding ("fire the whole team in one call"). Tear-down uses existing per-worker `qn org fire`.
7. No template usage at `qn org init` time — templates only used by hire-team after init.
8. No `oncall_rotation` template.
9. No hot-reload of template definitions — edits to templates.yaml take effect on next `qn org` start.
10. No per-template feature-flag / staged rollout — templates are either in `templates.yaml` or they aren't.

## 11. MVP done when…
1. `qn org hire-team --template=<name> --name=<team-name> --manager=<worker>` works for all 5 default templates.
2. `qn org templates list | show | validate` work.
3. `--under <parent-team>` required when `requires` non-empty; missing produces clear error.
4. `--override <role>:<count>` and `--override <role>:cost=<n>` work and are mutually compatible.
5. Auto-channel-create on hire-team; fail-loud on collision.
6. Rollback on partial failure: prior hires reversed; single error message with failure point.
7. `initial_okrs` filed via `qn org okr set` at hire-team time; goes through BOARD-RULES.
8. Live-LLM canary 12 (quinn-ai-l2wl) passes: CEO uses `qn org hire-team` to spin up product_team, then launch_pod under it.
9. Briefing template renders worker's template membership for new hires.
10. Full pytest suite green; canaries 01–11 still green.

## §Bead-corrections (apply during this requirements pass)
- `quinn-ai-lnwg` — description currently says "topological sort over template.requires" with cycle detection. Reference-existing semantics make this unnecessary in v0. Description updated to "validate `--under` reference exists and template type matches required parent type." Updated in this turn.
acceptance_criteria: docs/board-templates-requirements.md exists with >=5 example templates spelled out, composition semantics decided, non-goals listed.

title: [BOARD-RULES] Technical strategy: where rules load, how they inject, override mechanics
description: Why: with reqs + failing tests in place, settle the implementation plan before writing code. What: write a short strategy doc (or update docs/board-rules-system-design.md) covering (a) where rules are loaded — at qn-process startup via Context (so every CLI command has access without explicit threading), (b) how the engine is injected — a decorator @check_rules('action_name') applied to each command's body, OR an explicit ctx.rules.evaluate() call near the top of each command (decide which and document tradeoffs), (c) the override flow — --override accepts a bead-id, the engine looks up the bead, verifies status=='approved' AND assignee role contains 'board', returns allow if both pass, (d) audit logging strategy — append to org/live/audit.jsonl (one line per evaluation) AND emit to stderr at WARN level for ADVISORY+, (e) rollback plan if bugs surface — a kill-switch env QUINNAI_RULES_DISABLED=1 that short-circuits the engine to allow-everything-with-warning.
design:
# BOARD-RULES Phase 3 — Technical Strategy

Builds on quinn-ai-t2zb (system design). This bead resolves implementation strategy decisions and the open Phase-3 questions §J flagged.

## 1. Decorator-based wiring (open Q1 from t2zb)

**Decision: decorator wins.** Mirrors the existing `requires_permission` pattern in `cli/core/permissions/access_control.py:525`. Each rule-aware command gets `@requires_rule_check("qn-org.<action>")` above the `@click.command()` decorator. The decorator extracts click params, builds the action context, calls `evaluate_or_raise(ctx, action, context, justify_bead_id=..., override_bead_id=...)`.

**Testability concern:** decorators are harder to unit-test than inline calls. Mitigation: the engine itself is tested via direct `RuleEngine.evaluate()` calls (no decorator); decorator behavior is tested via `click.testing.CliRunner` with a mock engine. Two layers, two test surfaces, no overlap.

## 2. AuditLogger location (open Q2 from t2zb)

**Decision: ctx-bound.** `ctx.obj.rules_audit` is initialized in `cli/main.py`'s org-context loader. Same lifecycle as `ctx.obj.db`. Tests inject a fake AuditLogger via the Click context, no monkey-patching of module globals. Module-level singleton was the alternative; rejected because it leaks state between tests and across orgs in a long-lived `qn` process (host mode).

## 3. Briefing template ruleset access (open Q3 from t2zb)

**Decision: pass via Jinja context at render time.** `cli/core/onboarding.py` calls `load_rules(org_path)` once before rendering, passes `rules=ruleset.rules` to the Jinja env. The template iterates and renders. No disk read inside the template — that would create a circular import path between rendering and rule loading.

## 4. Kill-switch

**Mechanism:** environment variable `QUINNAI_RULES_DISABLED=1` short-circuits `evaluate_or_raise` to a `Decision(kind=ALLOW, message="rules engine disabled via QUINNAI_RULES_DISABLED")`. Every short-circuited evaluation is still audited with `kill_switch_used=true` so post-mortem investigators can find emergency-use windows.

**Use case:** the engine itself has a bug that's blocking legitimate work and the operator needs to ship a fix without first un-breaking the engine.

**Not allowed:** disabling individual ABSOLUTE rules at runtime. ABSOLUTE rules can ONLY be disabled by editing `rules.yaml` and restarting the org. The kill-switch is all-or-nothing.

## 5. Performance strategy

- **Regex compilation:** `RuleSet` loader compiles every `pattern.expr` at load time, not at evaluate time. Compiled patterns live in a side-cache `dict[str, re.Pattern]` keyed by `Rule.id`. Frozen `Rule` dataclass + side-cache lets us keep dataclass immutability without re-compiling on every evaluate.
- **Rule-set indexing:** `RuleSet.rules_by_action: dict[str, tuple[Rule, ...]]` built at load time. `evaluate(action, ...)` only iterates rules that target the named action — not the full ruleset. Linear in matching-rules, not total-rules.
- **Eval timeout:** wrap each `evaluate()` call in `signal.alarm(3)` (default 3s, configurable via `RULE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). On timeout: `Decision(kind=BLOCK, message="rule evaluation timeout — engine fail-closed")`. Audit logs the timeout.

## 6. Implementation order (Phase 4)

Sequential, each step independently testable:
1. `cli/core/rules/types.py` — dataclasses + enums. Closes prereq for engine + loader.
2. `cli/core/rules/audit.py` — `AuditLogger` writing JSONL. Mockable.
3. `cli/core/rules/loader.py` — `load_rules(org_path)`. Drives `cli/config/templates/default-rules.yaml` shipping.
4. `cli/core/rules/engine.py` — `RuleEngine.evaluate()` + `evaluate_or_raise()` helper. Makes severity-behavior tests (kj9s) green.
5. `cli/core/rules/decorators.py` — `requires_rule_check` Click decorator.
6. Wire decorators into 12 surfaces (one PR per group: lifecycle, resource, comms, beads).
7. `cli/core/rules/cli.py` — `qn org rules {add,list,disable,test,validate}` subcommands.
8. Briefing template integration (`cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2`).
9. Live-LLM canary 11 (snfq) green.

Each step has a corresponding Phase-2 test bead, so progress is verifiable end-of-step.

## 7. Migration / backward-compat strategy

- Orgs without `rules.yaml`: loader applies default catalog (14 rules from c5hb §3) with one-time stderr warning. Operator runs `qn org rules edit` (alias for opening the file) when ready to customize.
- Existing canaries 01–10: default catalog is intentionally non-blocking on canary scenarios. Verification: run all canaries against a pre-Phase-4 branch and a post-wired branch; compare for behavioral drift. Out of scope for this bead but is a Phase-5 acceptance gate.
- Schema: a new `rule_engine_loaded_at` column on the `orgs` table tracks which version of rules.yaml a given org boot loaded. Useful for post-mortem debugging.

## 8. Testing strategy

- **Unit (Phase 4 makes Phase-2 tests green):**
  - `RuleEngine.evaluate()` — direct call, fake Database, MagicMock AuditLogger.
  - `load_rules()` — `tmp_path`-backed; round-trips YAML → RuleSet.
  - `requires_rule_check` decorator — `click.testing.CliRunner` against a fake command.
- **Integration (Phase 4 closes 9luv):**
  - Real `qn org hire/fire/promote/demote` invocations against a tmp org with a tmp rules.yaml.
  - Verifies decision flows end-to-end (block, justify, override).
- **Live-LLM (Phase 5 closes snfq):**
  - Worker session sees rules in briefing.
  - Worker attempts ABSOLUTE rule → blocked.
  - Worker attempts REQUIRED rule → blocked, files override-request bead, manager approves, retry succeeds.

## 9. Risks + mitigations

| Risk                                                  | Mitigation                                                                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Regex-pattern crashes engine on bad input             | Pre-compile at load (fails closed); per-eval timeout via signal.alarm                       |
| Decorator order vs. existing decorators (e.g. permissions) on same command | Apply rule-check INSIDE permissions check (rule check assumes worker is authenticated)      |
| Audit log file fills disk                             | Out of scope for v0; operator handles rotation. Document in MVP-done as known-limitation    |
| Override bead flow lets manager approve their own rule violation | Engine checks `bead.approver_id == worker.manager_id`, NOT `bead.approver_id == worker_id`. CEO has no manager → cannot self-override |
| Kill-switch left on after emergency                   | Audit log flags `kill_switch_used=true`; recommend ops dashboard surface this in board UI  |
acceptance_criteria: strategy decisions documented; tradeoffs (decorator vs. inline call) named; kill-switch env documented.
close_reason: Strategy captured in --design. Decided: decorator-based wiring (mirrors requires_permission); ctx-bound AuditLogger; Jinja-context briefing render; QUINNAI_RULES_DISABLED kill-switch (audited); compiled-regex side-cache; signal.alarm timeout (3s default); 9-step impl order; permissions-then-rules decorator stacking.

title: [host-mode-init] Architecture & Interface Design
description: Component boundaries, interface contracts, file locations.
design:
Module-level architecture (revised post-strategy with $PATH shim mechanism).

NEW MODULES:

cli/core/host_mode.py:
  def find_org_root(start: Path) -> Path | None:
      walks up looking for .quinnai/ marker; returns the .quinnai/ path or None.
  def is_host_mode(org_path: Path) -> bool:
      reads org_state.project_root from quin.db. True iff non-null.
  def get_project_root(org_path: Path) -> Path:
      returns Path(org_state.project_root). Raises if not host mode.

scripts/quinnai-bd-shim (new file, bash 3.2):
  #!/bin/bash
  # Shim that intercepts bd commands and enforces per-assignee write isolation
  # when QUINN_WORKER_ID is set.
  REAL_BD=$(command -v bd)  # locate real bd, skipping ourselves via type -a if needed
  case "$1" in
    close|update)
      # detect close intent (bd close X | bd update X --status=closed)
      if [ -n "$QUINN_WORKER_ID" ]; then
        bead_id=$(<extract from args>)
        assignee=$("$REAL_BD" show --json "$bead_id" | <jq or sed for assignee>)
        if [ "$assignee" != "$QUINN_WORKER_ID" ]; then
          echo "Error: worker $QUINN_WORKER_ID cannot close bead assigned to $assignee" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
      ;;
  esac
  exec "$REAL_BD" "$@"

MODIFIED MODULES:

cli/core/org_init/init.py:
  initialize_org gains host_mode: bool = False kwarg. Branches in init_org:
    if host_mode: org_metadata_root = org_path / '.quinnai'; project_root = org_path
    else: org_metadata_root = org_path (existing path)
  Stores project_root into org_state on commit.

cli/core/org_init/scaffolding.py:
  create_folder_structure(base) gets called with .quinnai/ in host mode, org_path/ in greenfield.
  init_beads gets a host_mode_skip path (no-op in host mode).
  create_org_documentation skips root README in host mode; writes .quinnai/README.md instead (or skips entirely).
  install_bd_shim(project_root): copies scripts/quinnai-bd-shim to project_root/.quinnai/bin/bd; chmods +x. Idempotent.

cli/core/db/schema.py (or migrations dir):
  Add migration: ALTER TABLE org_state ADD COLUMN project_root TEXT NULL.
  Existing rows get NULL → is_host_mode() returns False for them.

cli/core/onboarding.py:
  get_worker_session_working_directory(org_path, worker_id) — branches on is_host_mode:
    if host: return get_project_root(org_path)
    else: return existing storage_manager.get_worker_path(worker_id)
  get_worker_env_vars(org_path, worker_id) — branches on is_host_mode:

title: [host-mode-init] Technical Strategy
description: Implementation order, risks, rollback plan.
design:
Implementation order (smallest blast radius first):

1. cli/core/host_mode.py: pure helper — find_org_root(start), is_host_mode(org_path), get_project_root(org_path). No side effects. Lands first because tests reference the import.

2. Schema migration: add nullable project_root column to org_state. Backward-compat — existing greenfield orgs leave it null and report is_host_mode=false.

3. cli/core/org_init/init.py + scaffolding.py: accept host_mode kwarg + project_root. Branch in init_org and create_folder_structure to lay out under project_root/.quinnai/ instead of org_path/. Skip bd init in host mode. Skip root template renders (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md).

4. .quinnai/bin/bd shim — REVISED MECHANISM. bd has no per-action hook system; bd hooks command manages GIT hooks only (pre-commit etc.). So the trust boundary uses a $PATH shim instead of a non-existent bd hook.
   - The shim is a bash 3.2 script at <project_root>/.quinnai/bin/bd.
   - Inspects bd subcommand. For 'close' or 'update --status=closed':
     * Read bead's current assignee via 'bd show --json <id>'.
     * If $QUINN_WORKER_ID is set AND assignee != $QUINN_WORKER_ID, exit non-zero with stderr error.
   - Otherwise exec the real bd binary with all args.
   - Source lives in scripts/quinnai-bd-shim. qn org init --host copies it to <project_root>/.quinnai/bin/bd and chmods +x.

5. Session env: in host mode, prepend <project_root>/.quinnai/bin/ to $PATH so workers' 'bd close' resolves to the shim. Humans on the host shell don't have that PATH entry, so they bypass.

6. cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2: pass is_host_mode + project_root into render context. Add a top-of-Responsibility-section block when host mode.

7. cli/core/onboarding.py: get_worker_session_working_directory and get_worker_env_vars branch on is_host_mode. cwd = project_root, $WORKER_STORAGE = .quinnai/storage/workers/<path>/.

8. CEO INITIAL_TASK.md template: host-mode variant runs bd ready as survey + msgr post + 5min idle then auto-claim CEO's own OKR (filter --label=okr --assignee=<ceo-id>).

9. CLI auto-detection in cli/commands/org/init.py: if --org-path has .beads/ or .git/ and --host wasn't passed and --no-host wasn't passed, enable host mode and print notice.

Risks:
- Schema migration on existing greenfield orgs: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with NULL default — must be tested against an existing org fixture.
- bash 3.2 compatibility: the shim must avoid associative arrays, mapfile, readarray.
- Workers in tmux invoke bd directly — $PATH manipulation must be in the spawn env (not just .bashrc/.zshrc which may not load in non-interactive shells).
- The shim adds a fork+bd-show roundtrip per close. Acceptable cost.
- Scenario harness FakeSpawner: must mirror host-mode env (PATH, WORKER_STORAGE) so canary tests exercise the same code path as live runs.

Rollback: each phase is its own commit. Schema migration is the only non-trivial rollback (column stays around but gets ignored).

What we're NOT doing in v1:
- Supervised approval queue.
- Multi-project monorepo.
- Migration tool from greenfield to host.
close_reason: Strategy locked. Key surprise during strategy phase: bd has no per-action hook; the trust boundary mechanism is a $PATH shim at .quinnai/bin/bd, not a .beads/hooks/pre-update file. Original architecture had this wrong; strategy phase caught it. Tests will be updated in Phase 4 to match the shim mechanism (integration contract tests stay as-is).

design:
# Board Rules — System Design (translated from quinn-ai-c5hb requirements)

> Note: bead description's original text said override needs "assignee.role contains 'board'". User clarified in batch-1 capture: REQUIRED override is direct-manager approval, not board. This document supersedes that wording.

## A. YAML schema — `org/config/rules.yaml`

### Top-level shape
```yaml
version: 1                       # schema version, required, integer
rules:                           # list, required, may be empty
  - id: no-drop-database         # required, kebab-case, unique within file
    severity: ABSOLUTE           # required, enum: SUGGESTED|ENCOURAGED|REQUIRED|ABSOLUTE
    actions:                     # required, list of action names (see §F)
      - "qn-bd.create"
    description: "Refuse SQL containing DROP TABLE..."  # required, string, shown in errors and briefing
    pattern:                     # optional, content match against action ctx (see §A.2)
      kind: regex
      target: body
      expr: "(?i)\\b(DROP\\s+TABLE|DROP\\s+DATABASE|TRUNCATE)\\b"
    scope:                       # optional, structural match against action ctx (see §A.3)
      env: prod
      worker_role_min_level: 0
    artifact_required: false     # optional, default false; ENCOURAGED only — if true, --justify is required
    notes: ""                    # optional, free-form, not surfaced to workers
```

### A.1 Required fields per rule
- `id`, `severity`, `actions`, `description`. Loader rejects rules missing any of these.

### A.2 `pattern` block (content matching)
- `kind` ∈ {`regex`, `contains`, `glob`}. Default `regex`.
- `target` ∈ {`body`, `command`, `argument:<name>`, `path`}. Names the field in action context to match against.
- `expr` is a string. For `regex`, must compile with `re.compile`; loader fails closed if not.
- If `pattern` absent, the rule fires on every invocation of the named actions (subject to `scope`).

### A.3 `scope` block (structural matching)
- `env` ∈ {`prod`, `staging`, `dev`} — matched against action ctx env. Optional.
- `worker_role_min_level` int — fires only if invoking worker is at or above this org-chart depth (CEO=0, direct reports=1, etc.). Optional.
- `worker_role` str — matches worker's role string exactly. Optional.
- `target_path_prefix` str — matches against any path-typed argument (e.g. for `rm -rf` or file tools). Optional.
- All present scope keys must match (AND), missing keys are wildcards. Empty scope = match everything.

### A.4 Defaults file
- `cli/config/templates/default-rules.yaml` ships with the 14 catalog rules from §3 of quinn-ai-c5hb.
- `qn org init` copies it to `org/config/rules.yaml` if no rules.yaml exists. Operator edits in place; no merge logic.

## B. In-memory data model — `cli/core/rules/types.py`

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum

class Severity(str, Enum):
    SUGGESTED = "SUGGESTED"
    ENCOURAGED = "ENCOURAGED"
    REQUIRED = "REQUIRED"
    ABSOLUTE = "ABSOLUTE"

class DecisionKind(str, Enum):
    ALLOW = "allow"               # no rule matched, or SUGGESTED with nudge issued
    BLOCK = "block"                # ABSOLUTE match, or ENCOURAGED/REQUIRED without valid override
    ALLOW_WITH_NUDGE = "allow_with_nudge"   # SUGGESTED match
    REQUIRES_JUSTIFY = "requires_justify"   # ENCOURAGED match, no --justify provided
    REQUIRES_OVERRIDE = "requires_override" # REQUIRED match, no --override provided

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Pattern:
    kind: str                      # regex|contains|glob
    target: str                    # body|command|argument:<name>|path
    expr: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scope:
    env: str | None = None
    worker_role: str | None = None
    worker_role_min_level: int | None = None
    target_path_prefix: str | None = None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rule:
    id: str
    severity: Severity
    actions: tuple[str, ...]
    description: str
    pattern: Pattern | None = None
    scope: Scope | None = None
    artifact_required: bool = False
    notes: str = ""

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RuleSet:
    version: int
    rules: tuple[Rule, ...]
    source_path: str               # absolute path to rules.yaml that produced this set

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Decision:
    kind: DecisionKind
    rule: Rule | None              # the matched rule, or None on ALLOW (no match)
    message: str                   # human-readable; safe to show in CLI output
    remediation: str               # what the worker should do next (file justify bead, request override, etc.)
```

## C. Public Python API — `cli/core/rules/engine.py`

```python
class RuleEngine:
    """Evaluates worker actions against a loaded RuleSet."""

    def __init__(self, ruleset: RuleSet, db: Database, logger: AuditLogger): ...

    def evaluate(
        self,
        action: str,            # canonical action name, e.g. "qn-org.hire"
        context: dict,          # action context (see §C.1)
        *,
        justify_bead_id: str | None = None,
        override_bead_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> Decision:
        """Evaluate the action against the ruleset. Always returns Decision (no exceptions on rule miss).

        Fail-closed: if ruleset is malformed, evaluate() raises RuleEngineError, which the
        decorator converts to a Decision(kind=BLOCK) with a clear remediation.
        """

# Module-level helper (used by CLI surfaces)
def evaluate_or_raise(
    ctx: ClickContext,
    action: str,
    context: dict,
    *,
    justify_bead_id: str | None = None,
    override_bead_id: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Evaluate via ctx.rules and raise click.ClickException on BLOCK-class decisions."""
```

### C.1 Required keys in `context: dict`
- `worker_id: str` — invoking worker (None for CLI run by board operator outside session).
- `worker_role: str | None` — worker's role string (looked up if not provided).
- `worker_role_level: int | None` — depth in org chart (CEO=0).
- `env: str` — "prod" | "staging" | "dev". Read from `org/config/env.yaml` or default "dev".
- `args: dict` — flattened click params for the action; key names match click option names.
- `body: str | None` — for actions that ship free text (msgr send, qn-bd create, qn-bd update --notes), the payload body.
- `target_paths: list[str]` — paths the action will read/write/delete; used by `target_path_prefix` scope matching.

### C.2 Decorator wiring — `cli/core/rules/decorators.py`
```python
def requires_rule_check(action: str):
    """Click decorator: invokes evaluate_or_raise before the wrapped function runs.

    Reads --justify and --override flags from click params if present.
    Reads worker context from ctx.obj if running inside a session.
    """
```
Mirrors `requires_permission` from `cli/core/permissions/access_control.py`.

## D. Override mechanism (REQUIRED severity)

### D.1 Worker flow
1. Worker invokes a REQUIRED action without `--override`. Engine returns `REQUIRES_OVERRIDE`.
2. CLI surface prints: `BLOCKED by rule <id>: <description>. To override, file an approval-request bead and re-invoke with --override <bead-id>.`
3. Worker runs: `qn-bd create --type=task --title="Override request: <action>" --notes="<context>" --assignee=<manager_id>`. The bead is now status=open.
4. Manager runs: `qn-bd update <bead-id> --status=approved`.
5. Worker re-invokes original command with `--override <bead-id>`.
6. Engine checks: bead exists, status == "approved", `bead.last_status_changed_by == worker.manager_id` (looked up via org_chart). All three must hold.
7. If valid → `Decision.kind=ALLOW`, audit log records the override usage. If invalid → `Decision.kind=BLOCK` with remediation.

### D.2 Direct-manager resolution
- `cli/core/org_chart.py` already provides org-chart traversal. Add `get_direct_manager(worker_id) -> worker_id | None`.
- "Direct manager" = the worker's parent in the org chart. CEO has no manager; REQUIRED rules cannot be overridden by the CEO except via rules.yaml edit.

### D.3 ENCOURAGED `--justify` flow
- Symmetric to override but lighter: `--justify <bead-id>`.
- Engine checks: bead exists, `bead.owner == worker_id`, `len(bead.body.strip()) > 0`. No status check, no approval needed. The bead IS the artifact.

## E. Audit logging contract — `cli/core/rules/audit.py`

Every `RuleEngine.evaluate()` call produces exactly one log line, written to `org/live/rules-audit.jsonl`:

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-04-29T14:32:01.123Z",
  "worker_id": "wrk-abc123",
  "action": "qn-org.fire",
  "rule_id": "no-fire-without-replacement-plan",
  "decision": "block",
  "decision_detail": "requires_override",
  "justify_bead": null,
  "override_bead": null,
  "context_summary": {"target": "wrk-xyz789", "env": "prod"}
}
```

- One line per evaluation, including no-match cases (rule_id=null, decision="allow").
- File appended atomically (open in 'a' mode, single write per call, no buffering across calls).
- Rotation/retention is out of scope for v0 (operator handles via filesystem).

## F. CLI integration points — 12 surfaces (v0)

Action name format: `<binary>.<command>` for top-level, `<binary>-<group>.<sub>` for nested. Action names are the canonical strings used in `rules.yaml :: rules[].actions`.

| # | Action name             | Decorator target (import path)                                  | Notes                                                       |
|---|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | `qn-org.hire`           | `cli.commands.org.hire:hire_cmd`                                | Adds context: target role, manager_id, team                 |
| 2 | `qn-org.fire`           | `cli.commands.org.fire:fire_cmd`                                | Adds context: target worker_id                              |
| 3 | `qn-org.promote`        | `cli.commands.org.promote:promote_cmd`                          | Adds context: target worker_id, new role                    |
| 4 | `qn-org.demote`         | `cli.commands.org.demote:demote_cmd`                            |                                                             |
| 5 | `qn-org.start-worker`   | `cli.commands.org.start:start_cmd`                              | Only fires if `--worker` flag is set; org-wide start exempt |
| 6 | `qn-org.budget-allocate`| `cli.commands.org.budget:budget_allocate`                       | Adds context: amount, source, target                        |
| 7 | `qn-org.delegate-auth`  | `cli.commands.org.delegate_authority:delegate_authority_cmd`    | Adds context: capability, target                            |
| 8 | `qn-org.okr-set`        | `cli.commands.org.okr.manage` (registered subcommand "set")     | Layers ON TOP OF existing KR validation in op_create_okr    |
| 9 | `qn-org.stop`           | `cli.commands.org.stop:stop_cmd`                                | Includes graceful_timeout context                           |
| 10| `msgr.send`             | `cli.msgr.commands.send:send`                                   | Body=message, args=channel/recipient                        |
| 11| `qn-bd.create`          | `cli.commands.qn_bd:main` (dispatched via wrapper, see §F.1)    | Body=title+description+notes concatenated for pattern match |
| 12| `qn-bd.update`          | `cli.commands.qn_bd:main` (same wrapper)                        | Fires on `--status`, `--assignee`, `--notes` mutating flags |

### F.1 qn-bd wrapper integration
`cli/commands/qn_bd.py:main()` shells out to the `bd` binary. The rule check sits before the shell-out:
1. Parse the args to determine action (create/update/close/etc.) and extract context.
2. Run `evaluate_or_raise` with action `qn-bd.<verb>`.
3. On allow, proceed with shell-out. On block, raise `click.ClickException`.
This means rules-awareness for bd is additive: no change to the bd binary itself.

## G. File layout

New files:
- `cli/core/rules/__init__.py` — re-exports public API.
- `cli/core/rules/types.py` — dataclasses + enums (§B).
- `cli/core/rules/loader.py` — `load_rules(org_path: Path) -> RuleSet`. Reads org/config/rules.yaml, falls back to default-rules.yaml on missing file. Fails closed on parse errors.
- `cli/core/rules/engine.py` — `RuleEngine` class + `evaluate_or_raise` helper (§C).
- `cli/core/rules/decorators.py` — `requires_rule_check(action)` Click decorator (§C.2).
- `cli/core/rules/audit.py` — `AuditLogger` (§E).
- `cli/core/rules/cli.py` — `qn org rules {add, list, disable, test, validate}` subcommands.
- `cli/config/templates/default-rules.yaml` — 14-rule catalog.

Modified files:
- `cli/core/constants/__init__.py` — add `RULES_AUDIT_FILENAME = "rules-audit.jsonl"`, `DEFAULT_RULES_TEMPLATE_PATH = ...`, severity action-name constants.
- `cli/commands/org/__init__.py` — register the `rules` subcommand group.
- `cli/commands/org/hire.py`, `fire.py`, `promote.py`, `demote.py`, `start.py`, `budget.py`, `delegate_authority.py`, `okr/manage.py`, `stop.py` — apply `@requires_rule_check("qn-org.<action>")` decorator.
- `cli/commands/qn_bd.py` — wrap `main()` with rule-check pre-pass.
- `cli/msgr/commands/send.py` — apply decorator.
- `cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2` — render active rules in a new "Active Board Rules" section (per A.4.7 of the epic).
- `shared/exceptions.py` — add `RuleEngineError`, `RuleViolation`.

## H. Performance budget

- `RuleEngine.evaluate()` target: <5ms for ≤50 rules in the ruleset, <20ms for ≤500 rules.
- Pattern matching uses pre-compiled regex (`re.compile` at RuleSet load time, stored on the `Rule` instance via `__post_init__` of a wrapper class — `Pattern` itself is frozen dataclass, but the compiled regex lives on a side-cache keyed by Rule.id).
- AuditLogger writes are synchronous append (no batching) to keep the audit trail correct under crash. Fine for <100 evaluations/sec, which is well above expected human-driven CLI rate.

## I. Backward compatibility

- Orgs that haven't run `qn org init` since this lands have no `rules.yaml`. Loader detects missing file and applies the default catalog (the 14 rules). No silent disablement; operator sees a one-time stderr warning at first rule-aware command: "Using default rules. Run `qn org rules edit` to customize."
- Empty `rules.yaml` with `version: 1` and `rules: []` is valid and disables all rules. Operator's explicit choice.
- Existing canaries 01–10 must still pass with rules wired in. Default catalog is intentionally non-blocking on canary scenarios (verified in Phase-5 validation).

## J. Open implementation choices

These are NOT user-facing decisions — flagged here so Phase 3 (technical strategy bead quinn-ai-p286) resolves them before code lands:
- (1) Decorator vs. inline `evaluate_or_raise()` call: decorator is cleaner but harder to test in isolation. Strategy phase decides.
- (2) Where the AuditLogger instance lives: on Click context (`ctx.obj.rules_audit`) or as a module-level singleton. Probably ctx-bound to keep tests isolated.
- (3) How the briefing template gets the active ruleset: pass via Jinja context at render time (current pattern) vs. read from disk in the template. Pass via context.

title: [BOARD-RULES] Capture user requirements for the rules system
description: Why: before any schema / impl, we need the rule taxonomy and use cases pinned by the operator. Without this Phase-1 step, we'll re-litigate severity semantics during impl. What: produce a 1-page requirements doc (commit to docs/) covering: (a) the four severity levels and exact operational behavior of each — what does ADVISORY 'warn-and-proceed' look like at the CLI? what does ENFORCED 'block-with-override' look like? (b) representative rules at each level (>=3 per level) drawn from the operator's actual concerns; (c) the set of action surfaces rules apply to (CLI commands by name, msgr broadcasts, bd state transitions, arbitrary tool invocations workers run); (d) explicit non-goals for v0 (e.g. live editing without restart? we're saying no); (e) acceptance criteria for the MVP — must answer 'when do we ship?'.
design:
# Board Rules — User Requirements (final)

## 1. Severity levels (v0)

User's vocabulary: SUGGESTED / ENCOURAGED / REQUIRED / ABSOLUTE.

| Level      | Behavior                                                                                                              |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SUGGESTED  | One-line stderr nudge. Proceed silently. No override needed.                                                          |
| ENCOURAGED | Proceed only if worker produces a defensible artifact (scoped report / test results / data). See §1a.                 |
| REQUIRED   | Block until the worker's *direct manager* approves via a linked bead (status=approved, approver=manager_id). See §1b. |
| ABSOLUTE   | Never overridable at runtime. Only path is editing rules.yaml + restarting the org (audited via git).                 |

### §1a — ENCOURAGED artifact substrate
Linked bead the worker files before proceeding; report / test output / data inline in the bead body. CLI: `--justify <bead-id>`. Engine verifies the bead exists, is owned by the worker, and has non-empty body text.

### §1b — REQUIRED override flow
- Worker files an "override request" bead, type=task, status=open, links the rule name and action context.
- Worker's direct manager (per org-chart) sets status=approved.
- Worker re-invokes with `--override <bead-id>`. Engine checks: bead exists AND status=approved AND approver_id == worker.manager_id.
- Direct-line manager is sufficient (NOT board-level). ABSOLUTE is the unoverridable tier.

## 2. Rule scoping
Optional `scope:` field matches against action context (env, target path, worker role/level). If absent, rule applies to all invocations. Lets `no-drop-database` be ABSOLUTE in prod and SUGGESTED in dev sandbox without duplicate rules.

## 3. Initial rule catalog (14 rules)

### SUGGESTED
1. `no-trivial-ceo-dm` — Workers ≥2 levels below CEO should not DM the CEO directly; route through manager.
2. `prefer-bead-over-channel-broadcast` — Task-shaped messages should be filed as beads, not broadcast to #general.
3. `pr-title-prefix` — Commits/PRs touching `cli/core/` should prefix with the module name.

### ENCOURAGED
4. `tests-before-merge` — No merging to main without `pytest cli/tests/` green. Artifact: paste of test output in the override bead.
5. `okr-link-on-features` — New `feature` beads should link to a parent OKR via `serves` dep. Artifact: justification bead if no OKR.
6. `coverage-floor` — Don't drop overall coverage below current baseline. Artifact: coverage diff.

### REQUIRED
7. `no-fire-without-replacement-plan` — `qn org fire <id>` requires manager approval (succession plan).
8. `budget-allocation-cap` — `qn org budget allocate >$X` requires manager approval. (X TBD per scope.)
9. `cross-team-hire` — `qn org hire` where new worker reports to a different team than requester needs manager approval.
10. `okr-set-mid-quarter` — Setting/replacing an OKR after quarter-start requires manager approval.

### ABSOLUTE
11. `no-drop-database` — Any SQL containing `DROP TABLE`, `DROP DATABASE`, `TRUNCATE` is refused.
12. `no-rm-rf-storage` — Any tool call with `rm -rf` targeting a path inside `storage/` is refused.
13. `no-force-push-main` — `git push --force` (or `+main`) targeting the main branch is refused.
14. `no-secret-commit` — Any commit touching `.env`, `*.pem`, files matching credential patterns is refused.

## 4. Action surfaces wired into the engine (v0 = 12 CLI surfaces)

### Lifecycle mutations
1. `qn org hire`
2. `qn org fire`
3. `qn org promote` / `qn org demote`
4. `qn org start --worker <id>` (single-worker spawn; org-wide start is NOT rules-aware)

### Resource mutations
5. `qn org budget allocate`
6. `qn org delegate-authority`
7. `qn org okr set` (additive layer on top of existing KR validation)

### Communication
8. `msgr send` (channel posts and DMs)

### Beads via qn-bd
9. `qn-bd create`
10. `qn-bd update --status=closed`
11. `qn-bd update --assignee=`

### Stop
12. `qn org stop`

### §4a — Out of scope for v0 (deferred to follow-up epic quinn-ai-f0vk)
- Worker-issued shell commands (rm -rf, git push --force, etc.) — needs session-adapter tool-call hooks.
- Worker-issued SQL (DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE) — same reason.
- `qn org start` (org-wide) — board-level action, not subject to engine.
ABSOLUTE rules #11–14 ship in the catalog but only fire when the dangerous content reaches one of the 12 v0 CLI surfaces (e.g. a `qn-bd create` with SQL fragments in the body). Tool-call enforcement lands when quinn-ai-f0vk ships.

## 5. Non-goals (v0)

1. No live rule editing — `rules.yaml` changes require org restart.
2. No tool-call interception — deferred to quinn-ai-f0vk.
3. No org-wide rule federation — each org defines its own rules.yaml.
4. No machine-learnable rule promotion — rules are explicit and human-authored.
5. No conditional-on-recent-history rules — engine evaluates current action context only.
6. No rule chaining or inter-rule dependencies — each rule evaluated independently.
7. No per-worker rule customization — `scope:` filters by role/level, never by worker_id (use org-chart permissions instead).
8. No rule expiry / time-bound rules — operator removes obsolete rules manually.
9. No enforcement on read-only ops (bd list, qn org status, bd show).
10. **Fail-closed on engine errors.** If rules.yaml is malformed or the engine crashes, ALL rule-aware CLI surfaces refuse with a clear error. Operator must fix YAML. Safer than fail-open and simpler than per-severity behavior.

## 6. MVP done when…

1. `qn org rules add | list | disable | test | validate` work end-to-end on the CLI.
2. All 4 severity levels exhibit per-spec behavior under unit tests:
   - SUGGESTED → warns to stderr, proceeds.
   - ENCOURAGED → blocks unless `--justify <bead-id>` references an existing worker-owned non-empty bead.
   - REQUIRED → blocks unless `--override <bead-id>` references an approved bead whose approver_id matches worker's manager_id.
   - ABSOLUTE → blocks unconditionally; no flag bypasses.
3. ≥10 of the 12 v0 CLI surfaces are wired into the rule engine (per Epic A acceptance criterion).
4. The 14-rule catalog ships as `cli/config/templates/default-rules.yaml` (or equivalent), loadable by a new org's `qn org init`.
5. `cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2` renders active rules so workers see them at session start (per A.4.7).
6. Engine fails closed: malformed `rules.yaml` or evaluation error → action refused with a clear error message.
7. Live-LLM canary 11 (quinn-ai-snfq) passes: worker sees rules in briefing, attempts to trigger an ABSOLUTE rule, is refused; attempts to trigger a REQUIRED rule, files an override-request bead, manager approves OR rejects, worker behavior matches.
8. Full pytest suite green, no regressions in canaries 01–10.

When all 8 hold, BOARD-RULES v0 ships and quinn-ai-ob97 closes.
acceptance_criteria: docs/board-rules-requirements.md exists, lists >=12 example rules across all 4 severities, names >=10 CLI command surfaces that must be rules-aware, and has an 'MVP done when' section.
notes: Output should land as docs/board-rules-requirements.md. The other agent's templates work (Epic B) is parallel; rule semantics for hiring will need to consider templates but rules MVP doesn't depend on templates.

Fail-closed across the board on engine errors.

title: [host-mode-init] System Requirements
description:
Translate the host-mode user requirements into technical constraints.

Layout:
- New flag 'qn org init --host' (default off; auto-enable if .beads/ or .git/ exists at --org-path).
- All org metadata namespaces under <project_root>/.quinnai/ (config/, live/, storage/, org-chart/). Project root is otherwise untouched.
- Reuse existing <project_root>/.beads/. Do NOT run 'bd init' in host mode.

Discovery:
- New helper find_org_root(start: Path) that walks up looking for .quinnai/ marker (git-style).
- New 'project_root' column in org_state so qn knows project root distinct from .quinnai/ org-path.

Session spawn (cli/core/sessions/...):
- In host mode: SessionConfig.working_directory = project_root.
- $WORKER_STORAGE env = absolute path to .quinnai/storage/workers/<hierarchy>/.
- $QUINN_WORKER_ID stays as today (already plumbed).

Onboarding (cli/core/onboarding.py):
- In host mode skip rendering of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md to project root. BRIEFING.md, STORAGE.md, WELCOME.md, INITIAL_TASK.md still land in $WORKER_STORAGE.
- BRIEFING.md leads with the project-CLAUDE.md-wins-for-code paragraph.

Backlog handling:
- CEO's first-action template in host mode: survey + msgr ping, NO auto-claim. After 5min idle or explicit direction, claim.

Bead-write trust boundary:
- New .beads/hooks/pre-update script: if $QUINN_WORKER_ID is set and the bead's assignee != $QUINN_WORKER_ID, refuse close/status=closed with a clear error.
- 'qn org init --host' installs this hook (idempotent).

API contract:
- 'qn org init --host' (or auto-detected): non-zero on identity-check fail, conflicting non-host org metadata at .quinnai/, or workers/ dir collision.
- Existing 'qn org init' (greenfield) flow unchanged.

No bd schema changes. Worker IDs continue to live in beads' assignee column alongside human assignees.
notes:
LOCKED 2026-04-29 (reconciled against 1.1).

CLI surface:
- New flag 'qn org init --host' (and --no-host counterpart). Default behavior: auto-detect — if .beads/ or .git/ exists at --org-path, host mode auto-enables and a one-line notice prints ('Host mode: overlay onto existing project at <path>. Use --no-host to force greenfield.'). --no-host forces greenfield even when markers are present.
- 'qn org init' (no flag) in a clean dir continues to greenfield path unchanged.

Directory layout (host mode):
- All org metadata under <project_root>/.quinnai/{config, live, storage, org-chart}/.
- .beads/ stays at <project_root>/.beads/ — project's existing tracker, untouched.
- Project root files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md) are NEVER created or overwritten in host mode.

Discovery:
- New helper cli/core/host_mode.py::find_org_root(start: Path) -> Path | None — walks up from start looking for .quinnai/ marker (git-style). Stops at filesystem root.
- 'qn' subcommands resolve org-path via: explicit --org-path > QUINNAI_ORG_PATH env > find_org_root(cwd).

Schema:
- ALTER TABLE org_state ADD COLUMN project_root TEXT NULL (backward-compat; greenfield orgs leave it null).
- is_host_mode(org_path) := bool(org_state.project_root).

Beads coexistence:
- Host mode does NOT run 'bd init' (project's tracker is authoritative).
- Org OKRs continue to use --type=okr --label=okr; worker tasks continue to use --assignee=<worker-id>. Existing convention; no new conventions invented.
- Add 'bd ready --human-only' filter (excludes worker assignees) — quality-of-life for the human owner. Optional for v1; can defer.
- Identity check: if bd's identity check fails on init, qn surfaces the error verbatim and refuses (don't bypass with BEADS_SKIP_IDENTITY_CHECK).

Session plumbing:
- In host mode: SessionConfig.working_directory = project_root (absolute).
- $WORKER_STORAGE env var = abs path to <project_root>/.quinnai/storage/workers/<hierarchy>/.
- $QUINN_WORKER_ID continues to be set per existing plumbing.
- Audit all four session adapters (claude_code, cursor, codex, gemini) confirm they read SessionConfig.working_directory; verify FakeSpawner mirrors host-mode plumbing for scenario tests.

Onboarding:
- In host mode: skip rendering CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md to project root.
- BRIEFING.md, STORAGE.md, WELCOME.md, INITIAL_TASK.md still land in $WORKER_STORAGE (not cwd).
- briefing.md.jinja2 gets a top-of-Responsibility-section block: '{% if is_host_mode %}You are working in an existing project at $PROJECT_ROOT (your cwd). The project's CLAUDE.md governs code conventions, architecture, and constraints. This BRIEFING.md adds your role-specific layer. When they conflict, project CLAUDE.md wins for code; this BRIEFING.md wins for role behavior.{% endif %}'

CEO first-action template (host mode only):
- INITIAL_TASK.md in host mode renders a survey-first sequence:
  1. bd ready (read-only survey of project's open beads)
  2. bd list --assignee=<known-humans> (who is mid-thought)
  3. msgr send #general '<summary of backlog + standing by>'
  4. Wait for human direction via msgr inbox poll.
  5. If 5min idle (no inbox events, no direct message): claim CEO's own highest-priority OKR (filter: --label=okr --assignee=<ceo-id>). NEVER auto-claim a pre-existing human-assigned bead.

Trust boundary (bead-write isolation):
- Install <project_root>/.beads/hooks/pre-update at qn org init --host time.
- Hook is bash 3.2 compatible (macOS). Reads bead's current assignee. If $QUINN_WORKER_ID is set AND assignee != $QUINN_WORKER_ID AND new status is 'closed', exit non-zero with stderr message 'worker <id> cannot close bead assigned to <other>'. Humans (no $QUINN_WORKER_ID env) bypass the check.
- Hook idempotent on re-init (replace if changed; leave alone if matches expected content).

Out of scope (v1):
- Supervised bead-write approval queue (per-assignee isolation only).
- Multi-project monorepo (single .quinnai/ per project root).
- Migration tool from greenfield to host layout.
- 'bd ready --human-only' filter is OPTIONAL for v1 (nice-to-have).
close_reason: System requirements pinned to 1.1 user reqs. CLI flag, layout, schema, discovery, beads coexistence, session plumbing, onboarding, CEO first-action, trust boundary all defined. Unblocks 2.1 (failing unit tests) and 2.2 (failing integration tests).

title: [EPIC] Board-level rules with graded absoluteness levels
description: Why: the human operator (the 'board') needs to enforce structural constraints on the autonomous org — soft preferences AND absolute prohibitions — without writing bespoke code per constraint. Today every new guardrail (don't push to main without review, never DROP TABLE without sign-off, don't DM the CEO with trivial questions, don't allocate >$X without delegation chain) requires custom logic at the relevant CLI surface; that doesn't scale. What: ship a graded rules system (SOFT/ADVISORY/ENFORCED/ABSOLUTE), a YAML loader, an enforcement engine wired into every mutating CLI command, an override mechanism (board-approved bead), a CLI for runtime rule management, briefing-template integration so workers know which rules are active, and an e2e canary proving the system works under live LLM operation. Acceptance: a board operator can add a rule via 'qn org rules add', it persists across org restart, it blocks (or warns, depending on severity) the right CLI invocations, and workers can see it in their briefing. Done when the e2e canary passes.
acceptance_criteria: (1) qn org rules add/list/disable/test work end-to-end; (2) all 4 severity levels enforce per-spec; (3) at least 5 mutating CLI surfaces are wired into the rule engine; (4) override flow requires a linked bd issue with status=approved AND assignee role contains 'board'; (5) briefing.md.jinja2 lists active rules; (6) e2e canary spec passes a live run.

description:

  - Workers' private storage is isolated under .quinnai/storage/workers/<path>/.

notes:
LOCKED 2026-04-29.

Who: developer with an active project (.git/, .beads/, CLAUDE.md, README.md) who wants to overlay a QuinnAI org without disrupting their existing work.

Done criteria:
- qn org init succeeds in a non-empty project; no greenfield-only refusal.
- All org metadata under <project_root>/.quinnai/. Project root files untouched.
- Project's existing .beads/ is the org's beads. OKRs land there with --label=okr.
- Workers spawn with cwd=project_root, $WORKER_STORAGE=.quinnai/storage/workers/<path>/. They edit project files directly.
- Worker BRIEFING.md instructs project's CLAUDE.md is authoritative for code conventions.
- Worker cannot bd close a bead assigned to a human or another worker (.beads/hooks/pre-update enforces).
- CEO surveys backlog on first action; never auto-claims a pre-existing human bead.

Three open decisions resolved (user signed off 2026-04-29):

Q1: AUTO-DETECT host mode when .beads/ or .git/ exists at --org-path. Print a notice. --no-host opts back to greenfield. Reduces friction.

Q2: CEO surveys, posts to #general summarizing backlog, then auto-claims THEIR HIGHEST-PRIORITY OWN OKR if no human direction within 5min. Never auto-claims a pre-existing human-assigned bead either way.

Q3: Existing greenfield orgs at ~/orgs/<name>/ are LEFT ALONE. New orgs use host mode in projects. Schema migration adds nullable project_root column so old orgs gracefully report is_host_mode=false. No migrate-to-host tool in v1.

Out of scope (v1): supervised bead-write approval queue, monorepo with multiple project roots per org, migrate-to-host tooling.
close_reason: Requirements captured + three open decisions resolved. Q1=auto-detect with notice; Q2=survey-then-auto-claim-own-OKR-after-5min; Q3=leave-existing-greenfield-orgs-alone. See --notes for full text. Unblocks 1.2 (System Requirements).

title: Tmux capture-pane startup race kills session monitor (caught by canary 07)
description:
At session spawn, ClaudeCodeStateMonitor begins polling tmux capture-pane
immediately. If the pane is not yet fully up, capture-pane returns
non-zero. shared/pyterm/tmux_session.py:extract() uses check=True, so
this raises CalledProcessError.

Cascade:
  extract() → CalledProcessError
  monitors/claude_code.py:154 → wraps as StateDetectionError
  _background_monitor_loop → counts toward _consecutive_errors
  after 10 consecutive errors → monitor PERMANENTLY STOPS

Once dead, the org is blind to that worker's state for the rest of the
session. The underlying tmux session is actually alive — send-keys
works, kickstart is received, workers ship deliverables. Only state
observation dies.

Surfaced live by canary 07 cross_functional_launch on 2026-04-28: CEO
Alice (wrkr-890396ab) had her monitor crash at startup. She still hired
4 specialists who shipped 3 of 4 deliverables (impl.py, tests.py,
docs.md). Test ultimately failed on the changelog wait, but the
underlying delegation worked.

Real fix candidates (non-bandaid):
1. pyterm/tmux_session.py:extract() should use check=False and on
   non-zero return, call has-session to discriminate transient pane
   issues (return empty ExtractedOutput) from session-died (raise
   SessionDied or transition state to CRASHED).
2. Add a startup warmup window in ClaudeCodeStateMonitor where the
   first N capture-pane failures don't count toward
   max_consecutive_errors.

Both together would be ideal: robust extract() + warmup tolerance.

Repro:
  set -a; . .envs/.local/.env; set +a
  QUINNAI_RUN_CANARY=1 QUINNAI_CANARY_BUDGET_USD=3.0 \
    QUINNAI_CANARY_BUDGET_SECONDS=900 \
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/canary/test_run_canaries.py \
    -k '07_cross_functional' -v -s 2>&1 | grep 'capture-pane'
notes: Real fix shipped in 8f25551. Failing tests written first (red), implementation, then green. Live canary re-run in progress to verify in production.
close_reason: Real fix verified in production via canary 07 cross_functional_launch. Before fix: 10 consecutive capture-pane errors → monitor stops → 13:57min run failing on missing changelog deliverable. After fix (8f25551): 0 cascade errors, all 4 deliverables shipped, test PASSED in 5:27. Three new tests prove the fix at unit + end-to-end level (test_extract_returns_empty_on_transient_capture_failure, test_extract_marks_session_exited_when_session_gone, test_extract_does_not_trip_state_monitor_consecutive_errors).

title: [BUG] Hired workers don't have a kickstart prompt — they idle in tmux until session dies
description:
