- qn org start delivers INITIAL_TASK.md to the CEO via Phase 5 (tmux send-keys 'cat INITIAL_TASK.md').
- qn org hire (and qn org budget allocate's auto-spawn) does NOT do an equivalent kickstart for hired workers.
- The hired worker's claude session boots, sits at the prompt, and idles indefinitely because nothing tells it to do anything.
- Eventually the session dies and the work is permanently lost.

This makes autonomous delegation unusable: a real CEO assigning beads via msgr expects subordinates to act on them. Today they don't.

Fix:
- spawn_worker_session should write a worker-flavored INITIAL_TASK.md (or reuse the CEO template adapted for non-CEO role) and inject 'cat INITIAL_TASK.md' via tmux send-keys after the pane is ready.
- The prompt should instruct: 'You are <role>. Read your BRIEFING.md, check msgr inbox, run bd ready, claim and complete any P0/P1 beads assigned to you, post status updates to #general, and stop only when no work remains.'
- Same _wait_for_pane_ready + _tmux_send_keys_with_retry helpers used by quinn-ai-k2cy.

Verification path: re-run canary 07 — should produce all 4 deliverables without any kickstart_worker scenario op.

Filed during paid live canary 07 run (~$1.50 spent on the run that found this).
close_reason: Real fix: spawn_worker_session in cli/commands/org/session_utils.py now writes INITIAL_TASK.md per worker and injects 'cat INITIAL_TASK.md' via tmux send-keys after pane readiness. CEOs still get their kickstart via qn org start Phase 5; hired workers now get an equivalent role-aware kickstart. Verified live with canary 07: 5 workers + 4 deliverables shipped in 210s, marketer wrote marketing, engineer wrote code, QA tests pass when actually run.

title: kickstart_worker silently mangles multi-line messages via tmux send-keys
description:
Surfaced live by canary 04 on 2026-04-28.

shared/testing/canary/canary_ops.py:op_kickstart_worker (and op_kickstart_ceo)
deliver scenario directives by calling _tmux_send_keys_with_retry(session,
message). 'tmux send-keys' types each character of the argument literally,
including newlines. Every '\n' in the message is therefore typed as an
Enter key — which on claude_code's TUI submits the partial input and
clears the prompt for the next chunk.

Effect: a message authored as a YAML block scalar ('message: |' ... three
paragraphs ...) reaches claude as ~10 separate submissions of partial
content. claude responds to whatever lands as the first complete-looking
sentence ('Hi Eve.') and discards the rest, which means the actual
directive (run this bash command) never reaches the model.

Surfacing path: canary 04 spent ~5 minutes timing out at
message_count_between(eve→frank) even though all 4 worker tmux sessions
spawned correctly. Eve's pane received '\n'-fragmented input and her
LLM never executed the msgr send.

Fix options:
  (a) In op_kickstart_worker, replace literal newlines with ' ' before
      send-keys — collapses multi-line YAML to a single typed string.
  (b) Build the message into a temp file and have the worker 'cat
      tmpfile' instead of typing it inline. (Heavier.)
  (c) Document the constraint in the canary spec template and validate
      at YAML-load time that no kickstart message contains '\n'. Force
      authors to write single-line directives.

(a) is the least surprising and survives existing single-line specs
unchanged. Worth shipping.

Workaround: I've collapsed canary 04's kickstart messages to single lines
by hand, but the harness should make this safe-by-default.
close_reason:
Fixed by other-agent commit 64f8ff8 (added _flatten_for_send_keys to canary_ops.py). My commit 2d428f5 added 6 regression tests in tests/canary/unit/test_flatten_send_keys.py pinning the contract: 
→space, 
 /  normalization, YAML block-scalar collapse, and no-op short-circuit on 
-free input. Multi-line kickstart messages now arrive as a single prompt submission instead of being shredded into per-line fragments.

title: qn org delegate-authority --level team-lead does not grant can_delegate=True for budget allocation
description:
Surfaced live by canary 04 on 2026-04-28.

Repro:
1. CEO Alice runs:
     qn org delegate-authority --to diana --level team-lead --budget 200 --max-reports 5 --force
2. Command succeeds; Diana shows up with hiring authority and a 200 hiring
   budget.
3. Diana runs:
     qn org hire --name Eve  --role engineer --manager <diana-id> --cost 30
     qn org hire --name Frank --role engineer --manager <diana-id> --cost 30
   Both succeed.
4. Diana then runs:
     qn org budget allocate eve  50
     qn org budget allocate frank 50
   Both FAIL because Diana lacks can_delegate=True. The CEO-default source
   path also fails because Eve/Frank report to Diana, not Alice.

Diana's own diagnosis (verbatim from her live session pane):
  'I don't have can_delegate=True on my budget, so I can't allocate from
  my pool to my reports, and the default allocation (from CEO) fails
  because they report to me, not Alice... I don't see a CLI surface to
  grant budget-delegation authority to myself.'

Why this is a real bug, not a configuration miss:
  --level team-lead is documented as a 'preset authority level' meant for
  managers who run their own teams. Granting hiring authority but NOT the
  budget-delegation flag means a team-lead can hire reports they will
  never be able to fund — a guaranteed dead-end state.

Likely fix: --level team-lead should imply can_delegate=True (or there
should be a --can-delegate CLI flag and the team-lead preset should
default it to True). Worth auditing the director and vp presets too —
same shape of bug likely lurks at higher levels.

Blocked downstream test work: tests/canary/specs/04_hierarchical_team_with_deliverable.yml
cannot reach worker_count=4-with-live-sessions until Diana can fund her
own hires.
close_reason: Fixed in 802b275 (delegate_authority.py calls set_allocation_can_delegate). Pinned in 2d428f5398c8ba935b640cdc41253dc0e2288e37 by new test_delegate_authority_flips_can_delegate_on_existing_allocation that asserts allocation.can_delegate is True after the preset+budget delegation.

title: find_orphaned_tmux_sessions kills sessions from sibling orgs running on the same machine
description:
Bug surfaced by running canary 03 and canary 04 in parallel.

Repro:
1. Start org A (e.g. canary 04 spawns CEO Alice -> qn-wrkr-A).
2. Start org B in a separate tempdir (e.g. canary 03 runs 'qn org start --worker bob').
3. Org B's startup invokes _cleanup_orphaned_sessions(db_B), which calls
   find_orphaned_tmux_sessions(db_B, ...).
4. That function lists ALL tmux sessions whose names start with 'qn-' (the
   global TMUX_SESSION_PREFIX) and marks as orphaned every session whose
   tmux_session_name is not in db_B's session table. qn-wrkr-A IS NOT in
   db_B (different org, different sqlite file) -> classified as orphan ->
   killed with kill_tmux=True.
5. Org A's CEO is now dead; its background state monitor logs 10 consecutive
   capture-pane errors and stops. Whatever Org A was waiting for never
   happens; tests/canaries time out.

Evidence (canary 04 run /tmp/canary04-run.log):
- 17:26:38 my Alice spawned (qn-wrkr-21c36864)
- 17:27:42-17:28:04 sibling canary spawned 3 new workers (qn-wrkr-1ba91257 etc.)
- 'ERROR State detection error: tmux capture-pane returned non-zero exit status 1'
  fires repeatedly for qn-wrkr-21c36864
- 'Stopping monitor after 10 consecutive errors'
- canary fails: 'wait_until timed out: worker_count: expected 2, got 1'

Why this matters:
- Parallel canary runs (CI fan-out, dev running multiple orgs) collide.
- Two orgs in the same tmux server is a legitimate config (each is fully
  isolated by tempdir + db); the cleanup is over-eager.

Proposed fix:
find_orphaned_tmux_sessions should restrict the scan to sessions tied to
THIS org. Two reasonable scopings:
  (a) Compute expected tmux session names from db_B's worker IDs ('qn-{id}'
      for each row in workers) and only consider tmux sessions whose names
      match that set as candidates for orphan classification.
  (b) Tag tmux sessions with the org id at create-time (env or session env
      var) and read it back via 'tmux show-environment' / 'show-options'.

(a) is the smaller change and is robust to future renames. The current code
already filters tmux sessions by TMUX_SESSION_PREFIX -- swap that filter for
'name in {expected for this org}'.
close_reason: Fixed by commit f8a353c (Scope orphan-tmux detection to THIS org's workers only). find_orphaned_tmux_sessions now extracts the wrkr-id from each qn-* tmux session name and filters to only those whose wrkr-id is in the current org's workers table. Sibling orgs running on the same machine (parallel canaries, dev sessions) no longer get murdered by another org's startup cleanup.

title: [BUG] qn org hire spawns worker session without QUINN_WORKER_ID env — msgr fails for hired workers
description:
Surfaced by live Tier 3 multi-worker canary.

Repro:
1. qn org init + qn org start (CEO spawned with env_vars from get_worker_env_vars).
2. CEO runs qn org hire --name Bob — Bob's tmux session spawned via spawn_worker_session.
3. Bob's claude tries: msgr send @<carol> 'hi'
4. Error: 'QUINN_WORKER_ID not set. Are you running in a worker session?'

Root cause: cli/commands/org/hire.py:224 calls spawn_worker_session(worker, provider, command, args_str) WITHOUT env_vars. The session_utils.py default is to pass nothing through, so QUINN_WORKER_ID/QUINN_ORG_PATH/WORKER_STORAGE/etc. are absent for hired workers — only the CEO (spawned by qn org start which DOES call get_worker_env_vars) gets them.

Effect:
- Hired workers can't use msgr (the canonical inter-worker messaging tool).
- qn-bd from a hired worker also breaks (needs QUINN_ORG_PATH).
- Worker can't introspect its own identity.

Fix:
hire.py should call get_worker_env_vars (and prepare_worker_onboarding) before spawn_worker_session and pass env_vars=... through. The same wiring used in org_start_controller for the CEO.

Filed during paid live canary (~$0.30 spent on the run that exposed this).
close_reason: Real fix: msgr (and qn-bd) now resolve worker-id from the surrounding tmux session name (qn-wrkr-XXX) when env propagation fails. qn-bd also recovers org_path from tmux show-environment. Verified end-to-end with paid live LLM run — workers DM each other without --worker-id.

      model: str

title: [T3-LiveCanary] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
Design notes:

- Components live in shared/testing/canary/. Sibling to shared/testing/scenarios/ — both reuse Tier 1 components and Tier 2's AssertionDSL/ScenarioSpec.
- LiveSessionDriver delegates to the existing claude_code provider in cli/providers/. Do NOT duplicate the session spawning code.
- BudgetGuard wraps SessionInterface — use the decorator pattern. Production code never imports it; canary tests do.
- Pricing table lives in shared/testing/canary/pricing.yaml — versioned with the codebase. When Anthropic changes prices, update the file; canary still runs.
- ProviderConfig: dataclass loaded from QUINNAI_CANARY_PROVIDER, QUINNAI_CANARY_MODEL, QUINNAI_CANARY_BUDGET_USD, QUINNAI_CANARY_BUDGET_SECONDS env vars.
- Failure semantics: distinguish 'budget exceeded' (treat as flaky/skip in CI) from 'assertion failed' (treat as real regression).
- Scenarios live in tests/canary/specs/ — sibling to tests/scenarios/specs/. Same YAML format. The DRIVER selection is the only difference.

Risks:
- API key leakage. Mitigation: only inject via GH Actions secret + environment scope; never echo in logs; redact transcripts before upload.
- Flaky LLM responses. Mitigation: assertion DSL must accept tolerant predicates ('any worker named ~bob' rather than exact match) — implemented as Tier 2 predicates; we just compose them.
- Cost runaway. Mitigation: BudgetGuard is mandatory; default $0.50 hard cap; CI warns before $0.20.

Rollback: canary is gated by an env var (QUINNAI_RUN_CANARY=1) and a CI workflow conditional. Flip the conditional off to disable. Code stays.

Output: bd update <id> --design='<strategy>'
design:
STRATEGY

- Reuse Tier 2's ScenarioSpec + AssertionDSL verbatim. Same YAML format.
- New op kinds (start_org, send_to_worker, wait_until) needed for live scenarios — add to a *separate* OPS_CANARY registry that's merged with Tier 2's OPS at canary load time. Tier 2 stays clean.
- BudgetGuard wraps a SessionInterface — uses delegation pattern. Production code never touches it.
- Pricing data lives in pricing.yaml — versioned with code; update when Anthropic prices change.
- LiveSessionDriver is a thin adapter over the existing claude_code provider in cli/providers/. Don't duplicate spawn logic.
- run_canary returns a structured CanaryResult so CI can distinguish failure modes (budget vs assertion vs spawn error).
- Manual gating by env var (QUINNAI_RUN_CANARY=1) prevents accidental $ in normal CI.

Order to make tests pass:
1. provider_config.py (smallest, unblocks test_provider_config.py)
2. budget.py (Pricing + TokenEstimator + BudgetGuard + BudgetExceeded)
3. driver.py (LiveSessionDriver — minimal stub-friendly entrypoint)
4. result.py (CanaryResult dataclass)
5. orchestrator.py (run_canary; reuses Tier 2 harness)
6. __init__.py public API
7. canary-specific ops (start_org/send_to_worker/wait_until) registered

Risks:
- Real claude_code provider import may pull heavy deps. Mitigation: lazy-import inside LiveSessionDriver.spawn.
- Token-cost estimation drift vs actual billing. Acceptable; the canary's budget cap is a safety belt, not a billing oracle.

Rollback: shared/testing/canary/ + tests/canary/ are isolated dirs. rm reverts.
close_reason: Closed

title: [T3-LiveCanary] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Translate user reqs into technical contracts. Three reusable components:

1. LiveSessionDriver
   - Same shape as Tier 2's FakeSpawner-driven harness — implements SessionInterface or wraps the existing claude_code SpawnStrategy.
   - Drives a real qn org init → start → hire flow against the published wheel (so it runs in the smoke-test env, not against repo source).
   - Captures the live transcript for post-mortem.

2. BudgetGuard
   - Wraps any SessionInterface; aborts the run when EITHER:
     a) wall-clock exceeds limit, OR
     b) cumulative API spend (estimated from token counts × per-model pricing table) exceeds limit.
   - Emits a clear failure mode (budget_exceeded vs scenario_failed) so CI can distinguish flakes from regressions.

3. ProviderConfig
   - Loads from env: provider name (claude_code|anthropic|openai), model id, api key env var name, pricing table override.
   - One config per canary run; allows the same scenario YAML to run against different providers without code change.

Reuses from Tier 2: ScenarioSpec YAML format (literally same files), AssertionDSL (same predicates).
Only the SESSION DRIVER swaps — the scenario harness asks for a session, gets a LiveSession instead of a FakeSession.

Test API target: 1 canary scenario in release.yml; runtime 1-5 min; cost <$0.10 typical.

Output: bd update <id> --notes='<contracts>'
notes:
SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

Library: shared/testing/canary/

Components:
1. ProviderConfig (frozen dataclass)
   - provider: 'claude_code' | 'anthropic' | 'openai'

title: [T2-Scenarios] 3.2 Architecture & Interface Design
description:
Module layout:

shared/testing/scenarios/__init__.py        (public API re-exports)
shared/testing/scenarios/harness.py         (ScenarioHarness context manager)
shared/testing/scenarios/spec.py            (ScenarioSpec dataclass + YAML loader)
shared/testing/scenarios/fake_responses.py  (response library + registry)
shared/testing/scenarios/assertions.py      (built-in predicates)
shared/testing/scenarios/ops.py             (op dispatcher: name -> CLI invocation)

tests/scenarios/specs/*.yml                 (scenarios as data)
tests/scenarios/conftest.py                 (pytest_generate_tests for spec discovery)
tests/scenarios/test_run_specs.py           (single test driven by parametrize)
tests/scenarios/unit/test_*.py              (component-level tests)

Public API signatures:

  @dataclass
  class ScenarioSpec:
      name: str
      setup: dict
      ops: list[dict]
      assertions: list[dict]
      @classmethod
      def from_yaml(cls, path: Path) -> 'ScenarioSpec': ...

  class ScenarioHarness:
      def __init__(self, spec: ScenarioSpec, response_library: FakeResponseLibrary | None = None): ...
      def __enter__(self) -> 'ScenarioRun': ...
      def __exit__(self, *exc): ...

  class ScenarioRun:
      org_path: Path
      def run_op(self, op: dict) -> None: ...
      def check(self, assertion: dict) -> Optional[str]: ...

  Op   = Callable[[ScenarioRun, dict], None]
  Pred = Callable[[ScenarioRun, dict], Optional[str]]
  OPS:        dict[str, Op]    # registered op handlers
  PREDICATES: dict[str, Pred]  # registered assertion predicates

Op handler examples:
  'hire'          -> invoke qn org hire via CliRunner
  'fire'          -> invoke qn org fire
  'transition'    -> direct DB write to push lifecycle/runtime state (used by scenarios that don't model the full LLM flow)
  'create_bead'   -> invoke qn-bd create
  'claim_bead'    -> invoke qn-bd update <id> --status=in_progress
  'create_okr'    -> invoke qn org okr create

Output: bd update <id> --design='<architecture>'
design:
ARCHITECTURE

shared/testing/scenarios/__init__.py    re-exports
shared/testing/scenarios/spec.py        ScenarioSpec dataclass + YAML loader + validation
shared/testing/scenarios/harness.py     ScenarioHarness ctx mgr + ScenarioRun
shared/testing/scenarios/ops.py         OPS registry + built-in op handlers
shared/testing/scenarios/predicates.py  PREDICATES registry + built-in assertions
shared/testing/scenarios/db.py          read-only sqlite handle + helpers (find_worker_by_name, get_org_status, etc.)

Op handlers (ops.py):
- init        -> CliRunner.invoke(qn, ['--org-path', path, 'org', 'init', '--ceo-name', ..., '--ceo-role', ..., '--skip-okrs'])
- hire        -> CliRunner.invoke(qn, ['--org-path', path, 'org', 'hire', '--name', ..., '--role', ..., '--manager', ...])
- fire        -> CliRunner.invoke(qn, ['--org-path', path, 'org', 'fire', worker_id, '--reason', ...])
- transition_lifecycle -> direct DB UPDATE (validates new state via Tier 1 TransitionDriver first)
- promote / demote -> CliRunner invocations
- create_okr / assign_kr -> CliRunner invocations
- create_bead / claim_bead -> CliRunner invocations on qn-bd; auto-skip if bd binary absent
- induce_escalation / resolve_escalation -> direct DB UPDATE on escalation table

Predicate handlers (predicates.py):
- org_status      -> SELECT status FROM org
- worker_count    -> SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workers
- worker_lifecycle_is -> JOIN on name; checks lifecycle_status
- manager_subordinates -> recursive query on manager_id
- org_chart_depth -> recursive CTE
- okr_owner / kr_owner -> joins on okr/kr tables
- bead_status_is / bead_assignee -> joins on beads
- escalation_state_is -> joins on escalations table

DB module: caches ScenarioRun.db property as a sqlite3.Connection opened with ?mode=ro on demand.

Scenario lookups: workers indexed by lowercase name; ops resolve 'manager: ceo' to the CEO row's id, etc. id_var feature: an op result can store a generated id (bead id) into a context dict; subsequent ops/assertions reference it as 'bead_var' or '@var'.

title: [T2-Scenarios] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
Design notes:

- Build on FakeSpawner / FakeSession — do not rewrite session abstraction.
- Components live in shared/testing/scenarios/ — same root as Tier 1 but a different subpackage. Both tiers stay testing-only and importable from any test dir.
- Scenarios as YAML loaded with PyYAML (already a runtime dep — no new deps).
- Use the existing CLI commands as the API: import qn click groups and invoke them via CliRunner from click.testing. No subprocess. This gives real DB writes + state transitions without process boundaries.
- AssertionDSL functions take (org_path, db_handle) and return Optional[str]. Reused later in Tier 3 against a real running org.
- Scenarios live in tests/scenarios/specs/*.yml. The harness discovers them automatically; no per-scenario Python required.
- Per-spec pytest parametrize generation: pytest_generate_tests reads specs/ on collection.

Risks:
- Scenarios drift from real CLI behavior if commands change signatures. Mitigation: harness uses the same Click groups production uses; signature drift breaks scenarios immediately.
- Combinatorial scenario growth. Mitigation: keep specs minimal, prefer assertion density over scenario count.
- Fake responses go stale relative to real prompts. Acceptable — Tier 2 is not testing prompts; Tier 3 covers that.

Rollback: scenarios live in tests/scenarios/; deleting reverts.

Output: bd update <id> --design='<strategy>'
design:
STRATEGY

- Use Click's CliRunner to drive 'qn' in-process (proven pattern in cli/tests/test_audit_qn_org_init.py).
- Reuse with_fake_spawner() from cli.tests.harness for spawner replacement.
- Use sqlite3 directly for DB introspection from assertions (read-only via uri='file:...?mode=ro').
- YAML loaded via PyYAML (already a runtime dep).
- Op + predicate handlers are functions in two module-level dicts; adding either = adding a function and registering. No harness changes.
- Scenario validation happens at ScenarioSpec.from_yaml time so unknown ops fail loud at load, not mid-run. Bypass flag _allow_unknown_kinds=True for tests that want to drive ad-hoc ops.

Order to make tests pass:
1. spec.py (unblocks test_spec.py)
2. ops.py + predicates.py (registries with built-ins)
3. harness.py (depends on spec + registries)
4. __init__.py public API
5. wire integration test_run_specs.py — file each scenario bug as separate bead, mark scenario xfail.

Risks:
- Click 'qn' top-level invokes import-time side effects we can't easily mock; CliRunner.invoke handles isolation.
- DB schema may differ from notes (workers table, fields). Read schema by introspection on first connection.
- Some scenarios may surface real bugs in qn org hire/fire/etc. Per user direction: file bugs separately, mark scenario xfail, ship the framework.

Rollback: rm -rf shared/testing/scenarios + tests/scenarios reverts.

title: [T2-Scenarios] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Translate user reqs into technical contracts. Four reusable components:

1. ScenarioHarness — context manager that:
   - creates a tmp org dir + DB
   - swaps the global session registry to FakeSpawner via with_fake_session_registry
   - yields a handle exposing run_op(name, **kwargs) (calls qn CLI internals directly, no subprocess) and assert(predicate)
   - tears down cleanly even on assertion failure

2. ScenarioSpec — pure data:
   spec = {
     'name': 'manager_hires_engineer',
     'setup': { 'ceo': {'name': 'Alice'} },
     'ops': [{'op': 'hire', 'name': 'Bob', 'role': 'Manager', 'manager': 'ceo'}, ...],
     'assertions': [{'kind': 'worker_count', 'value': 3}, ...]
   }

3. FakeResponseLibrary — registry of canned session-output snippets keyed by (worker_role, op_kind). Reusable across scenarios. E.g. an Engineer responding to a get_work prompt returns a deterministic 'I will pick up bead-X' string.

4. AssertionDSL — predicates that read live DB / org state:
   worker_count, worker_lifecycle_is, manager_subordinates, okr_owner, bead_status_is, escalation_state_is, runtime_state_is.
   Pure functions: (org_handle) -> Optional[str].

Test API target: a scenario fits in ~10 lines of YAML. The harness imports ZERO scenario logic.

Performance budget: harness setup <500ms; per op <100ms; full 10-scenario suite <15s.

Output: bd update <id> --notes='<contracts>'
notes:
SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

Library: shared/testing/scenarios/

Reuses: click.testing.CliRunner (already used in cli/tests/test_audit_qn_org_init.py), cli.commands.main.qn (top-level Click group), cli.tests.harness.with_fake_spawner (in-process spawner replacement), shared.testing.state_machines (Tier 1, for state-graph assertions on DB-derived state).

Public API:

1. ScenarioHarness (context manager)
   - __init__(spec: ScenarioSpec)
   - __enter__ -> ScenarioRun
   - swaps spawner via with_fake_spawner() on entry
   - creates tmp org dir
   - tears down both on exit (even on exceptions)

2. ScenarioRun
   - org_path: Path
   - runner: CliRunner
   - run_op(op_dict) -> None — dispatches to OPS registry
   - check(assertion_dict) -> Optional[str] — dispatches to PREDICATES registry
   - db: DBHandle property — opens shared/quinn.db read-only

3. ScenarioSpec (frozen dataclass)
   - name: str, setup: dict, ops: list[dict], assertions: list[dict]
   - classmethod from_yaml(path: Path) -> ScenarioSpec
   - validation in __post_init__: known op kinds, known assertion kinds

4. OPS registry: dict[str, Callable[[ScenarioRun, dict], None]]
   Initial set:
   - 'init': qn org init --skip-okrs
   - 'hire': qn org hire --name --role --manager [--cost --skills]
   - 'fire': qn org fire <id> --reason
   - 'transition_lifecycle': direct DB write to push worker.lifecycle_status
   - 'transition_runtime': direct DB write to push worker.runtime_status
   - 'create_okr': qn org okr create
   - 'create_bead': qn-bd create (skipped if bd not on PATH; auto-skip)

5. PREDICATES registry: dict[str, Callable[[ScenarioRun, dict], Optional[str]]]
   Initial set:
   - 'org_status': checks org.status field
   - 'worker_count': counts workers in DB
   - 'worker_lifecycle_is': worker by name -> lifecycle_status
   - 'manager_subordinates': manager name -> sorted list of subordinate names
   - 'org_chart_depth': max depth from CEO
   - 'okr_owner': okr_id -> assignee
   - 'no_violations': uses Tier 1 cross-machine invariants on DB-derived states

Performance:
- Harness setup <500ms; per op <100ms (CliRunner is in-process); 10-scenario suite <15s.
- Real DB writes (SQLite); no LLM, no subprocess, no tmux.

Coupling:
- shared/testing/scenarios/ MAY import from cli.commands.main (entry), shared.* (DB/models), cli.tests.harness (FakeSpawner).
- Production code (cli/, board_ui/) MUST NOT import from shared/testing/.

YAML format:
  name: ceo_hires_manager
  setup:
    init: { ceo_name: Alice, ceo_role: CEO }
  ops:
    - { op: hire, name: Bob, role: Manager, manager: ceo, cost: 100 }
  assertions:
    - { kind: worker_count, value: 2 }
    - { kind: manager_subordinates, manager: ceo, expected: [bob] }

title: [T1-SM-Seq] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
Design notes:

- Components live in shared/testing/state_machines/ — kept inside shared/ so production code never depends on test infrastructure but tests are co-located with what they verify.
- Pure functions everywhere — no class state where a function suffices.
- Driver is a thin wrapper: store transitions + current; one method 'apply'.
- Runner is reduce(steps, initial_drivers).
- Invariants are functions: (drivers) -> str | None. List comprehension to collect violations.
- Scenarios as @pytest.mark.parametrize lists OR YAML loaded via importlib.resources. Pick one — recommend parametrize for first cut (no YAML parser, no extra deps).
- Reachability check: BFS over transitions dict.

Risks:
- Over-engineering. Reject 'invariant DSL' or 'state machine builder API'. Just dicts + functions.
- Coupling to QuinnAI specifics. Components must accept the dict shape, not a QuinnAI-specific class.

Rollback: tests live in tests/state_sequences/; deleting that dir reverts everything.

Output: bd update <id> --design='<strategy>'
design:
TECHNICAL STRATEGY

Core decisions ratified by the failing tests:
- API surface = 4 modules: driver, runner, invariants, reachability + a re-export __init__.
- Functions over classes wherever possible. Only TransitionDriver is a class (it carries state).
- Step and StepResult are frozen dataclasses for immutability + free __eq__ for test comparisons.
- run_sequence is a free function (not a method on a Runner class) — easier to reuse, no construction overhead.
- Invariants are plain Callables with a closure-captured config — no Invariant class needed.
- Reachability uses BFS from collections.deque; backward reachability is the same algorithm on a reversed adjacency list.

Order to make tests pass:
1. driver.py — unblocks test_driver.py (fastest feedback)
2. runner.py — unblocks test_runner.py
3. reachability.py — unblocks test_reachability.py
4. invariants.py — unblocks test_invariants.py (depends on reachability)
5. __init__.py — re-exports public API (also unblocks the integration test in test_real_sms.py)

Risks:
- Dataclass frozen=True is incompatible with __setattr__ raising AttributeError vs FrozenInstanceError. Both subclass Exception so 'pytest.raises((AttributeError, TypeError))' covers both.
- TransitionDriver.transitions read-only view: use MappingProxyType for the dict and tuples for the lists.

Rollback:

title: [T1-SM-Seq] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Translate user requirements into technical contracts. Three reusable components, each generic over the state-machine dict shape:

1. TransitionDriver(transitions: dict[str, list[str]], initial: str)
   - Stateful walker that holds current state + applies transitions.
   - Methods: apply(target) -> raises if invalid; can_transition(target) -> bool.
   - Pure data; no I/O.

2. SequenceRunner(driver_factory, sequence: list[Step]) -> Result
   - Runs an ordered sequence of (machine, target) steps across one or more drivers.
   - Step shape: { machine: str, action: str | target_state }.
   - Aggregates per-step pass/fail + final state per machine.

3. InvariantChecker(invariants: list[Invariant]) -> list[Violation]
   - An Invariant is a callable (drivers_by_name) -> Optional[str].
   - Built-in invariants: 'every state reaches terminal',
     'no transition references unknown state', 'cross-machine: runtime state requires session_allowed lifecycle'.

Test API target: ~10 lines per scenario in YAML or pytest parametrize.
No deps beyond stdlib + pytest.

Output: bd update <id> --notes='<contracts>'
notes:
SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

Library: shared/testing/state_machines/

Public API contracts:

1. TransitionDriver
   - __init__(transitions: dict[str, list[str]], initial: str)
   - apply(target: str) -> None  | raises InvalidTransition (subclass of ValueError) on bad target
   - can_transition(target: str) -> bool
   - state property (current state)
   - transitions property (read-only frozen view)

2. SequenceRunner (function, not class)
   - run_sequence(drivers: dict[str, TransitionDriver], steps: list[Step]) -> list[StepResult]
   - Step = @dataclass(frozen=True) with .machine: str and .target: str
   - StepResult = @dataclass(frozen=True) with .step, .ok: bool, .from_state, .to_state, .error: str|None
   - Halts on first failed step by default; halt=False keyword to continue collecting violations.

3. InvariantChecker
   - Invariant = Callable[[dict[str, TransitionDriver]], Optional[str]]
   - check(drivers, invariants) -> list[str]  (list of violation messages; empty == clean)
   - Built-in invariants:
       all_states_reachable_from(initial: str) -> Invariant
       no_orphan_terminal_paths() -> Invariant     # every state can reach a terminal
       cross_machine_invariant(name: str, predicate: Callable[[dict[...]], bool], message: str) -> Invariant

4. Reachability helpers
   - reachable_states(transitions, initial) -> set[str]    # BFS forward
   - states_reaching(transitions, target) -> set[str]      # BFS backward
   - terminal_states(transitions) -> set[str]              # states with empty transitions list

Errors:
- InvalidTransition(from_state, target, allowed): clear message, allows test asserting allowed list.
- UnknownState(name): raised when transitions dict references a state not in implicit state set.

Performance:
- All operations O(states + edges); BFS over <100 states is microseconds.
- No I/O, no global state, no module-level side effects.

Test deps: pytest only. No new runtime deps.

Coupling rules:
- This package MUST NOT import from cli, board_ui, or shared.{enums, state_machines}.
- It MAY be imported by tests/state_sequences/ which then composes it with shared.state_machines.

Output: contracts above will be encoded in tests in Phase 2.1.

title: [E2E-VALIDATION] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Translate user requirements into technical constraints.

To capture in --notes:
- Test runner: pytest with the existing tests/e2e/ subprocess-based fixtures (cli_runner, temp_org_dir from conftest.py). NO Click CliRunner — those tests live in cli/tests/.
- Each test gets a fresh tmp_path-rooted org dir; no test reuses or mutates another test's org.
- bd binary: discovered via the same path qn uses (cli/bin/{platform}/bd → system PATH bd → fail). Tests skipped (with a clear marker) if no bd is available.
- Per-test timeout: 60s default, with --timeout=120 on the long full-workflow tests.
- Commands to cover (one happy-path test per command minimum, plus 1-2 error cases each):
    qn org init / status / start / stop / restart  (already covered, may need restart added)
    qn org okr set / add / list / cascade / show / progress / update-kr / link
    qn org hire / fire / promote / demote
    qn wrkr list / show / restart
    qn org provider list / default
    Board intervention (via qn-bd or direct qn calls — board UI not exercised)
- Performance budget: full e2e suite under 5 minutes when run serially.
- CI: add a 'make test-e2e' make target + a github actions step.
- Out of scope: test_smoke_* files stay as they are (don't refactor).
notes:
# System Requirements

## Test invocation
- Use the installed 'qn' binary on PATH (verified: /Users/qosha/Repos/ai/quinn-ai/.venv/bin/qn). The new e2e tests should call 'qn' directly via subprocess, NOT 'python -m cli.commands.main' (the existing smoke tests do the latter — leave them as-is for now). Calling the entry-point script tests one more layer.
- Each test gets a fresh `tmp_path`-rooted org dir. No test reuses or mutates another test's org. Cleanup happens automatically via tmp_path.
- Per-test timeout: 60s default. Decorate the full-lifecycle test with @pytest.mark.timeout(180) — it does init+start+hire+fire+stop sequentially.
- Suite-level: 'pytest tests/e2e/' completes in under 5 minutes serially. No -n auto (bd / dolt are not concurrency-safe under the test fixtures).

## bd binary discovery
- Tests need a real bd. Discovery order matches qn's own (cli/bin/{platform}/bd → `shutil.which('bd')`).
- If neither exists, the entire e2e suite is **skipped** with a clear pytest skip reason. No test errors.
- Decorator: @pytest.mark.skipif(not _bd_available(), reason='bd binary not found') applied via conftest autouse.
- CI: 'make test-e2e' must install bd (brew install bd OR download release binary) before invoking pytest.

## AI provider story (no real LLM during tests)
- No mock provider exists in cli/core/sessions/ (verified — only claude_code, codex, gemini, openai). Adding one is out of scope.
- Strategy:
  * For org lifecycle / OKR / hire-fire / intervention / provider-config tests: use 'qn org start --no-spawn-ceo' so no real session is spawned. Tests cover state-machine and db transitions, not LLM responses.
  * For tests that absolutely need a running session (e.g. wrkr restart with active tmux): mark @pytest.mark.requires_real_session and skip in CI. Out of scope for THIS lifecycle.

## Env hygiene (autouse fixture)
- Strip from subprocess env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, CLAUDE_*, QUINN_ORG_PATH, QUINN_WORKER_ID.
- Restore on teardown — don't permanently modify the test process's env (matters for any python-level imports that read env at module load).

## Tmux state
- Some tests may incidentally create tmux sessions (e.g. if a hire spawns a session). Conftest teardown kills any session whose name starts with 'qn-' to prevent leakage.
- 'qn org stop --force' in fixture teardown handles the explicit case.

## Performance budget
- Budget: 5 min for the full e2e suite.
- Per-test: ~2-15 seconds typical; the full-lifecycle test is the slowest (estimate 30-60s).
- Heavy operations to time-bound: 'qn org init' (~3s, includes git init + bd init), 'qn org start' (~1s with --no-spawn-ceo, ~5s+ otherwise), 'qn org stop' (~5s + graceful timeout).
- If we blow the budget: split into 'fast' and 'slow' marks; CI runs both, dev's 'make test-e2e' runs only 'fast' by default.

## CI integration
- New job in .github/workflows: 'e2e' on Linux + macOS runners.
- Steps: checkout → setup python → install bd (platform-specific) → make setup → make test-e2e.
- Block PRs on green.

## Out of scope (for THIS feature, file separately if needed)
- Mock session provider (would let us test session run without LLM)
- Multi-org parallel scenarios
- Per-option matrix coverage (one happy + 1-2 errors per command)
- 'qn board ui' TUI exercise (deferred via quinn-ai-nb6, needs real TTY)
- 'qn org observe' / 'qn org logs' streaming behavior (just exit-zero coverage)
close_reason: System requirements captured: real qn binary via subprocess, fresh tmp_path orgs, real bd with skip-if-missing, --no-spawn-ceo strategy for non-session tests, env hygiene autouse, 5min suite budget, CI matrix on Linux+macOS. Mock-session provider deferred to a future bead.

title: [E2E-VALIDATION] 1.1 User Requirements
description:
Capture WHO needs the e2e validation suite and WHY, plus acceptance criteria.

Starting context:
- tests/e2e/ already has 31 smoke tests for org init/status/start/stop + 5 full-workflow tests (verified via tests/e2e/COVERAGE.md).
- Gap: OKR commands (set/list/cascade/show/progress/update-kr/link/add), worker commands (hire/fire/promote/demote), session run, board intervention (pause/resume/fire from board → CEO/worker), org stop edge cases not yet covered.
- Existing fixtures (temp_org_dir, cli_runner) in tests/e2e/conftest.py are subprocess-based (no Click CliRunner), which is the right e2e pattern.

To capture in --notes:
- User: developers running 'make test-e2e' before PRs + CI on every push
- Problem: no proof that a fresh user can take qn from 'init' through hire/fire/intervention/stop. Refactors land green and break behavior at the integration boundary.
- Acceptance: a single `pytest tests/e2e/` run exercises every documented qn command at least once against the real qn binary and a real bd binary, in under 5 minutes total.
- Non-goals: testing AI provider responses (those are mocked at the SessionInterface boundary); perf/load testing; multi-org parallel scenarios; the board TUI itself (TUI exercise needs a real TTY — already deferred via quinn-ai-nb6).
notes:
# User Requirements

## Who is the user?
- **Developers** running 'make test-e2e' before opening a PR.
- **CI** running the same target on every push and PR.
- **Future evaluators** who want to confirm a fresh checkout works end-to-end.

## What problem does this solve?
Refactors keep landing green because the existing test suites (cli/tests/, terminal-app/, pyterm/) are unit/integration scoped — they exercise individual modules with mocks at boundaries. Recent work proved this gap: the qms.1, 8tt.*, 4bs.* refactors all passed their suites but each one rebound a public symbol that real CLI invocations would notice. Without an e2e suite, the only place those bind-time mistakes surface is when a human types 'qn'.

tests/e2e/ already has 31 smoke tests for org init/status/start/stop + 5 full-workflow tests (per tests/e2e/COVERAGE.md). They follow the right pattern (subprocess to a real qn binary, real bd, fresh tmp_path org dir, no Click CliRunner). Need to extend that pattern to the rest of the surface.

## Acceptance criteria — when is this done?
1. `make test-e2e` exits 0 on a fresh checkout.
2. Every documented qn command listed below runs at least once against the real qn + real bd + a fresh temp org dir.
3. Total e2e suite runtime under 5 minutes serially.
4. CI workflow has a 'test-e2e' job; PRs are blocked on its green.
5. tests/e2e/COVERAGE.md updated with per-command pass status.
6. No production code changes — only new test files, fixtures, Makefile targets, CI workflow, and docs.

## Command surface to cover (verified via 'qn --help' on this checkout)

### qn org
init, status, start, stop, restart, cleanup, logs, observe, chart, budget,
hire, fire, promote, demote, delegate-authority, revoke-authority, delegations,
okr (subgroup → list, set, add, link, cascade, show, progress, update-kr),
provider (subgroup → list, default)

### qn wrkr
status, get-work, report, restart, cleanup, delegate, search

### qn board
status, alerts, health, pause, resume, fire   (skip 'ui' — TUI needs real TTY)

### qn config
set-provider, validate

That's ~35 commands across 4 groups. Existing smoke tests cover 4 of them. Gap: ~31.

## Non-goals
- AI provider responses: mocked at the SessionInterface boundary. Tests use --no-spawn-ceo or a mock provider where applicable.
- Performance / load testing: separate effort.
- Multi-org parallel scenarios: separate effort.
- 'qn board ui' (TUI): needs interactive TTY. Already deferred via quinn-ai-nb6.
- 'qn org observe' / 'qn org logs': both stream output; e2e covers exit-zero on a stopped session, not log content.
- Exhaustive option-matrix coverage: one happy-path test per command + 1-2 representative error cases. Per-option behavior stays in cli/tests/.

## Constraints discovered while writing this
- 'qn org start --no-spawn-ceo' lets us start a running org without needing a real LLM. Most hire/fire/intervention tests will use this.
- bd availability: tests must skip with a clear marker if no bd binary is found, instead of erroring. CI must install bd before running the suite.
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY etc.: tests must strip these from the subprocess env so a dev's shell keys don't accidentally cause a real API call.
- Worker naming: 'qn org hire --name=X' takes a string name not an id; need to capture the assigned worker-id from output for downstream tests.
close_reason: Requirements captured in --notes. Verified the qn surface via 'qn --help' on this checkout: ~35 commands across 4 groups, existing e2e covers 4. Gap: ~31. Non-goals + constraints documented.

title: Create GitHub Actions release workflow: build + publish to PyPI on v* tag
description:
No publish workflow exists. `.github/CICD_QUICKSTART.md` references `ci.yml` and `validate.yml` that do not exist (only `test-integration.yml` is real).

## Required
New `.github/workflows/release.yml` triggered on `v*` tag push:
1. Run integration tests (reuse existing job)
2. Build bd binaries for 4 platforms via `scripts/build-all-platforms.sh`
3. Build wheel(s)
4. Publish to PyPI via `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` using OIDC trusted publishing (no token needed) — preferred over `PYPI_TOKEN` secret.
5. Create GitHub Release with wheel + bd binaries attached
6. Auto-generate notes from `release-notes/v<version>.md`

## Setup steps
- Reserve `quinnai` on PyPI (verified free 2026-04-27)
- Configure trusted publisher at pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/
- Document required workflow permissions: `id-token: write`, `contents: write`

## Acceptance
Push a `v0.2.1` tag → wheel appears at pypi.org/project/quinnai/0.2.1/ and at github.com/qosha1/quinn-ai/releases/tag/v0.2.1.
close_reason:
Added .github/workflows/release.yml in commit 8f093dd. Triggered on 'v*' tag push:
1. test: pytest on cli/tests/ excluding bd_integration (runners don't have system bd; wrapper unit tests still cover the path).
2. build: verifies tag == VERSION == both pyproject.toml versions, then builds wheels + sdists for quinnai and quinnai-board.
3. publish-pypi: PyPA gh-action-pypi-publish with OIDC trusted publishing, gated on 'pypi' GitHub environment.
4. github-release: attaches dists, uses release-notes/v${ver}.md if present.

YAML validated locally with safe_load; version-match logic dry-run against current VERSION/pyprojects all return MATCH. Trusted-publisher + environment one-time setup is in docs/operations/release-bootstrap.md (1f3).

title: Reconcile package layout: drop or align unused cli/, shared/, terminal-app/ pyproject.toml files
description:
Three sub-pyproject.toml files exist but only the root one is used by the published wheel.

## Verified state
- Root `pyproject.toml` (name=`quinnai`, v0.2.0): `packages=["cli", "shared"]` — this is what builds
- `cli/pyproject.toml` (name=`quinnai-cli`, v0.1.0): `packages=["core","providers","commands","msgr","bin","config"]` — would only work if you `cd cli && build`. Declares `qn-bd` script that root wheel does NOT ship.
- `shared/pyproject.toml` (name=`quinnai-shared`, v0.1.0): `packages=["."]` — same issue
- `terminal-app/pyproject.toml` (name=`quinnai-board`, v0.1.0): standalone, depends on `quinnai`. This one is intentional.

## Decision needed
Either:
(a) **One package** — delete cli/ and shared/ pyproject.toml; keep root + terminal-app. Move `qn-bd` script declaration into root pyproject.
(b) **Three packages** — make root pyproject not ship cli/shared, restructure imports, publish quinnai-cli + quinnai-shared + quinnai-board with quinnai as meta-package depending on all three.

Recommend (a) for simplicity. It matches what already ships.
close_reason: Deleted cli/pyproject.toml and shared/pyproject.toml — neither was built or installed by any tool. requirements-dev.txt now uses '-e .[dev]' + '-e ./terminal-app[dev]'. DEVELOPMENT.md and CICD_QUICKSTART.md updated. Verified post-change: root quinnai wheel builds, terminal-app quinnai-board wheel builds, fresh venv 'pip install -r requirements-dev.txt' produces working qn + qn-board scripts (Py3.14). Commit 2adafb0.

title: Verify clean-room install: pipx install ./dist/quinnai*.whl in empty venv, run qn org init
description:
Before any publishing work, prove the wheel actually works after install.

## Why
We've verified the wheel BUILDS but not that it RUNS post-install. Someone could pip-install it and find that `qn` ImportErrors, can't find bd, can't find configs, etc.

## Acceptance
```bash
python3.11 -m venv /tmp/quinn-test-env
/tmp/quinn-test-env/bin/pip install ./dist/quinnai-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl
/tmp/quinn-test-env/bin/qn --version
/tmp/quinn-test-env/bin/qn org init --org-path /tmp/test-org
/tmp/quinn-test-env/bin/qn org status --org-path /tmp/test-org
```
Each must exit 0. Failures get filed as separate bugs blocking the epic.
close_reason:
Verified via clean-room install of fresh wheel into Py3.14 venv. Surfaced 3 issues:
1. jinja2 missing from runtime deps — FIXED (commit f728048).
2. qn-bd console script not installed — already tracked as quinn-ai-hnv.
3. qn board ui error message references dev install path — filed as quinn-ai-xsv.

title: [HARNESS L1.1] Acceptance: define FakeSpawner contract
description:
Capture what the FakeSpawner must support to make the deferred bead tests possible. Output as bead notes.

Required behaviors (from deferred-bead reading):
1. Implement SpawnStrategy ABC: spawn(SpawnerConfig)→SpawnResult, terminate(session_id), is_alive(session_id), get_status(session_id)
2. Record every spawn call (config, timestamp) so tests can assert on them
3. Default fake state: RUNNING immediately after spawn (no async startup delay)
4. Programmable state: tests can mark a session crashed/idle/stopped to drive state-machine paths
5. Send-input recording: capture any 'send_keys' / 'send_input' calls so tests can assert on the kickstart prompt
6. Graceful termination: terminate() flips state to STOPPED but keeps record
7. No global state leak: each test gets a fresh fake (or reset hook)

Also enumerate which audit beads will benefit (qn org start phases 3-6, qn org hire full bind, qn org fire transitions, qn board pause/resume/fire, qn wrkr restart).
close_reason:
Acceptance contract finalized.

FakeSpawner must implement SpawnStrategy ABC (cli/core/sessions/spawner.py:77):
- name: str (property) — returns 'fake'
- spawn(SpawnerConfig) → SpawnResult: assigns deterministic session_id (e.g. 'fake-{counter}'), records call, default state RUNNING
- stop(session_id, force=False) → bool: flips state to STOPPED; returns True if known, False otherwise
- is_alive(session_id) → bool: True iff state in {RUNNING, IDLE}
- send_input(session_id, text) → bool: records the call; returns True if alive
- read_output(session_id, timeout_ms=None) → str: returns the per-session output buffer (writable by tests)
- attach / send_signal: default ABC behavior is fine

Beyond ABC, the harness exposes test-only controls:
- spawned: list[SpawnerConfig] — every config passed to spawn()
- inputs: list[tuple[session_id, text]] — every send_input call
- stops: list[tuple[session_id, force]] — every stop call
- set_state(session_id, state) — flip a session to RUNNING/IDLE/CRASHED/STOPPED
- set_output(session_id, text) — preload what read_output returns
- reset() — clear everything (or rely on per-test instances)

Integration: registered via SpawnerFactory.register(FakeSpawner('fake')); tests get default factory via get_default_factory() (cli/core/sessions/spawner_factory.py) and replace/restore.

title: qn org init crashes with opaque AttributeError when --org-path is unset
description:
qn --org-path /tmp/foo org init works, but invoking 'qn org init' without --org-path or QUINN_ORG_PATH set crashes with: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'name' at cli/commands/org/init.py:164 (line: name=org_path.name).

The qn group's --org-path help text says it 'auto-detects from current directory' — but for init that auto-detection clearly does not happen (the org doesn't exist yet to be discovered). Either (a) default org_path to Path.cwd() when not provided, or (b) raise click.ClickException with a clear message: 'qn org init requires --org-path or QUINN_ORG_PATH; the org does not yet exist so it cannot be auto-discovered.'

Repro: in any directory not containing live/quinn.db, run 'qn org init --skip-okrs'.

title: qn CLI broken: cli/ has unprefixed imports after major refactor
description:
After commit 35a80cc 'major refactor', files in cli/ use unprefixed imports that fail when qn is invoked from the installed entry point.

Repro:
  .venv/bin/qn --help

Output:
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'commands'
  (originating in cli/commands/main.py → cli/commands/config.py:13: 'from commands.context import pass_context, Context')

Other broken imports observed:
  cli/core/db/__init__.py:17  → 'from core.constants import DB_SCHEMA_VERSION, DEFAULT_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS'
  cli/commands/config.py:14   → 'from core.config import ...'
  cli/commands/config.py:23   → 'from providers.base import ...'
  cli/commands/config.py:63   → 'from providers import get_anthropic_provider'
  cli/commands/config.py:75   → 'from providers import get_openai_provider'

These should be 'from cli.commands.', 'from cli.core.', 'from cli.providers.' respectively.

Impact: 115 of 1153 collectable tests fail at HEAD; 76 of cli/tests/* fail to even collect. qn CLI cannot start.

Out of scope of B2B cleanup (filed during quinn-ai-pl4 / Phase 5.1 baseline comparison) but blocks any meaningful CLI work until fixed. Suggested fix: search/replace unprefixed imports in cli/ with cli.-prefixed equivalents and re-run pytest --collect-only to confirm.
notes:
Fixed via mechanical perl rewrite:
  find cli -name "*.py" -type f -print0 | xargs -0 perl -i -pe \
    's/^(\s*)(from|import) (commands|core|providers|msgr)\./$1$2 cli.$3./'

Result: 146 files edited, 895 unprefixed imports → cli.-prefixed imports.

Verification:
  .venv/bin/qn --help → works (full help text rendered)
  .venv/bin/pytest --collect-only → 3758 tests collected, 0 errors (was 1282 / 76 errors)
  .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_no_b2b_residue.py tests/test_no_b2b_imports.py → 31 passed

title: [B2B-CLEANUP] Technical Strategy
description: Decide order: (1) verify nothing in cli/shared imports B2B code; (2) delete backend/ app/ landing/ e2e/ compose/ docker-compose.*.yml; (3) delete root MD docs DEPLOYMENT/DOCKER; (4) prune Makefile template-* targets; (5) delete openspec/changes/add-{b2b set}; (6) delete tests for removed modules; (7) clean CHANGELOG, release-notes/TEMPLATE.md, scripts/bump-version.sh; (8) sync VERSION and pyproject.toml. Rollback: single PR, revertable via git.
design:
EXECUTION ORDER (single PR, atomic but stepwise commits):

Step A — Pure deletions (no logic risk):
  rm -rf backend/ app/ landing/ e2e/ compose/ .envs/ openspec/changes/
  rm -f docker-compose.local.yml docker-compose.production.yml DEPLOYMENT.md DOCKER.md
  rm -f release-notes/TEMPLATE.md

  rm -f scripts/verify-setup.sh

Step B — Code edits (small surface):
  cli/commands/config.py:231     → drop the ".envs/.local/.django" help echo
  shared/__init__.py:5            → remove "backend" word from docstring

Step C — Script edits:
  scripts/setup-dev.sh           → remove .envs setup block (lines ~50-90)
  scripts/run-board.sh           → drop env-file load
  scripts/run-qn.sh              → drop env-file load
  scripts/bump-version.sh        → swap b2b-saas-template URL for qosha1/quinn-ai

Step D — Doc edits:
  README.md:514-516              → remove backend/, app/, landing/ from structure
  CONTRIBUTING.md                → drop .envs setup steps; drop backend/pyproject.toml ref
  DEVELOPMENT.md:5               → revise monorepo claim

Step E — Config edits:
  Makefile                        → drop template-fetch/diff/merge/cherry blocks
  CHANGELOG.md                    → strike B2B 0.1.0 entry; add 0.2.0 cleanup entry
  pyproject.toml                  → version 0.1.0 → 0.2.0

Step F — Validate:
  .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_no_b2b_residue.py tests/test_no_b2b_imports.py -v
  Expect: all green.
  Then: full pytest suite to catch regressions.

ORDER MATTERS:
- Steps A→E first; F last.
- Within A, openspec/changes/ must go last because pre-commit hooks (if re-enabled) might trip on stale openspec state.
- B before A would orphan code that imports from deleted dirs (none currently, but defensive).

RISKS & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: hidden import we missed in cross-ref scan. Mitigation: run full pytest after Step E; rollback step is a single git revert.
- Risk: the ".envs" example files might be sourced at runtime by a CI workflow. Mitigation: confirmed .github/workflows/test-integration.yml has zero refs to .envs/, backend/, compose/.
- Risk: bd init created a commit ahead of origin. Mitigation: separate concern from this cleanup; flag to user but do not amend.
- Risk: scripts referenced from someone's workflow. Mitigation: scripts/ is local tooling, not user-facing CLI.

ROLLBACK:
- Single PR, single squash. `git revert <merge-sha>` restores everything.
- Pre-cleanup state available at commit 35a80cc (last commit before bd init).

WHAT WE WON'T DO:
- Won't rewrite CLAUDE.md — reality moves to match it.
- Won't refactor cli/ or shared/ beyond the 2 surgical edits.
- Won't auto-format the whole repo (out of scope).

title: [B2B-CLEANUP] User Requirements
description: Capture user requirements for B2B SaaS template removal. CLAUDE.md says QuinnAI is a Python CLI tool, but repo contains Django backend, NextJS app, NextJS landing, Playwright e2e, Docker compose. Acceptance: repo matches CLAUDE.md identity, no dangling refs, tests pass. Non-goals: no new features, no CLI behavior changes.
notes:
WHO: QuinnAI maintainers (single-developer project, Quinn driving). No external users yet.

PROBLEM:
- The repo identity declared in CLAUDE.md (Python CLI tool for AI org orchestration) does not match the on-disk repo, which still contains a full B2B SaaS template (Django backend/, NextJS app/, NextJS landing/, Playwright e2e/, Docker compose, Stripe billing, multi-tenant auth/teams/users).
- Confirmed by reality check: CHANGELOG calls v0.1.0 "B2B SaaS template", openspec/changes/ contains add-{auth-teams,backend-django-core,billing-stripe,frontend-app,landing-page,docker-infrastructure}, Makefile has template-fetch/diff/merge/cherry targets pointing at https://github.com/qosha1/b2b-saas-template.git.
- Drift confuses contributors and (more importantly) Claude itself - CLAUDE.md instructs agents to ignore parts of the repo that are present.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Repo top-level matches CLAUDE.md "Project Structure": cli/, shared/, terminal-app/, tests/, example_orgs/, docs/, openspec/cli-* + scripts/ + standard root files.
2. No backend/, app/, landing/, e2e/ (root), compose/, docker-compose.*.yml, DEPLOYMENT.md, DOCKER.md.
3. No Makefile template-* targets.
4. No openspec/changes/add-{auth-teams,backend-django-core,billing-stripe,frontend-app,landing-page,docker-infrastructure}.
5. No tests/test_{auth_teams,backend,billing,frontend_app,landing_page,infrastructure}.py.
6. CHANGELOG, release-notes/TEMPLATE.md, scripts/bump-version.sh contain no B2B-template-sync references.
7. VERSION matches pyproject.toml [project].version (currently 0.2.0 vs 0.1.0).
8. New verification test (tests/test_no_b2b_residue.py) passes.
9. No cli/ or shared/ imports break after deletion.
10. Existing CLI tests still pass (or are not regressed by this change).

NON-GOALS:
- No new CLI features.
- No CLI behavior changes.
- No refactor of cli/ or shared/ beyond what's needed to remove broken refs.
- Not rewriting CLAUDE.md (just letting reality match what it already says).
- Not addressing any pre-existing test failures unrelated to B2B residue.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Single bundled change is acceptable - this is one logical cleanup, splitting it would be churn.
- Must be revertable via single `git revert` if needed.
- No push without explicit ask.
close_reason: Requirements captured in notes - 10 acceptance criteria, 5 non-goals, scope bounded to deletion + version sync, no behavior changes

title: bd pre-commit hook calls removed 'bd sync --flush-only' — blocks all commits
description: The bd-generated .git/hooks/pre-commit hard-exits 1 when 'bd sync --flush-only' fails. bd >=0.43 removed the 'sync' subcommand in favor of 'bd export' (+ Dolt backend), so the hook fails on every commit once there are pending bead changes. Locally patched the hook to try 'bd sync --flush-only' then fall back to 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' and warn-not-fail (beads are authoritative in Dolt). Root-cause fix belongs in whatever installs/generates the hook (bd setup / scaffolding.init_beads) so fresh clones get the working version.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh 'bd setup'/org init installs a pre-commit hook that flushes via the current bd command and never hard-fails a code commit.

title: test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py is stale post-quinn-ai-6odb (3 failing tests)
description:
## Problem
`cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py` has 3 always-failing tests on main:

- test_bootstrap_okr_appears_in_beads_view
- test_bootstrap_okr_id_matches_between_stores
- test_bootstrap_okr_id_format_is_bead_style

All three assume `qn org init --skip-okrs` plants a bootstrap OKR titled 'Establish organizational foundation'. That assumption is no longer valid.

## Root cause
Two closed beads encode contradictory behaviour:

- **quinn-ai-lxp** (closed 2026-04-26): bootstrap OKR MUST appear in beads when `qn org init --skip-okrs` runs. Added these tests as the regression guard.
- **quinn-ai-6odb** (closed 2026-04-29): `qn org init --skip-okrs` MUST plant zero OKRs (including the bootstrap fallback) because the bootstrap was derailing canaries.

The 6odb fix landed via `OrgInitConfig.skip_okrs` gating both `create_initial_okrs` AND `create_initial_tasks` in `cli/core/org_init/init.py`. That correctly suppresses the bootstrap — but the lxp regression tests weren't updated/deleted, so they now fail.

## Failure mode
Running `pytest cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py` on a clean main:

    test_bootstrap_okr_appears_in_beads_view: 'No OKRs found.' has no 'Establish'
    test_bootstrap_okr_id_matches_between_stores: TypeError unpacking None (no row in okrs table)
    test_bootstrap_okr_id_format_is_bead_style: TypeError unpacking None

## Fix
Either:
1. **Delete the file** — the behaviour it guards against (bootstrap OKR appearing) is now considered a bug, not a feature.
2. **Rewrite to test the inverse** — `--skip-okrs` produces zero OKRs (the 6odb invariant). But `test_org_init_skip_okrs_plants_no_okrs_at_all` already covers that; this file would be redundant.

Recommend option 1 (delete). Document in commit that the lxp invariant was superseded by 6odb.

## Discovered while
Running broader test suite to validate the run_bd dolt fix (quinn-ai-k9ff) didn't regress anything.
close_reason: Deleted cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py. The behaviour it guarded against (bootstrap OKR appearing on --skip-okrs) is now considered a bug, not a feature — superseded by quinn-ai-6odb's invariant that --skip-okrs plants zero OKRs (already covered by test_org_init_skip_okrs_plants_no_okrs_at_all).

title: Board UI health: no_okrs warning fires on workers when parent OKR uses --assignee <name> not <worker_id>
description:
## Problem
`bd create --assignee Cleo` stores assignee as the literal string 'Cleo'. The board health check appears to look up OKRs by worker_id (e.g. `wrkr-e47c8976`) and finds none, so it reports 'no_okrs' for Cleo even though she IS the OKR's assignee.

Re-running `bd update <okr-id> --assignee wrkr-e47c8976` doesn't clear the warning either (need to confirm — the board may also be reading from a stale mirror).

## Repro
1. Create OKR with `bd create ... --assignee <worker-name>`
2. Run `qn board health` → 'no_okrs' warning for that worker

## Suggested fix
Either:
- Health check resolves names ↔ ids before comparing assignee, OR
- bd should reject a non-id assignee with a clear error and force callers to pass worker_id, OR
- qn org okr set should always normalize assignee to worker_id before bd create

## Impact
False-positive warnings train operators to ignore health output. Discovered in ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise.
close_reason:
Fixed in cli/commands/org/okr/_helpers.py:_create_okr.

Resolved the owner name → worker_id BEFORE constructing 'bd create --assignee', not just for the SQLite mirror. Previously bd stored '--assignee Cleo' (literal name) while downstream queries (board health check, bd list --assignee, etc.) passed worker_id and got no match.

Falls through to the raw owner string only if resolution fails, preserving existing behaviour for unrecognised owners.

Tests: new TestOkrSetResolvesOwnerToWorkerId test in cli/tests/test_okr_command.py asserts the resolved value (wrkr-...) appears in bd args, not the literal name. All 49 okr_command tests pass.

Closing despite open umbrella nu51 — uk9v's specific narrow fix is independent of the broader board sync audit.

title: quinn-ai .beads identity mismatch: metadata.json project_id != db _project_id
description:
## Problem
This repo's .beads/ has a project_id mismatch:

    metadata.json project_id: 9f1ff2f7-f01a-4036-8542-528e9e0f6fee
    database _project_id:     94544b16-6d83-4f8f-ba80-bdfa2f1cb99a

bd 1.0.2 refuses writes (any `bd create`/`bd update`/`bd close`) without `BEADS_SKIP_IDENTITY_CHECK=1`. Reads (`bd list`, `bd ready`, `bd show`, `bd context`) work.

bd's own diagnostic suggests: 'BEADS_DIR points to different project / Dolt endpoint changed / metadata.json was copied from another project.' Most likely cause here is the latter — possibly a merge or branch-switch overwrote one but not the other.

## Repro
- cd /Users/qosha/Repos/ai/quinn-ai
- bd create --title test --type task
- → workspace identity mismatch error

## Impact
Workflow assumes bd writes from the repo work normally. Every `bd close`/`bd update` from agents currently fails. Override env var unblocks individual commands but is not a fix.

## Investigation needed
- Is the metadata.json or the dolt db the authoritative one for this repo's history?
- Pull latest dolt + main; check if a recent commit touched metadata.json.
- Decide: rewrite metadata.json to match db, or vice versa.

## Discovered while
Trying to file a bug against quinn-ai during ~/orgs/debugg-fundraise setup.
close_reason: fixed: updated .beads/metadata.json project_id to match dolt db's _project_id (94544b16-6d83-4f8f-ba80-bdfa2f1cb99a). The committed metadata.json from initial 'bd init' (commit 2405381) was stale relative to the current dolt db, likely after the db was reseeded post-init. Verified writes now work without BEADS_SKIP_IDENTITY_CHECK.

title: [BOARD-RULES+TPL] Extend canary_ops + predicates for canaries 11 and 12
description: Why: canaries 11 (board-rules-blocks-action) and 12 (template-driven-hiring) are written but cannot RUN until tests/canary/canary_ops.py + shared/testing/scenarios/predicates.py learn new vocabulary. The Phase-2-P2 subagent flagged each invention as a TODO comment at the top of each canary YAML. Phase 5 acceptance for both epics depends on this vocabulary landing first. What: extend the existing canary_ops + predicates modules with: (1) op rules_yaml_seed — write rules.yaml content to <org>/config/ before init; (2) op templates_yaml_seed — write templates.yaml content to <org>/config/ before init; (3) predicate audit_log_contains — assert <org>/live/rules-audit.jsonl has a JSONL line matching a subset dict (rule_id / decision / action); (4) predicate bead_does_not_exist — inverse of bead_status_is; asserts no bead matches a title substring; (5) predicate team_count — count rows in teams table (supports value: or min:); (6) predicate channel_exists — true iff a channel with the given name exists; (7) predicate team_parent_is — assert teams.parent_team_id of <child> resolves to team_id of <parent>.
acceptance_criteria: all 7 new ops/predicates land in canary_ops.py / predicates.py with type hints + tests; canaries 11 and 12 yaml-validate AND parse cleanly through the canary driver (dry-run mode without QUINNAI_RUN_CANARY=1) without unknown-vocabulary errors; the dry-run pass surfaces a planner-friendly summary of ops without actually invoking the live LLM.
notes:
Added 2 ops + 5 predicates for canaries 11/12.

Ops (shared/testing/canary/canary_ops.py):
  - rules_yaml_seed: writes <org>/config/rules.yaml
  - templates_yaml_seed: writes <org>/config/templates.yaml

Predicates (shared/testing/scenarios/predicates.py):
  - audit_log_contains: subset-match against rules-audit.jsonl
  - bead_does_not_exist: inverse of bead_status_is via bd list --json
  - team_count: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM teams (value: or min:)
  - channel_exists: SELECT 1 FROM channels WHERE name=?
  - team_parent_is: looks up child + parent by name in teams, asserts parent_team_id

Tests: tests/scenarios/unit/test_canary_vocabulary.py — 24 tests, all pass.
Full unit suite (tests/scenarios/unit/): 42/42 pass.
Canary unit suite (tests/canary/unit/): 21/21 pass.

Strict registry-checking validation (ScenarioSpec.from_yaml) of both canary
specs now passes:
  11_board_rules_blocks_action.yml: 4 ops, 3 assertions  OK
  12_template_driven_hiring.yml: 5 ops, 5 assertions  OK

Decisions:
  - Ops in canary_ops.py (LIVE-tier seed); predicates in predicates.py (DB/FS
    reads work for both Tier 2 + Tier 3) — matches bead spec layout.
  - audit_log_contains accepts both terse top-level form ({rule_id:..., decision:...})
    and explicit {match: {...}} form; min: defaults to 1.
  - team_count requires at least one of value/min; rejects empty arg with a
    descriptive violation rather than treating as no-op.
  - bead_does_not_exist returns None (skip) when bd is unavailable, matching
    the established pattern of bead_status_is/bead_assignee.
close_reason: Landed 2 ops (rules_yaml_seed, templates_yaml_seed) + 5 predicates (audit_log_contains, bead_does_not_exist, team_count, channel_exists, team_parent_is) with 24 unit tests in tests/scenarios/unit/test_canary_vocabulary.py. Both canary YAMLs (11, 12) now pass ScenarioSpec.from_yaml strict validation.

title: [host-mode] CEO INITIAL_TASK.md survey-then-claim variant
description:
Follow-up to host-mode-init (closed in quinn-ai-5qr9 et al.).

In host mode the CEO inherits the project's existing backlog. The
locked user requirements (quinn-ai-llvh) said the CEO must survey
first and never auto-claim a pre-existing human bead. The current
INITIAL_TASK.md template is the same in both modes — no survey-first
sequence — so the host-mode behavior depends on the CEO interpreting
the OKR text correctly rather than the template enforcing it.

Add a host-mode variant of INITIAL_TASK.md that renders something like:

  1. Run 'bd ready' to survey what's already open in this project.
  2. Run 'bd list --assignee=<known-humans>' to see who's mid-thought.
  3. Post a summary to #general: 'Here's what I see in the backlog.
     Standing by for direction or will start with my own OKR.'
  4. Watch msgr inbox.
  5. If 5 minutes pass with no inbox activity, claim YOUR highest-
     priority OKR (filter --label=okr --assignee=<your-id>) — NEVER
     a pre-existing human-assigned bead.

Mechanism: thread is_host_mode + project_root through the INITIAL_TASK
render path (likely cli/core/org_start_controller.py:_send_initial_prompt_to_ceo
or wherever the template renders). Add a {% if is_host_mode %} block
in the template.

Why deferred: the bd shim already prevents workers from closing
human-assigned beads (the destructive action). The survey-first ritual
is good org hygiene but not load-bearing for safety. Real hosts using
the v1 will get a working overlay; this refines first-action UX.
close_reason: Host-mode CEO gets _INITIAL_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_HOST_MODE: survey-first (bd ready, identify owners, post to #general), then waits for direction before claiming any beads.

title: [FIX] BRIEFING.md: add 'every N min check msgr inbox + must-reply to every DM with a Q' for ALL workers
description:
Concrete fix derived from quinn-ai-srwt + quinn-ai-szn2 evidence (StartSimpli canary 2026-04-29). Filed as its own bead so it's claimable independent of the discovery beads.

Problem (recap):
  - Workers (CEO + engineers) don't autonomously poll msgr inbox; turn ends after their last action.
  - When nudged to read inbox, the CEO sometimes summarizes-but-doesn't-reply, leaving DM questions unanswered.
  - Engineers sometimes treat clear directives ('please pick up X') as suggestions needing confirmation.
  - Net effect: a 3-worker org needs ~3 manual nudges per orchestration cycle to keep moving.

Concrete fix — update cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2 to add a new section near the existing 'AUTONOMOUS OPERATION MODE' / 'Team Communication' content, applicable to every worker (not just CEO/manager branches):

  ## Inbox discipline (REQUIRED)

  Treat msgr inbox as a continuous polling queue, not a passive notification. After every action — finishing a task, hitting a wait state, replying to a DM — your next action MUST be:

      msgr inbox

  If the inbox shows messages with QUESTIONS or DIRECTIVES:
    - Answer EVERY question. 'No reply' is not a valid response.
    - Execute every directive ('please pick up X', 'take on Y', 'switch to Z') immediately. Don't reply with 'Want me to proceed?' — confirmation questions belong to ambiguous scope, not to clear assignments.
    - For ambiguity-resolution Qs ONLY, ask back with the specific decision you need, then keep working on what's already clear.

  Repeat the inbox check every 5 minutes during long tasks. The org's throughput depends on you closing inbox loops, not on your manager re-prompting you.

Implementation:
  1. Edit cli/config/templates/briefing.md.jinja2 — add the section above, applies to every branch (CEO / is_manager / regular worker).
  2. Add a regression test in tests/e2e/test_smoke_org_start.py that asserts BRIEFING.md after spawn contains the phrase 'msgr inbox' as a required action AND the phrase 'silence is not a valid response' or equivalent.
  3. Optional second-tier: add an INITIAL_TASK.md addendum reinforcing the same rule for the FIRST 5 minutes (most-likely stall window).
  4. Re-run a StartSimpli-style canary to verify a 3-worker org keeps moving without manual nudges.

Acceptance:
  - In a fresh canary, the org runs for 30+ min without external tmux send-keys nudges.
  - All DMs with questions get answered within ~5 min.
  - Engineers execute directive DMs immediately; no 'Want me to proceed?' patterns.

Source evidence: quinn-ai-srwt (round-by-round observations) + quinn-ai-szn2 (specific case).
close_reason: Shipped in 9a6ef7080834de44ee0de691c0a82b7dc2343eb9: briefing.md.jinja2 inbox-discipline section + INITIAL_TASK template strengthening + e2e regression test. Will re-canary on a fresh StartSimpli org to verify cascading-stall is resolved.

title: [EPIC] Session-tool guardrails: rule engine fires on worker tool calls
description: Why: the v0 board-rules system (epic quinn-ai-ob97) intentionally only fires on qn CLI surfaces. ABSOLUTE rules like no-rm-rf-storage, no-drop-database, no-force-push-main can be 'escaped' today by a worker invoking the dangerous command directly via their session's Bash tool — bypassing every CLI guardrail. That's a real safety hole. What: extend the SessionInterface contract with a pre-tool-call hook that pre-evaluates tool calls (Bash command strings, Edit targets, SQL queries) against the rule engine, blocking before the underlying tool runs. Each provider adapter (ClaudeCodeSession, CursorSession, …) implements the hook against its provider's tool-use protocol. Acceptance: a worker session running under any registered provider cannot rm -rf storage, cannot DROP TABLE, cannot git push --force main, even when invoking the underlying command directly. Live-LLM canary proves it.
acceptance_criteria: (1) SessionInterface gains pre_tool_call(action, ctx) -> Decision hook; (2) >=2 provider adapters implement it (claude_code minimum, cursor if reachable); (3) ABSOLUTE rules 11-14 from BOARD-RULES catalog fire on direct tool invocations not just CLI; (4) live-LLM canary spec: worker explicitly attempts rm -rf storage and is refused at the tool layer; (5) no false positives on legitimate worker tool use in canaries 01-12.
notes: Filed as a follow-up to BOARD-RULES (quinn-ai-ob97) per user decision in batch-3 requirements capture (Q3=a, deferred from v0). Depends on the rules engine itself shipping — wait for quinn-ai-tlh0 (RuleEngine.evaluate) to close. Cross-references: rules #11/12/13/14 in the BOARD-RULES catalog are catalog-only in v0 and become enforceable when this epic ships.
close_reason: Session-tool guardrails shipped: qn-tool-guard, hook injection, bd→qn-bd shim, shell.bash in ABSOLUTE rules. Committed 18036ac + a14a612.
