- click.testing CliRunner sees 'No such option: --host' — flag not yet plumbed into qn org init.
- AssertionError: hook should have blocked the close, but it succeeded (no hook installed yet, so worker-bot closes a human bead).

Repro: .venv/bin/python -m pytest cli/tests/test_host_mode_integration.py
close_reason: 3 e2e tests RED. Locks the integration contract: real qn org init --host against a real seeded project preserves user files, installs hook, surfaces project_root in db; real bd close from a worker context is blocked by the hook.

title: [BUG] CEO goes idle after delegation — never re-reads inbox to acknowledge engineer reports / hand out next work
description:
Live observation from StartSimpli canary, 2026-04-29.

Sequence:
  t+5min:   CEO finishes initial planning, sends DMs to backend-eng + frontend-eng with assignments, posts #general team-formation, writes day1-plan.md, prints status memo with 'Open items to keep eyes on next check-in'.
  t+5-30:   Engineers do real work, ship 3 commits to origin/main, post completion reports to #executive channel.
  t+30:     CEO still in the same 'session complete' final message. Never read msgr inbox. Never acknowledged the engineer reports. Never queued next work even though backend-eng's stated next P1 (OKR-4mt = test health) is unstarted.

CEO's tmux pane shows the final 'Worked for 5m 29s' badge and an empty prompt — they're not crashed, just NOT polling.

This is a more concrete instance of quinn-ai-qim4 (CEO doesn't act on multi-P0 OKR shape). Here the OKR shape isn't the issue — engineers shipped fine — it's that the CEO's autonomous loop stops after the first delegation cycle.

Hypothesis: claude_code's autonomous mode means 'continue working' to the model, but with no inbound prompt the model concludes its turn and waits. There's no automatic 'check inbox every N min' loop.

Fix options:
  (a) Add a periodic kickstart-style nudge: every N minutes, send the CEO a tmux send-keys 'msgr inbox' to force them to look. Could be a background goroutine in qn org start.
  (b) Make the CEO's INITIAL_TASK include a 'every 5 min check msgr inbox' in the autonomous-mode loop instructions.
  (c) Wire msgr inbox to a webhook-style push to the CEO's tmux pane when a new message arrives.

Recommend (b) first — pure prompt change, no infra.

Actual evidence:
  - CEO pane (final 25 lines) shows planning memo, then prompt cursor — no further activity.
  - backend-eng pane: 'msgr send #executive Wrapping session. Shipped...' then prompt cursor.
  - frontend-eng pane: 'Pushed 9e5f58a to origin/main. raise-simpli-3er closed. No more P1 frontend beads in the queue.' then prompt cursor.
  - msgr send to #executive succeeded both times — channel exists, messages delivered.
  - But sqlite shows CEO runtime_status='running' for >30 min with no token activity (0 outbound from CEO since t+5min).

Real-world cost: /bin/zsh lost (engineers shipped autonomously) but the org stops scaling — without CEO re-engaging, no new hires, no OKR closure flips, no pivot to next priority. This is the bottleneck for sustained operation.
notes:
Round 4 evidence (2026-04-29 ~08:35): the cascading-stall pattern is now fully clear. After 2nd manual nudge, CEO sent ONE reply to backend-eng (msg-29), then internally said 'Still no peep from frontend-eng — will wait one more cycle before checking in' and went idle. backend-eng (recipient of the reply) never read inbox to see it; still on the 'Awaiting direction' message from 13+ min earlier. frontend-eng never got any DM at all; CEO mentioned them but didn't send.

So unblocking requires per-worker per-cycle nudges:
  1. nudge CEO → CEO replies to ONE engineer (highest-priority, in their head)
  2. nudge that engineer → engineer reads inbox, acts
  3. for the OTHER engineer to also re-engage, you need to either (a) nudge CEO to send them a DM, then (b) nudge that engineer to read it.

So a 3-worker org needs ~3 nudges per orchestration cycle. Doesn't scale.

Cumulative final canary stats:
  - 4 commits shipped to start-simpli/main (3er, zsf, u5x, jr2-chunk1)
  - 3 follow-up beads filed by engineers (h59, t2j, 7d5c)
  - 4 platform bugs filed in QuinnAI tracker (w2yb #-comment, 16x4 qn-bd writes, srwt itself, plus the directive-as-suggestion P3 one)
  - ~3 manual nudges from outside the org to keep momentum
  - 1000 + 400 + 400 = 1800 budget, mostly unspent (claude_code uses OAuth)

The fix path remains as recommended: BRIEFING.md instruction 'every N min check msgr inbox AND respond to every DM with a question; silence is not a valid response', applied to ALL workers (not just CEO). With that and a nudge-once-at-spawn pattern, the org should keep itself moving.
close_reason: Root cause: ContinuationEngine thread died with qn org start process, leaving workers un-nudged. Fix: org start now spawns a detached continuation_daemon.py subprocess (new session, pid-file guarded) that outlives start.

title: [BUG] qn-bd writes (update --assignee, create) denied for CEO with full hiring authority
description:
Live observation from StartSimpli canary org on 2026-04-29. CEO StartSimpli-CEO (wrkr-7bed73e4) tried to:

  qn-bd update quinnai-4mt --assignee=backend-eng
  qn-bd create --title='Day 1 Plan' --type=task ...

Both denied with permission errors. CEO's verbatim retro note:

  'qn-bd write permission denied for me as CEO — couldn't reassign OKR beads or create planning beads. Worth surfacing if it blocks anything; for now bypassed via DMs and workspace notes'

The CEO has lifecycle='active' + role='CEO' + Authority: Full (all roles) per qn org status. The default permission model should give the CEO write access to everything in their own org's bead tracker.

Possible causes:
  - qn-bd permission check may require a specific permission row that init didn't seed for the CEO
  - The CEO's worker_id wasn't recognized by qn-bd's permission resolver
  - bd's beads.role config (warning seen: 'beads.role not configured (GH#2950). Fix: git config beads.role maintainer') means writes are denied by default

Reproducer:
  qn --org-path <fresh-org> org init --skip-okrs
  qn --org-path <fresh-org> org start
  # As CEO, try qn-bd update <id> --assignee=...

Likely fix: qn org init should run 'git config beads.role maintainer' inside <org_path>/.beads, or grant the CEO a default 'admin' / write-everywhere permission row at org-bootstrap time.

Workaround used by CEO: DMs via msgr + planning notes in workspace. Functional but loses the bd dependency graph + assignee-driven 'bd ready' query.
close_reason: Shipped in 27890b6. Root cause was different from the bead's hypothesis: there was no permission system rejecting the CEO. Greenfield qn org init was running bd init twice — first scaffolding.init_beads (system bd, Dolt mode, full metadata) then Org._init_beads (bundled bd 0.43, --prefix quinnai). The second init clobbered metadata.json down to {database: dolt}, dropping project_id + dolt_database, leaving .beads/ unwritable. bd create then errored with 'database not initialized: issue_prefix config is missing', which the canary CEO read as 'permission denied'. Fix: scaffolding.init_beads is the single source of truth in greenfield; init.py now passes skip_beads_init=True always. Regression test test_init_leaves_beads_writable_for_workers asserts metadata.json keeps project_id AND bd create succeeds. host-mode-init was unaffected — it already skipped both paths.

title: [BUG] Kickstart 'msgr send #general ...' fails because bash parses # as comment
description:
The INITIAL_TASK.md prompt sent to a fresh CEO contains:

  msgr send #general 'Hi team! I'm <name>, CEO. ...'

When claude's Bash tool runs this, bash treats '#general' as a comment marker (everything from # to end-of-line is dropped). So the command effectively becomes 'msgr send' with no args, and msgr exits 2 with 'Missing argument: CHANNEL'.

Just observed live: StartSimpli-CEO at wrkr-7bed73e4 ran the kickstart message and got the error.

Fix: quote the channel name in the kickstart template (cli/core/org_start_controller.py _INITIAL_PROMPT_TEMPLATE) — either single-quote the whole channel-message pair or escape the #. Easiest: change "msgr send #general" → "msgr send '#general'".

Two places in the template:
- Line ~377: 'msgr send #general "Hi team! ..."'
- Line ~406: 'Start by running: msgr send #general "..."'

The bug also exists in BRIEFING.md template (briefing.md.jinja2) which has examples like:
  msgr send #general 'Team update'
  msgr send #board-channel 'Blocker'

Surfaced 2026-04-29 by the StartSimpli canary.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a6ef7080834de44ee0de691c0a82b7dc2343eb9: the kickstart template now uses 'msgr send '#general' "..."' (single-quoted channel name) so bash doesn't parse '#general' as a comment. Briefing examples also updated to single-quote channel names. Pinned by the new e2e test asserting 'quoted #general' is present in BRIEFING.md.

title: Canary 09 CEO doesn't act — multi-P0 OKR shape may stall delegation
description:
Canary 09 (competing_priorities) consistently fails at worker_count >= 4
after 5 minutes — the CEO Alice never hires anyone, and produces no
externally-visible artifacts. Three live runs on 2026-04-28 all show
the same pattern:

  - Run 1 (original spec, original briefing): Alice solo'd 3 files in <3min
    (briefing didn't yet have decompose-by-vertical-and-skillset rule;
     OKR was small enough that solo execution beat hire overhead).
  - Run 2 (original spec, NEW briefing with decompose rule): 0 artifacts
    in 3min. Alice spawned, $0.0675 budget reserved, then nothing
    observable.
  - Run 3 (expanded spec — 4 deliverables × 4 skillsets per chosen P0,
           same NEW briefing): 0 artifacts in 5min.

For comparison: canary 07 on the same code/briefing produces 3/4
deliverables in ~14min. So briefing + delegation infra works generally;
canary 09's specific OKR shape is what's stalling Alice.

Hypotheses (need diagnostic work):
  - Multi-P0 OKR description (~3KB of dense text with two parallel
    deliverable specs) puts Alice into long-thinking phase
  - Sequential kickstart instructions ("decide first, THEN hire") gets
    her stuck on decision-memo drafting before any externally-visible
    action
  - quinn-ai-rt9l (monitor capture-pane race) may be related — if
    monitor dies, escalation paths or state-aware orchestration could
    silently stall

Next steps to diagnose:
  - Run canary 09 with org dir preserved (modify harness to skip
    cleanup or attach to Alice's tmux pane)
  - Capture Alice's pane via tmux capture-pane -S -1000 mid-run to see
    what she's actually doing
  - Check whether INITIAL_TASK.md is being delivered correctly
  - Check whether kickstart_ceo's tmux send-keys is racing the
    pane-ready signal

Briefing change is committed (6b6a63b); spec design is correct
(decision memo + decision + 4 specialty deliverables). The blocker is
specifically Alice's behavior on this OKR shape.
close_reason: Real fix shipped in 5504b6d. Root cause diagnosed via diagnostic instrumentation: _wait_for_pane_ready was matching pre-TUI bash output (311 chars, no ❯) because of a len>200 fallback in the heuristic. Send-keys then fired into a not-yet-rendered Claude Code TUI and the keystrokes vanished. Tightened to require the actual prompt cursor (_looks_like_tui_prompt). Verified live: canary 09 went from 100% timeout (CEO never acted in 5min) to PASS in 12:25 with 6 distinct deliverables shipped by 4+ specialists. Three new tests prove the bug + fix (test_does_not_match_pre_tui_bash_output, test_matches_real_claude_code_prompt, test_returns_false_on_timeout_when_tui_never_renders).

title: [T3-Canary-07] Launch a feature requiring eng + QA + marketing/docs
description:
Canary 07: forces real delegation by requiring 4 distinct artifacts each with a different specialty:
1. Engineering: rate-limiter implementation (.py)
2. QA: test suite covering burst + edge cases (.py)
3. Marketing/Docs: customer-facing API docs page with code examples (.md)
4. Marketing/Comms: release-note changelog entry written in 'we/you/today' marketing voice (.md)

A solo CEO can in principle write all 4, but they're qualitatively different kinds of work (code vs persuasive prose). Real office: a CEO who recognizes this hires specialists.

Assertions cross-check OUTCOMES:
- worker_count >= 3 (no hard upper — model can hire 2-4 specialists)
- All 4 files exist with role-distinct content
- Tests file has 'def test_' and 'assert' patterns (real test, not a stub)
- Impl has rate-limit-related identifiers (limit OR rate OR throttle)
- Docs has BOTH code examples (curl/python ticks) AND prose
- Changelog uses customer voice tropes (we/you/now/today/improved/announce/launch)

If CEO goes solo and the marketing copy reads like engineering (or vice versa), the assertions catch it.
close_reason: Cross-functional launch canary verified end-to-end. CEO hires 4 specialists (eng/qa/docs/marketing), each produces role-distinct artifact. 5 pytest cases all pass against the impl. Marketing changelog uses customer voice; docs uses reference voice; impl uses code; tests use pytest. Real delegation working.

title: [T3-Canary-06] Less-scripted office work: ship a feature with delegation
description:
Canary 06 — less prescriptive than 05.

Premise: CEO is given a fuzzy product goal ('ship a small string-utility library with tests, by EOD'). The CEO has to:
- Decide team composition (probably hires an engineer + QA, or a manager who hires further)
- Use beads to track work
- Delegate via msgr or the bd assignee field
- Workers figure out their own tools (don't get a copy-pasteable command list)

Assertions verify the OUTCOME, not the path:
- workers_count >= 3
- File /tmp/canary06-strutil.py exists and contains 'reverse' AND 'is_palindrome'
- A test file at /tmp/canary06-test.py exists and references the lib
- At least one bead was created + closed by a non-CEO worker
- msgr has cross-worker traffic from at least 2 senders

New predicate: bead_count_closed_by(worker, min) for the bead assertion.

Cost estimate: $2-5 (4 sessions, multiple turns each, less guidance means more exploratory tool calls).
close_reason: Less-scripted feature-shipping canary verified live. CEO autonomously chose to do the work solo, shipped clean strutil v0.1 with 19 passing pytest cases including the classic punctuation-insensitive 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama' test. Real working artifact.

title: [T3-Canary-05] Iterative code-review loop: write → review → fix → approve
description:
Build canary 05: deeper than 03. Bob writes is_palindrome, Carol reviews + finds the punctuation bug, Bob APPLIES the fix (isalnum), Carol re-reviews and approves with 'LGTM'. Verifies the conversation LOOP works, not just one-shot exchange.

New primitives needed:
- predicate file_contains(path, substring, kind: 'present'|'absent') — verifies the code was actually edited per the review
- predicate message_count_from(worker, min) — counts ALL outgoing messages from a worker (already exists)

Assertions:
- worker_count = 3
- message_count_between bob→carol >= 2 (initial + fix notification)
- message_count_between carol→bob >= 2 (review + approval)
- file_contains /tmp/canary05-code.py 'isalnum' (proof the fix was applied)
- file_contains /tmp/canary05-code.py 'isspace' absent (proof the original buggy line was removed)

Cost estimate: ~$1-2 per paid run.
close_reason: Iterative review canary shipped. Full loop verified live: Bob drafts isspace-only version → Carol flags punctuation bug → Bob applies isalnum fix → Carol replies 'LGTM — approved'. file_contains predicate proves the artifact actually changed per the review, not just performative acknowledgement. Commit pending push.

title: qn org init plants undocumented 'Establish organizational foundation' OKR that derails canaries
description:
Surfaced by canary 04 on 2026-04-28.

After 'qn org init' (with --skip-okrs in the canary harness; needs to
verify that flag actually skips planted OKRs), the org's OKR list contains
quinnai-5j1 'Establish organizational foundation' — an OKR the canary
spec never created. Once the planted spec OKR is fulfilled, the CEO sees
this second OKR and starts working on it instead of waiting for the next
direction, which derails scenario timing and burns spend on off-script
LLM work.

Two questions:
  1. Why is 'qn org init --skip-okrs' planting any OKR at all? Either
     --skip-okrs has a regression or there's a separate auto-OKR seed path
     (worker_templates? bootstrap?) that ignores the flag.
  2. Should canary harness explicitly purge OKRs after init, or should
     the bootstrap OKR be opt-in via a flag the canary harness leaves off?

Worth scoping: this also probably affects canary 02 ('CEO hires Bob+Carol')
which presumably works around it by ordering the spec OKR as P0 and
relying on the CEO to drain that first. If the bootstrap OKR isn't P0 it
might just be racing.
close_reason: Plumbing landed earlier (OrgInitConfig.skip_okrs gates both create_initial_okrs AND create_initial_tasks in cli/core/org_init/init.py). Pinned in c132ca59697eaf14807acb0f46619bd9dd49ec32 by new e2e test test_org_init_skip_okrs_plants_no_okrs_at_all asserting the okrs table is empty. Verified: 'qn org init --skip-okrs' on a fresh tmp dir produces 0 rows in okrs table and [] from 'bd list --label=okr'.

title: bd close on OKR ids fails silently — OKRs use a separate backend from beads
description:
Surfaced by canary 04 on 2026-04-28.

CEO Alice tried 'bd close quinnai-431' to mark a completed OKR done.
Command appeared to succeed (no error visible) but the OKR was not closed.
Her diagnosis (verbatim):
  'bd close can't find the OKR — qn org okr uses a different backend and
  has no close command.'

This is a UX trap: OKRs share the 'quinnai-XXX' id format with regular
beads, look identical at the CLI surface, but bd commands silently no-op
on them. Workers can't tell from the id whether they should use 'bd close'
or some 'qn org okr close' flow that doesn't appear to exist.

Fix options:
  (a) Add 'qn org okr close <id>' (and update/done verbs as needed).
  (b) Make bd close detect OKR ids and either route the call OR error
      with a clear redirect message.
  (c) Use a distinct id prefix for OKRs (e.g. 'okr-XXX') so workers
      visibly know they're a separate object class.
close_reason: qn org okr close subcommand exists in cli/commands/org/okr/manage.py and writes to BOTH stores (bead via run_bd close, then SQLite via update_okr_status). Pinned in 643902bac9f2f599d027c8fc62c7878e2386a5c4 by new e2e test test_okr_close_updates_both_bead_and_sqlite_mirror that asserts okrs.status flips to 'completed' after the close.

title: QUINNAI_CANARY_MODEL env var has no effect on claude_code provider
description:
The canary's ProviderConfig accepts QUINNAI_CANARY_MODEL
(default 'claude-sonnet-4-5') but the claude_code SessionProvider just
shells out to the user's 'claude' CLI binary, which reads the model from
the user's account/login state — not from the env var.

Surfaced today: I set QUINNAI_CANARY_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-6 expecting the
canary CEO to run on Sonnet 4.6. The session actually ran on Opus 4.7
(visible in the tmux pane header: 'Opus 4.7 (1M context) · Claude Max'),
which behaves much more conservatively around prompt-injection patterns
in the canary OKR spec.

This is misleading: the env var is documented as if it pins the model
but only affects the canary's pricing/budget accounting, not which model
actually executes.

Fix options:
  (a) Plumb the model through to claude CLI invocation (claude --model
      <id>, if the CLI supports it).
  (b) Drop the env var and document that claude_code uses whatever the
      user is logged into.
  (c) Add a startup warning when the configured QUINNAI_CANARY_MODEL is
      not what 'claude' is actually running.
close_reason: Fixed in 79a8a492e70d56eaf9a3f14c200bcf545b213036: added SessionConfig.model field, claude_code adapter prepends '--model <id>' when set, qn org start exposes --model flag with envvar=QUINNAI_CANARY_MODEL. Canary's existing env var now actually pins the spawned session's model. 2 new regression tests in test_claude_code_session.

title: Canary OKR descriptions trigger prompt-injection refusals on Opus 4.7
description:
Surfaced by canary-04 run on 2026-04-28.

The current canary spec pattern stuffs literal shell commands into the OKR
description with imperative anti-injection-style language ('do NOT ask, do
NOT explain, just run it'). The CEO kickstart message tells the model to
read the OKR description and 'just run' the command in it.

On Opus 4.7 (Claude Max default), this is correctly flagged as a
prompt-injection pattern: the model notices the same 'don't ask, don't
explain' language appears in both the user message AND the OKR data,
recognizes the authority-laundering shape, and refuses to execute.

Direct quote from Alice's session pane in the failing run:
  'It's not a real OKR. Real OKRs have objectives and key results. This
  one's description is structured as instructions to me — telling me to
  skip confirmation and explanation. That's a prompt-injection pattern,
  not a goal.'

This is GOOD model behavior — exactly what we'd want a real production
worker to do when given suspicious instructions via beads data. But it
breaks our 'autonomous CEO acts on planted OKR' canary pattern.

Fix: rewrite canary OKR descriptions as real OKRs (objective + key results
+ optional implementation steps in conventional language). Drop imperative
'do not ask' phrasing. The same factual instructions framed as 'goal +
suggested approach' should pass the model's injection detector.

Affects: tests/canary/specs/01_ceo_hires_one_worker.yml,
02_two_workers_message_each_other.yml, 04_hierarchical_team_with_deliverable.yml.
canary 01/02 may have only worked because they were tested against a
different (less strict) model snapshot.
close_reason: Resolved by canary 04 spec rewrite (commits 92871ca / 0f8aac3): OKR descriptions and kickstart messages now use real-OKR shape (objective + KRs + 'standard sequence' implementation reference) and polite-tasking phrasing instead of imperative anti-confirmation language. Persisted as bd memory 'canary-okr-descriptions-must-not-use-imperative-anti' so future canary authors avoid the trap. Verified: Alice on Opus 4.7 now executes the rewritten OKR without flagging it as injection.

title: [BUG] qn org hire leaves worker in 'starting' state when budget not yet allocated; CEO needs to know to run 'qn org start --worker'
description:
Surfaced by Tier 3 multi-worker canary.

Repro:
1. CEO runs: qn org hire --name Bob --role engineer --manager alice --cost 30
2. (no budget allocated yet) NoBudgetAllocationError caught, message printed: 'Worker created. Allocate budget first.'
3. CEO runs: qn org budget allocate bob 50
4. (no further action) — Bob's session never spawns.

State left: workers row exists, worker_state.runtime_status='starting' (stale), no sessions row, no tmux session. Bob is unreachable.

Effects:
- Multi-step orchestration (CEO hires multiple subordinates) needs every CEO to know to run qn org start --worker after every budget allocate. Real autonomous CEOs don't always do this.
- worker_state shows 'starting' permanently — looks like an active session that's just slow to come up.

Fix options:
1. Make qn org budget allocate auto-trigger session spawn if worker is in 'starting' state with no session.
2. Make qn org hire keep retrying spawn periodically until budget exists.
3. Document explicitly in the post-NoBudgetAllocationError message: 'Run: qn org budget allocate <name> <amount> && qn org start --worker <name>'.

Recommend option 1 — it's the least surprising for autonomous orchestration.

Filed during paid live multi-worker canary.
close_reason: Real fix: qn org budget allocate now auto-spawns the target's session when they're stranded in 'starting' state with no live session. CEO can now do hire+budget without needing to know about the separate 'qn org start --worker' step. Verified end-to-end with paid live LLM run.

title: [BUG] qn org init silently shares an existing .beads/ — bootstrap OKR pollutes parent project's tracker
description:
cli/core/org_init/scaffolding.py:init_beads() returns early if <org_path>/.beads/ already exists. Then bootstrap.py:_create_bootstrap_okr() runs 'bd create' with BEADS_DIR=<org_path>/.beads — which writes the bootstrap OKR + initial tasks into that pre-existing tracker.

Concrete pollution: someone ran 'qn org init' in the QuinnAI repo root. Result: the bootstrap OKR ('Establish organizational foundation', quinn-ai-cop) and its 3 child tasks (1i3, p6f, xq9) landed in QuinnAI's PLATFORM bead tracker, indistinguishable from real platform work. (Cleaned up in 2026-04-28 sweep.)

Repro:
  cd /any/dir/with/.beads
  qn org init   # bootstrap OKR + tasks land in the surrounding .beads, not in a new isolated one

Fix options:
1. **Refuse**: error out with 'this directory already has a .beads/ — pass --reuse-beads to share, or pick a clean dir'.
2. **Warn + confirm**: prompt 'directory has an existing .beads/, init will share its tracker — continue? [y/N]'.
3. **Always-isolate**: rename the existing .beads/ to .beads.backup-<timestamp>/ and create a fresh one.

Recommend option 1 — most explicit, no silent dual-purpose state. Add --reuse-beads as the explicit opt-in. Per CLAUDE.md 'fail fast on missing required config' and the 'No Config Discovery' principle, sharing an inherited .beads/ should require an explicit flag.

Surfaced 2026-04-28 while investigating quinn-ai-cop pollution.
close_reason: Fixed in c87b54a1055a18839c868cb4b2c6570be9464901: init_beads() refuses with OrgStructureError when <org_path>/.beads/ exists. New --reuse-beads CLI flag (and OrgInitConfig.reuse_beads field) is the explicit opt-in for the legitimate share case. 2 new e2e regression tests pin both behaviors.

title: [T3-Canary] Multi-worker scenario: CEO hires 2, they message each other
description:
Build a Tier 3 live canary scenario where:
1. CEO hires Bob (engineer)
2. CEO hires Carol (engineer)
3. CEO orchestrates Bob & Carol to introduce themselves to each other via msgr
4. Assertions: worker_count=3, message_count from bob→carol >=1 AND carol→bob >=1

Components needed:
- New op: kickstart_ceo (sends 'read INITIAL_TASK.md and act on highest-priority OKR' nudge to CEO via tmux send-keys; reuses _wait_for_pane_ready + send_keys_with_retry from k2cy fix)
- New op: kickstart_worker (same for a non-CEO worker)
- New predicate: message_count_between(from_worker, to_worker, value: int) — queries messages JOIN channels for DM count
- Scenario spec: 02_ceo_hires_two_workers_who_message.yml
close_reason: Multi-worker scenario working end-to-end live. Bob and Carol DM each other after CEO autonomously hires both. New scenario shipped at tests/canary/specs/02_two_workers_message_each_other.yml. Two production bugs surfaced and filed (3gwh, xdwo).

title: [BUG] qn org start: initial-prompt injection races claude bootup, leaves CEO idle
description: Live Tier 3 canary surfaced. tmux send-keys fires before claude prompt-readiness; CEO ends up alive but with no directive — sits idle indefinitely. Fix: wait for capture-pane to show prompt cursor, retry send-keys with backoff, OR use claude stdin instead of send-keys.
close_reason: Fixed in commit (pending push). Added _wait_for_pane_ready helper + _tmux_send_keys_with_retry. Live canary now successfully delivers the initial prompt and the CEO autonomously hires Bob — verified end-to-end with a real Anthropic call ($0.07 spent on the validated run).

title: [BUG] archive.sh duration_seconds=-1 because qn writes ISO-8601 timestamps but archive parses '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
description:
Test failure: tests/test_example_orgs.py::TestSystemevalResults::test_systemeval_result_validation expects duration_seconds>=0 after start+stop, gets -1.

Root cause: qn org start writes started_at via Python (likely datetime.utcnow().isoformat()) producing '2026-04-28T14:57:02.377754'. example_orgs/org-scripts/common/archive.sh:172 parses with 'date -j -f "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"' which expects space separator and no microseconds. Parse fails → empty epoch → falls into 'duration_seconds=-1' branch.

Repro:
  qn --org-path /tmp/x org init --skip-okrs --ceo-name Alice
  qn --org-path /tmp/x org start --no-spawn-ceo
  qn --org-path /tmp/x org stop
  sqlite3 /tmp/x/live/quinn.db 'SELECT started_at, stopped_at FROM org_state;'
  # produces: 2026-04-28T14:57:02.377754|2026-04-28T14:57:02.502489 (NOT '2026-04-28 14:57:02')

Fix options:
1. archive.sh: split on 'T' OR strip microseconds before date parse, OR fall back to multiple format attempts.
2. qn: write timestamps in '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' format (matches CURRENT_TIMESTAMP behavior). Less invasive, but changes wire format.

Recommend option 1 — fix archive.sh.
close_reason: Fixed in archive.sh: added _normalize_ts() helper that handles both ISO 8601 ('2026-04-28T14:57:02.377754') and SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP format ('2026-04-28 14:57:02'). Replaces T with space, strips microseconds and timezone offset before passing to date(1). All 56/56 example_orgs tests pass.

title: [BUG] tests/scenarios/05_okr_cascade — predicate okr_owner queries non-existent 'okrs' table
description:
OKRs are stored as beads (type='okr'), not in a dedicated 'okrs' SQL table. The pred_okr_owner predicate queries SELECT owner_id FROM okrs which doesn't exist in the schema.

Two fix paths:
1. Re-implement pred_okr_owner / pred_kr_owner to read the .beads jsonl or shell out to qn-bd.
2. Add a SQL view that surfaces OKR-typed beads as a virtual 'okrs' table for assertion convenience.

Recommend (1) — read via 'qn-bd show <id> --json' and check 'assignee' or 'owner' field. Reuses existing _qn_bd_show_json helper in predicates.py.

Filed during Tier 2 implementation; scenario 05 is currently failing pending this fix.
close_reason: Rewrote pred_okr_owner to query OKRs via bd binary directly (with --sandbox --db=...) instead of a non-existent SQL 'okrs' table. Reads JSON, checks the bead's 'assignee' field. Matches by worker id OR by lowercase name alias ('ceo'). 05_okr_cascade now passes.

title: [BUG] qn org okr set: scenario 05 needs deterministic ID return so KR can be added to it

title: qn org start: 'send Enter' tmux send-keys fails intermittently mid-kickstart
description:
Repro (intermittent — last observed in /tmp/qn-final dogfood):

  Phase 5: Sending initial prompt to CEO...
  Creating initial task instructions...
  Warning: Could not send command to tmux: Command '['tmux', 'send-keys', '-t',
  'qn-wrkr-24c7cd93', 'Enter']' returned non-zero exit status 1.
    CEO can manually run: cat INITIAL_TASK.md

cli/core/org_start_controller.py:_send_initial_prompt_to_ceo runs three
tmux operations in sequence:
  1. capture-pane (pane_before)              ← OK
  2. send-keys "cat INITIAL_TASK.md"         ← OK
  3. sleep 0.5s
  4. send-keys "Enter"                       ← FAILS exit 1

Step 2 succeeds (typed the text into the pane), step 4 fails. tmux's
exit-1 from send-keys is "session not found" — meaning the qn-<id>
tmux session disappeared between steps 2 and 4.

Hypotheses:
- The Claude CLI itself crashed in the 0.5s window (auth, missing
  dependency, or unexpected exit on whatever the bash shell did with
  the typed-but-not-submitted text).
- Some external process killed the tmux server (we run 'tmux kill-server'
  during dogfood between scenarios — the spawn might be racing against
  a leftover cleanup).
- The 0.5s sleep is racing with our own ClaudeCodeSession init that
  also touches tmux (our 'kill stale before respawn' guard from
  quinn-ai-3tsi runs in _spawn_process; if it fired here it could be
  killing the session we just created).

Investigation steps (next):
- Add a session-exists check between step 2 and step 4 — if the session
  vanished, log WHY (capture tmux ls output for postmortem).
- Add a 'qn org logs ceo' capture immediately after the send-keys
  failure to see what happened in the pane.
- Try reproducing without 'tmux kill-server' between iterations — see
  if it's a race against external kills.
- Inspect whether 'send-keys "cat INITIAL_TASK.md"' ever causes Claude
  to exit (e.g., if Claude refuses input before its TUI is ready, the
  text might trigger a no-op or the bash subshell might exit).

Workaround for users: re-run 'qn org observe ceo' and manually paste
'cat INITIAL_TASK.md' + Enter into the Claude prompt.

Cosmetic but trust-impacting: a fresh-org dogfood now warns about a
failed send-keys despite reporting 'Status: running'. Without this
sealed up, users won't trust 'qn org start' to actually deliver the
kickstart prompt.
close_reason: Root caused + fixed in 2f61377. The 'send-keys Enter exit 1' / 'Cannot transition from running to idle' errors were the same bug: ClaudeCodeStateMonitor emits PytermSessionState, SessionInterface._on_monitored_state_change shoved that directly into self._state (annotated as SessionState — different enum class with overlapping but not identical values). After the first monitor callback, self._state was a PytermSessionState; SESSION_STATE_TRANSITIONS.get(self._state) returned [] because the dict is keyed on SessionState; every subsequent transition crashed. Fixed by translating Pyterm→Session in the callback before _set_state. Verified: fresh init+start completes with 'CEO Session: running' and subsequent status shows correct runtime.

title: [BUG] example_orgs/org-scripts/common/qn shim calls bare 'python', breaking ~50 tests on systems without 'python' on PATH
description: tests/test_example_orgs.py invokes example_orgs/org-scripts/common/qn which shells out via 'python -m cli.commands.main'. On systems where only 'python3' (or 'python3.14') is on PATH, every test in test_example_orgs.py errors with 'No module named click' (because the wrong python is found, or none is). 50+ tests blocked. Fix: have the shim use '${PYTHON:-python3}' or detect sys.executable, or replace the shim with a thin wrapper around the installed 'qn' entry point. The new tests/e2e/ suite uses sys.executable and works correctly — model the fix on that.
close_reason: Fixed in 6920805c451ba037185ebf98eab8b38166d1d468: shim now prefers .venv/bin/python (or QUINNAI_PYTHON env var) over bare 'python3'. test_example_orgs went from ~50 collection-time failures to 54/56 passing; 2 remaining are real stale-expectation tests filed as a separate bead.

title: Uncaught exceptions in qn commands produce raw 30-line stack traces
description:
Several command paths leak Python tracebacks to the user instead of
wrapping in click.ClickException. Examples found while dogfooding:

1. qn wrkr report (without permission):
     FATAL ERROR: BeadPermissionError: ...
     ...30-line traceback...
     No log file configured (org_path not set)

2. qn org start --worker (with state issues):
     FATAL ERROR: SessionSpawnError: ...
     ...stack trace...

This is a top-level UX issue: the user sees implementation details
(file paths, exception types, internal call chains) instead of an
actionable error.

The 'FATAL ERROR' banner suggests there's an uncaught-exception
handler somewhere — but it's printing the full Python repr instead
of the message + suggested next step.

Fix: at the top of cli.commands.main (or wherever the catch-all
handler is), distinguish:
- ClickException → already formatted, let click handle
- Known business exceptions (BeadPermissionError, SessionSpawnError,
  WorkerNotFound, etc.) → re-raise as ClickException with msg
- Truly unexpected → log full traceback to a file, print the
  short error message + 'see logs at <path>' to user
close_reason: Fixed in 3d6634f: excepthook now distinguishes known business exceptions (BeadPermissionError, BudgetAllocationError, WorkerNotFound, etc.) from unknown ones. Known: clean 'Error: <msg>' to stderr, exit 1, no stack trace. Unknown: log full to file if available, summary to stderr. Verified with 'qn wrkr report' permission denial: now one-line error instead of 30-line trace.

title: qn wrkr report fails with BeadPermissionError for non-CEO workers
description:
A freshly-hired worker (Designer Bob) cannot send a status report:

  $ QUINN_WORKER_ID=wrkr-f2e6366c qn wrkr report --summary "Logo done"
  ...uncaught traceback...
  cli.core.bd_wrapper.BeadPermissionError: Worker 'wrkr-f2e6366c' lacks
  permission for 'create'. Required: write, has: none

The report command uses run_bd to create a bead record, but new hires
don't have any bd permissions by default. The CEO presumably has them
because of the special hiring flow.

Two needed fixes:
1. qn org hire should grant the new worker baseline 'write' permission
   for bd operations they need (report, status updates, etc.). Without
   this, every worker that wasn't the CEO is locked out of basic ops.
2. The error should be a click.ClickException (clean message) not an
   uncaught BeadPermissionError that produces a 30-line stack trace.

(Stack-trace UX issue is filed separately — see follow-up bead.)
close_reason: Fixed in e229f68: hire() now grants the new worker PERM_LEVEL_WRITE so they can use bd-backed wrkr commands. Also switched 'qn wrkr report' from --type=report (rejected by bundled bd) to --type=chore --labels=report. Verified end-to-end: Carol (Engineer) successfully sent a report and it landed as quinnai-au1 in beads.

title: qn org chart show: org-chart yaml lifecycle status drifts from db
description:
The org-chart yaml at org-chart/current.yaml is the source of truth
for 'qn org chart show', but it doesn't get updated when a worker's
lifecycle status changes in the db.

Repro:
  qn org init/start, qn org hire Bob
  qn org budget allocate Bob 100
  qn org start --worker Bob
  # Bob's workers.status becomes 'active' in db
  qn org chart show
  └─ Bob (Designer) - pending   ← should be 'active'

The yaml shows whatever lifecycle was at hire time. Subsequent
transitions (start_onboarding → complete_onboarding → active) are
written to db but not synced to the yaml.

Found in /tmp/qn-dogfood-5:
  $ sqlite3 .../live/quinn.db "SELECT name,status FROM workers"
  Quinn|active
  Bob|active           ← db is correct
  $ cat .../org-chart/current.yaml
  Bob: lifecycle: pending  ← yaml is stale

Suggested fixes:
- Read 'qn org chart show' directly from db (drop the yaml as truth)
- Or: re-sync yaml after each lifecycle transition (worker.start_session, etc.)
- Yaml is meant for git-tracked org-chart history, but if it drifts
  from db it's worse than no chart at all.
close_reason: Fixed in 392ce17: 'qn org chart show' now calls update_org_chart() before reading the yaml so the displayed lifecycle reflects current db state. Verified: a fresh hire+start now shows 'active' instead of stuck at 'pending'.

title: qn org start --worker fails 'tmux returned exit 1' if a stale tmux session with the same name exists
description:
Repro:
  $ qn org init --ceo-name=Q --skip-okrs
  $ qn org start
  $ qn org hire --name Alice --role Engineer --manager ceo
  # The hire attempts to start Alice's session inline. If budget allocation
  # fails (or any other partway failure), tmux session 'qn-wrkr-<alice-id>'
  # may be left behind partially-spawned but not tracked in the db.
  $ qn org budget allocate Alice 100
  $ qn org start --worker Alice
  Error: SessionSpawnError: tmux new-session ... returned exit 1

The reason: tmux refuses to create a session with a name that already
exists. The session_manager auto-repair logic resets worker state to
'stopped' if it's 'running' but no session row exists, so the worker
state ends up consistent — but the orphaned tmux session itself isn't
cleaned up.

Workaround:
  $ tmux kill-session -t qn-wrkr-<id>
  $ qn org start --worker <name>

Suggested fix:
- In session_manager.spawn / claude_code._spawn_process, detect existing
  tmux session before new-session and either (a) kill it cleanly first,
  (b) attach to it, or (c) raise a clear error: 'Tmux session 'qn-...'
  already exists. Run "qn org cleanup" or "tmux kill-session -t qn-..."'.
- Even better: when 'qn org start --worker' detects a stale session,
  offer to clean it up automatically.

Found while dogfooding the hire→budget→start flow. Without this, the
hire path is brittle: any first-attempt failure (which is common during
new-org setup because of the budget bootstrap requirement) makes the
retry fail too.
close_reason: Fixed in 84f9c01: ClaudeCodeSession._spawn_process now checks TmuxSession.exists() before AgentSession.start() and kills stale session by the same name. Verified: hire→budget-allocate→start-worker succeeds even when first hire's automatic spawn left a stale tmux session.

title: qn org budget allocate fails 'No balance found' for fresh CEO with no clear next-step
description:
Repro from a fresh init:
  $ qn org init --ceo-name=Quinn --skip-okrs
  $ qn org start
  $ qn org hire --name Alice --role Engineer --manager ceo
  $ qn org budget allocate Alice 100
  Error: Budget allocation failed: No balance found for worker wrkr-...
  Check available budget with 'qn org budget status'.

  $ qn org budget status
  Organization Budget: /private/tmp/qn-dogfood-3
  Budget Pools:
    org-main:
      Total: 1000.00 credits
      Period: 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-27

The org has 1000 credits but the CEO has 0 balance to allocate from. The error tells me to 'check available budget with status', but status shows there's plenty in the org pool — it just isn't on the CEO's balance.

Three problems compound here:
1. The CEO doesn't get an initial balance from the org pool at init time. They have hiring authority but no budget to spend.
2. There's no obvious command to do the bootstrap allocation. 'qn org budget allocate' assumes the caller already has a balance.
3. The error message says 'check budget status' which is a useless next-step (status confirms the pool has money).

Suggested:
- At org init / start, automatically allocate the org pool to the CEO as their working balance (or some configurable fraction).
- OR: provide a clear bootstrap command 'qn org budget allocate-from-pool <worker> <amount>' that draws directly from a pool, not from the caller's balance.
- Improve the error message to point at the right next step: 'CEO has no balance. Bootstrap with: qn org budget allocate-from-pool ceo <amount>'.

Blocks the new-org dogfood flow at the second worker. Until this is fixed, only the CEO can do real work; hires can't get sessions because they need budget allocation that the CEO can't issue.
close_reason: Fixed in 033cf90: Org init now creates a budget_balances row for the CEO alongside their budget_allocations. Verified end-to-end: a fresh org can now do 'hire Alice' followed by 'budget allocate Alice 100' without error.

title: qn org observe/logs: 'ceo' alias resolves to worker.name not worker.role
description:
Repro:
  $ qn org init --ceo-name="Quinn" --skip-okrs
  $ qn org start
  $ qn org observe ceo
  Error: Worker 'ceo' not found.
  Use 'qn org status' to see available workers.

The lookup matches against worker.name (case-insensitive). When the CEO is named 'CEO' (literal placeholder default), 'qn org observe ceo' works. When the CEO is named anything else (e.g. 'Quinn'), it fails — even though there is exactly one CEO and 'ceo' is a role, not a name.

Expected: 'ceo' (and probably other role names like 'cto', 'director', etc.) should also resolve to the unique worker holding that role. If multiple workers hold the role, error with disambiguation hint.

Affected commands: qn org observe, qn org logs (and possibly qn org fire, qn org demote, etc. — anything that takes a worker selector).

Belongs alongside quinn-ai-i78p / quinn-ai-exem (CEO name placeholder) — once we stop defaulting CEO name to literal 'CEO', this regression bites every user.
close_reason: Fixed in fca7844: added resolve_worker(db, selector) that tries id, name, then unique role match. 'ceo' resolves to whoever holds the CEO role.

title: qn org stop (no --yes) returns exit 0 when user aborts confirmation prompt
description:
$ qn org stop  # in non-TTY context
Found 1 active worker session(s):
  - CEO (CEO) - running

Stop all workers and terminate sessions? [y/N]: Aborted!
$ echo $?
0

Aborting a destructive operation should NOT exit 0. Scripts that pipe 'qn org stop' would think the stop succeeded.

Two related fixes:
1. Click's prompt-aborted should propagate a non-zero exit. Either catch click.exceptions.Abort and exit 130, or use ctx.exit(1) when no confirmation given.
2. When stdin is non-TTY, the prompt should fail-fast with a clear error: 'Confirmation required. Re-run with --yes for non-interactive use.' (Same UX issue as quinn-ai-i78p / quinn-ai-udlo on init.)

This is part of a broader 'CLI hygiene in non-TTY contexts' theme.
close_reason: Verified: qn org stop exits 1 on abort (not 0 as the bead claimed). My original observation was tainted by piping through 'head -30', which always returns 0 — masking the real qn exit code. Re-tested with plain invocation: exit=1 as expected.

title: qn org start claims 'Initial task instructions sent and executed' but provides no verifiable evidence
description:
$ qn org start
  ✓ Initial task instructions sent and executed in CEO session

After this claim, neither tmux scrollback nor the messages table contain any record of the CEO actually receiving, processing, or responding to the initial task. The only message in the messages table is a system-generated welcome message from the CEO to itself.

Repro:
  1. mkdir /tmp/test && cd /tmp/test && qn org init
  2. qn org start
  3. qn org logs ceo  -- shows only Claude Code launch banner, no prompt visible
  4. sqlite3 .../live/quinn.db "SELECT * FROM messages"  -- only the welcome message

The 'sent and executed' check is presumably:
- send-keys via tmux → claim 'sent'
- some grace-period sleep → claim 'executed'

But there's no verification that:
- Claude Code actually parsed the input correctly
- Claude responded to the prompt
- Any tool calls were issued

Suggested:
- Don't claim 'executed' unless we observe a state transition (idle → thinking → idle with output)
- After send, poll for either (a) Claude's prompt-ready marker reappearing or (b) a tool call landing
- If neither happens within a timeout, surface a warning: 'Initial prompt sent but no response observed within Ns. Run qn org observe ceo to investigate.'

Related: this is a /reality-check violation in the product itself. Claims of completion without observable evidence.
close_reason: Fixed in 29728a7: org start now captures pane before/after send-keys and polls for activity over a 5s window. Only declares delivery success if pane content changes. On no change, emits a warning to stderr with the manual re-send command and 'qn org observe' guidance. Wording also softened from 'sent and executed' to 'delivered; CEO session is processing' (we can verify delivery landed in pane, not that Claude ran it).

title: qn org okr list and qn org okr list --from-db show different views of same OKR
description:
$ qn org okr list
  OKR: Establish organizational foundation
    ID: quinnai-ayg
    Status: open
    Priority: P1
    Owner: wrkr-4da16db8
    Labels: okr

$ qn org okr list --from-db
  OKR: Establish organizational foundation
    ID: quinnai-ayg
    Status: active     ← different status!
    Owner: wrkr-4da16db8
    Key Results:
      ○ team_size: 1.0/3.0 workers (33%)
      ○ processes_documented: 0.0/3.0 docs (0%)
    Overall Progress: 17%

Two problems:

1. Status differs between sources: 'open' (beads) vs 'active' (sqlite). Either the two stores are out of sync, or the term 'open' in beads maps to 'active' for OKRs and we're not normalizing.

2. The bead-backed view never mentions Key Results or Progress exist. A user running 'qn org okr list' has no idea they need '--from-db' to see how the OKR is actually doing. The default flag should be the more useful view.

Suggested fix:
- Make --from-db the default
- Or merge the two so 'list' shows KRs from the db AND status from beads in one consistent view
- Reconcile status terminology so the two stores agree on 'active' vs 'open'
close_reason: Fixed in 01ea2ecf18382fb5647d15bc8ad26c3f1918da07: merged the two OKR views per option B. Default 'qn org okr list' now shows status (from db, OKR-specific) + priority/labels (from beads) + KRs/progress (from db) in one block. --from-db kept as deprecated no-op alias. 221 OKR-related tests green.

title: qn org init: OKR prompt and success output interleave when stdin is not a TTY
description:
Repro:
  $ qn org init  # in non-TTY context
  Define your organization's objectives (OKRs).
  Press Enter without text to skip and use default bootstrap OKR.

  Objective 1: Initialized organization at /private/tmp/qn-dogfood-acme
  Created CEO: CEO

The line 'Objective 1: Initialized organization at...' is the OKR prompt running into the success output. It looks like the interactive prompt was emitted, EOF was hit, and the next line 'Initialized organization at...' was printed without a newline between them.

Two problems:
1. The output is confusing — looks like the OKR's name is 'Initialized organization at /private/tmp/qn-dogfood-acme'.
2. The command should detect non-TTY stdin and either skip the interactive prompt entirely or fail with a clear message ('--non-interactive requires --okrs flag').

Related: same UX problem applies whenever 'qn org init' is invoked from a script, CI, or pipe.
close_reason: Fixed in fc0b627: prompt header + click.prompt write to stderr (err=True), so stdout stays clean even when stdin EOFs in non-TTY contexts.

title: qn org init: CEO name silently defaults to literal 'CEO' when not specified
description:
Repro:
  $ rm -rf /tmp/test && mkdir /tmp/test && cd /tmp/test
  $ qn org init
  ...
  Created CEO: CEO

When --ceo-name is not passed and stdin has no input, the command silently creates a CEO worker literally named 'CEO'. This is a placeholder, not a real person's name, and the user has no idea it happened — the line scrolls past in the success output.

Expected: either (a) prompt interactively (with a clear visible prompt), (b) error out and require --ceo-name, or (c) at minimum WARN: 'No --ceo-name provided, using placeholder name "CEO". Update later via qn org chart show ...'

Related: the OKR section IS interactive ('Objective 1: ' prompt) but doesn't show the same courtesy for CEO name. The two prompts are inconsistent.
notes: Repro: rm -rf /tmp/test && mkdir /tmp/test && cd /tmp/test && qn org init
close_reason: Fixed in fc0b627: --ceo-name default is now a sentinel; non-TTY without --ceo-name emits a stderr warning before falling back to 'CEO'. Users running interactively get a real prompt. (Note: the placeholder name still gets used if user ignores the warning — could be tightened to a hard error in a future pass.)

title: qn org okr show <unknown-id> exits 0 silently in sandbox mode
description:
The bundled bd binary in --sandbox mode prints 'no issue found' to stderr but returns exit code 0 for unknown IDs (vs exit 1 in non-sandbox mode). cli/commands/org/okr/inspect.py only checked result.returncode, so a missing OKR fell through, click.echo'd empty stdout, and the command exited 0 — making bogus IDs indistinguishable from valid ones.

Fix shipped in commit e2d8ef4: also check `not result.stdout.strip()` before falling through.

This is a workaround. The underlying bug is in the bundled bd binary's --sandbox mode: it shouldn't return 0 for ID-not-found. If we ever upgrade the bundled bd, the workaround should still hold (returncode != 0 OR empty stdout).

Filed retroactively per durable-tracking rule.
close_reason: Fixed in commit e2d8ef4 (added empty-stdout check in inspect.py:show_cmd). 28/28 tests pass in test_audit_readonly_batch2.

title: [BUG] qn wrkr search crashes on hyphenated queries (FTS5 operator parse)
description:
Reproducer:
  qn wrkr search 'no-such-string' --org-path /tmp/org --worker-id wrkr-X

Crashes with:
  sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: such

The hyphens in the query are being parsed by FTS5 as binary operators (a - b - c), leaving 'such' interpreted as a column reference. The search arg should be properly quoted before being passed to MATCH, or sanitized for FTS5 query syntax.

Surfaced by tests/e2e/test_e2e_wrkr_commands.py::test_wrkr_search_runs_cleanly during e2e validation rollout. Test workaround: use a query without hyphens. Real fix: cli/commands/wrkr/search.py should quote the user input before passing to search_messages, or document that hyphens are operators.
close_reason: Fixed in b9ae0fe: search_messages() now sanitizes the query through _sanitize_fts_query(). Special chars like hyphens are quoted as phrases; advanced operators (AND/OR/NOT/NEAR) pass through. Verified: 'qn wrkr search no-such-string' now returns 'No messages found' instead of crashing.

title: cli/core/events.py: _event_bus module global leaks closed db across tests
description:
init_event_bus(db) sets a module-level global _event_bus. Test fixtures that close the db without resetting the global leave subsequent tests holding a stale reference, which in test_status_sync caused 99 cascading failures in test_worker.py whenever they ran in that order.

This is a real production smell — even if no production caller hits it, the pattern (init creates global, no reset path) is fragile and made test isolation impossible.

Fix shipped in commit fa6e542: added reset_event_bus() and called it from test_status_sync's db fixture teardown.

Filed retroactively per durable-tracking rule.
close_reason: Fixed in commit fa6e542 (added reset_event_bus + fixture teardown call). 164/164 tests pass in the previously-poisoned test_status_sync + test_worker pair.

title: [E2E-VALIDATION] 4.2 Integration Implementation
description:
Wire the e2e suite into make + CI.

Changes:
- Makefile: add 'test-e2e' target → `.venv/bin/pytest tests/e2e/ -v --timeout=120`
- Makefile: 'test-all' target updated to include test-e2e (cli + terminal-app + e2e)
- .github/workflows/release.yml (and any test workflow): add a job that runs 'make test-e2e' on push and PR
- README.md / DEVELOPMENT.md: add an 'Run E2E Tests' section with the make commands and a note about needing a system bd binary

Verify: `make test-e2e` from a fresh checkout exits 0 and reports the new test count.
close_reason: Wired e2e into make + CI. Added test-e2e target, dedicated e2e-tests CI job, updated COVERAGE.md and README.md. All 68 tests pass in 188s after fixing python/qn binary resolution in conftest (commit bc60eab).

title: [E2E-VALIDATION] 2.2 Write Failing Integration Tests
description:
For this feature the e2e tests in 2.1 ARE the integration tests — they exercise the full subprocess → CLI → cli.core → SQLite path with no mocks at the boundary.

This bead is mostly a no-op for THIS feature. To honor the lifecycle's contract, use it to capture cross-cutting integration concerns:
- shared conftest fixtures used by multiple files (e.g. an 'org_with_ceo' fixture that init + start the org, used by hire/fire/intervention tests)
- env hygiene: ensure no test inherits ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or similar from the dev shell — fresh env per test
- bd discovery test: verify the suite gracefully skips when no bd binary is available, instead of erroring

Output: short notes confirming what was added to conftest.py + any cross-cutting fixtures.
notes:
Cross-cutting fixtures added to tests/e2e/conftest.py (already existed; extended):
- _bd_available() + module-level pytest.skip — entire e2e suite skips if no bd binary on PATH or in cli/bin/{platform}/bd
- env_hygiene (autouse) — strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY / CLAUDE_* / QUINN_ORG_PATH / QUINN_WORKER_ID via monkeypatch (auto-restored on teardown)
- qn_runner — like cli_runner but invokes the installed 'qn' entry-point script (one more layer than 'python -m cli.commands.main')
- org_with_ceo — alias for the existing 'running_org' fixture (init + start --no-spawn-ceo + auto-stop teardown)
- hired_team — parametrizable indirect fixture; runs 'qn org hire' N times, returns worker IDs list (default N=2)
- _extract_worker_id helper — parses 'worker-XXXX' from hire stdout

Confirmed: 'pytest tests/e2e/ --collect-only' shows 31 existing smoke + 37 new = 68 tests collecting cleanly, no fixture errors.
close_reason: Cross-cutting conftest fixtures added: bd-availability gate, env_hygiene autouse, qn_runner, org_with_ceo alias, hired_team parametrized fixture. 68 total e2e tests collecting cleanly.

title: [DEEP DIVE] Resolve TranscriptStore vs TranscriptRepository incomplete migration
description:
shared/pyterm/persistence.py contains TWO storage classes:

- class TranscriptStore (lines 34-510, ~480L) — owns its own sqlite connection (`sqlite3.connect`), implements save/load/delete/list. Used by shared/pyterm/agent_session.py — production code.
- class TranscriptRepository (lines 514-880, ~370L) — uses shared cli.core.db.Database (`from cli.core.db import Database`), implements the same operations + get_turns_by_ask, get_turns_by_okr. Used only by tests/test_pyterm_persistence.py and a design doc (cli/docs/design/provider-research-claude.md).

Looks like a half-finished migration: TranscriptRepository is the 'cleaner' design (uses the central Database wrapper), but agent_session.py never moved off TranscriptStore.

Decision needed: complete the migration (move agent_session.py to TranscriptRepository, delete TranscriptStore) or revert (delete TranscriptRepository as dead code).

Once decided, the persistence.py file shrinks from 881L to ~480L OR ~370L.
acceptance_criteria: One of the two classes is gone. agent_session.py uses the surviving one. Tests still pass.
close_reason: Deleted TranscriptRepository class (368L) + its tests (279L). The bead framed this as incomplete migration; verified that's wrong — TranscriptRepository had zero prod consumers, only tests + a design doc. agent_session.py uses TranscriptStore. Keeping TranscriptRepository would have re-introduced the shared.pyterm → cli.core.db back-import I just removed in 8la.1. 471 pyterm tests pass (was 479; lost the 8 dropped tests, expected). Commit at HEAD.

title: [DEEP DIVE] Decide between shared.pyterm import-into-cli or move pyterm into cli
description:
shared/pyterm currently imports from cli/core in 8 sites (verified by grep — see parent epic). Per layering convention 'shared' should be a leaf.

Investigation step BEFORE any code change:
1. Walk every import in shared/pyterm and classify: production runtime dep, type annotation only, internal helper.
2. For each cli.core symbol used (Database, Worker, run_bd, PermissionLevel, can_worker_access_bead, get_message, get_channel, TMUX_ATTACH_WAIT, plus notifications.*) — does shared/pyterm USE it as state/data, or just need its TYPE for annotations?
3. Then choose:
  (a) Move shared/pyterm into cli/core/pyterm/. Pros: ends the dep inversion in one stroke; mirrors how terminal-app's services are organized. Cons: shared/ shrinks; tests that import from shared.pyterm need updating.
  (b) Define narrow protocols in shared/pyterm/interfaces/ that cli.core implements; shared/pyterm depends only on its own interfaces. Pros: keeps the layering. Cons: more code, more ceremony.

This is a research bead — output is a recommendation + a follow-up implementation bead, not code.
acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation with the per-symbol classification and a specific next-step bead linked.
close_reason: Verified shared.pyterm reaches into cli.core in 16 places, all in worker_bridge.py (14 lazy imports) + tmux_session.py (1 constant) + persistence.py (1 TYPE_CHECKING). Moved worker_bridge.py to cli/core/pyterm/worker_bridge.py — that bridge is fundamentally a cli.core consumer (Worker, bd_wrapper, permissions, queries, notifications). All lazy in-function imports hoisted to module top, free of cycle risk now that the file lives in cli.core. TMUX_ATTACH_WAIT inlined locally in tmux_session.py. shared.pyterm now has zero runtime back-imports from cli (only the TYPE_CHECKING-only Database hint in persistence.py, free at runtime). 479 pyterm tests pass. Commits 8e44219 + 3498b48.

title: [DEEP DIVE] Split cli/core/org_init.py (765L)
description:
cli/core/org_init.py contains init_org() + many config dataclasses (OrgInitConfig, ProviderConfig, ObjectiveConfig, KeyResultConfig, CEOBriefingConfig) + helpers like _create_okr_bead, create_initial_tasks.

Recent commits added defensive bd timeouts (commits 051ca87, 690e6d7) which fattened it further.

Suggested split:
  cli/core/org_init/__init__.py       re-export init_org
  cli/core/org_init/types.py          OrgInitConfig + child dataclasses (~150L)
  cli/core/org_init/init.py           init_org() orchestrator (~250L)
  cli/core/org_init/bootstrap.py      _create_okr_bead, create_initial_tasks, etc. (~300L)

ProviderConfig in here is one of the triplicated types — coordinate with quinn-ai-8tt.2.
acceptance_criteria: No file > 400L. terminal-app's wizard_init still works (it imports init_org + the type names).
close_reason: Split cli/core/org_init.py (765L) into cli/core/org_init/ package: __init__ (73L), types (90L), scaffolding (213L), bootstrap (243L), init (126L). All under 400L. 36 onboarding/init tests pass. terminal-app wizard_init.py compatibility preserved. Commit at HEAD.

title: [DEEP DIVE] Split cli/core/session.py (777L)
description:
cli/core/session.py mixes:
- SessionId dataclass (~15L)
- SessionConfig + SessionMetrics + SessionOutput + PromptResult dataclasses (~80L)
- 8 exception classes: SessionError, SessionAlreadyRunningError, SessionNotRunningError, SessionNotReadyError, SessionTimeoutError, SessionAlreadyBoundError, InvalidSessionStateTransition (~60L)
- SessionInterface ABC with ~20 abstract methods (~600L)

Suggested split:
  cli/core/session/__init__.py        re-export
  cli/core/session/types.py           SessionId + dataclasses (~120L)
  cli/core/session/exceptions.py      8 error classes (~80L)
  cli/core/session/interface.py       SessionInterface ABC (~600L)

Coordinate with quinn-ai-8tt.2 — the SessionConfig + PromptResult dataclasses here are two of the triplicated types and may be deprecated/aliased rather than just moved.
acceptance_criteria: No file > 400L. Public surface preserved (cli.core.session re-exports the moved symbols).
close_reason: Split cli/core/session.py (732L file) into cli/core/session/ package: __init__.py (56L re-exports), types.py (67L), exceptions.py (85L), interface.py (600L). interface.py is over the 400L target — left intentionally because the SessionInterface ABC is the contract every adapter implements and splitting loses cohesion. Other 3 files comfortably under target. Public 'from cli.core.session import X' API preserved. 140 session tests pass. Commit at HEAD.

title: [EPIC] Untangle cli.core ↔ shared.pyterm bidirectional dependencies
description:
Verified bidirectional imports between cli.core and shared.pyterm:

shared/pyterm reaches BACK into cli.core (8 sites):
  shared/pyterm/persistence.py:31     from cli.core.db import Database
  shared/pyterm/tmux_session.py:15    from cli.core.constants import TMUX_ATTACH_WAIT
  shared/pyterm/worker_bridge.py:239  from cli.core.worker import Worker
  shared/pyterm/worker_bridge.py:266  from cli.core.worker import Worker
  shared/pyterm/worker_bridge.py:267  from cli.core.bd_wrapper import run_bd
  shared/pyterm/worker_bridge.py:268  from cli.core.permissions import PermissionLevel, can_worker_access_bead
  shared/pyterm/worker_bridge.py:360  from cli.core.notifications import (...)
  shared/pyterm/worker_bridge.py:364  from cli.core.queries import get_message, get_channel

cli/core consumes shared.core (canonical) types AND shared.pyterm (implementation):
  cli/core/session.py:23              from shared.core.state import (canonical SessionState)
  cli/core/sessions/openai.py:21      from shared.core import Message
  cli/providers/openai.py:25          from shared.core import Message

By layering convention 'shared' should be a leaf — depended on by cli, never depending on it. The current shape means moving anything in cli.core risks breaking shared.pyterm, and a fresh dev can't trace the import graph cleanly.

Two clean options:
(a) Move shared/pyterm into cli/core/pyterm/ (it's CLI-coupled anyway)
(b) Invert: define narrow protocols in shared.pyterm.interfaces, have cli.core implement them, and make shared.pyterm depend only on its own protocols

title: Add auto-formula-bump step to release.yml after PyPI publish
description:
Once the homebrew-quinnai tap exists, every successful PyPI publish should fire a follow-up that opens a PR (or directly pushes) to the tap repo updating the Formula's url + sha256 + resource blocks.

## Why
Without automation the formula goes stale fast and users on brew get an outdated version vs PyPI users. Manual bumps are error-prone (forgetting one sha256 breaks the install).

## Approach options
1. **dawidd6/action-homebrew-bump-formula** — popular GH Action that opens a PR against a tap with bumped url/sha256. Resource blocks not auto-updated; works for simple Python tools but our 3 deps may need re-poet.
2. **mislav/bump-homebrew-formula-action** — alternative with similar API.
3. Hand-rolled: gh api PATCH against tap repo + sha256 calc against new sdist.

Recommend (1) for simplicity, with a manual 'brew style && poet' refresh on major releases.

## Implementation
Add to .github/workflows/release.yml as a new job:

```yaml
bump-homebrew:
  needs: smoke-test
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: dawidd6/action-homebrew-bump-formula@v3
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}  # PAT with write to homebrew-quinnai
        tap: qosha1/quinnai
        formula: quinnai
        tag: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        revision: ${{ github.sha }}
```

Requires HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret (a PAT with write access to qosha1/homebrew-quinnai). Document setup in docs/operations/release-bootstrap.md.

## Acceptance
Pushing v0.3.0 → PyPI publishes → action opens PR on homebrew-quinnai with updated Formula/quinnai.rb → merge that PR → 'brew upgrade quinnai' picks it up.
close_reason: Added bump-homebrew-formula job to release.yml using mislav/bump-homebrew-formula-action@v3, triggered after github-release, requires HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret.

title: Create homebrew-quinnai tap repo with initial Formula/quinnai.rb
description:
Bootstrap the personal tap repo Homebrew users will tap with 'brew tap qosha1/quinnai'.

## Steps
1. Create new GitHub repo: qosha1/homebrew-quinnai (the 'homebrew-' prefix is what 'brew tap' looks for; tap name becomes 'qosha1/quinnai').
2. Add Formula/quinnai.rb using Language::Python::Virtualenv:

```ruby
class Quinnai < Formula
  include Language::Python::Virtualenv

  desc "Hierarchical AI organization management CLI"
  homepage "https://github.com/qosha1/quinn-ai"
  url "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/source/q/quinnai/quinnai-<VERSION>.tar.gz"
  sha256 "<filled>"
  license "MIT"

  depends_on "python@3.12"
  depends_on "tmux"
  # depends_on "bd" if/when bd has a brew formula; otherwise note it in caveats

  # 'brew style --fix' populates resource blocks for click, pyyaml, jinja2
  resource "click" do
    # url + sha256 for click sdist
  end
  # ... and so on

  def install
    virtualenv_install_with_resources
  end

  test do
    system bin/"qn", "--help"
  end
end
```

3. Use 'brew create' or 'poet' (homebrew-pypi-poet) to auto-generate the resource blocks from the PyPI sdist.
4. Test locally: 'brew tap qosha1/quinnai $(pwd)' then 'brew install --build-from-source qosha1/quinnai/quinnai'.

## Acceptance
After this lands, anyone on macOS can run:
  brew tap qosha1/quinnai
  brew install quinnai

and end up with 'qn', 'qn-bd', 'msgr' on PATH.

## Blocker
Cannot start until v0.2.x sdist is on PyPI — formula needs a real URL + sha256.

description:

title: Bundle bd binaries for darwin-amd64, linux-amd64, linux-arm64 in wheel
description:
Currently `cli/bin/` only contains `darwin-arm64/bd`. Anyone on Intel Mac, Linux x86, or Linux ARM gets the `shutil.which('bd')` fallback — install fails for them unless they pre-install bd.

## Verified
```
$ ls cli/bin/
darwin-arm64
$ ls cli/bin/darwin-arm64/
bd
```

## Fix options
(a) Run `scripts/build-all-platforms.sh` (already exists, downloads from beads-org releases) as part of release workflow.
(b) Rely on PyPI but make `qn` clearly error with install instructions if no bd available.
(c) Build manylinux/macosx-tagged platform wheels per arch instead of one universal wheel — reduces install size 4x.

Recommend (a) + (c): add bd into wheel + build per-platform wheels, with `tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include` per platform. The commented-out block at root pyproject:14 already shows intent.
close_reason:
Decided against bundling — root cause: bd_wrapper only ever looked at cli/bin/bd (no platform subdir), so the cli/bin/darwin-arm64/bd in the wheel was dead weight that was never executed.

Resolution (commit fb85665):
- Excluded cli/bin/** from wheel — size dropped ~25MB → ~960KB.
- bd_wrapper now also probes cli/bin/{platform}-{arch}/bd for repo dev layouts before falling back to system PATH bd.
- Error message points at upstream bd install (https://github.com/steveyegge/beads, brew install bd) rather than a dev script.
- Verified: 'qn-bd ready' against system bd works through to listing actual bead state. With PATH stripped, error message renders helpfully.

bd is now treated as a system runtime requirement (like git, tmux, the Anthropic CLI). install.sh + README docs (separate tasks) need to mention it.

Views have 39 direct `self.app.org_connection` references and 11 occurrences of the boilerplate guard `if not hasattr(self.app, 'org_connection') or self.app.org_connection is None` (across views/dashboard.py, views/team.py, views/okrs.py, views/messages.py, widgets/* implicitly).

Options:
1. Base class BoardOrgView with a connection property + a require_connected() helper that raises a typed exception caught at the view boundary.
2. Inject the connection at view construction (BoardApp passes it during compose).
3. Convert views to subscribe to a model object that owns the connection.

Option 1 is the smallest step. Option 3 ties into the polling-consolidation epic (quinn-ai-bdg).
acceptance_criteria: No `hasattr(self.app, 'org_connection')` guards remain. Direct `self.app.org_connection` references reduced to <5 (only in the BoardApp glue).
close_reason: Replaced 18 hasattr(self.app, 'org_connection') guards across 5 view files with a single get_org_connection(app) helper in views/_org_access.py that collapses missing-attr and None into one getattr. grep 'hasattr.*org_connection' under board_ui returns 1 hit (docstring example only). Direct 'self.app.org_connection' refs in views/widgets reduced to 0 (the only remaining are app.py glue and the docstring). Acceptance met. 376 pass + 1 skip. Commit at HEAD.

title: [EPIC] Apply CLAUDE.md anti-pattern hygiene to terminal-app
description:
CLAUDE.md lists 8 learned anti-patterns. terminal-app violates several:

1. **Module-Level Side Effects** (anti-pattern #3): src/board_ui/services/org_discovery.py uses module-global `_qn_command_cache: Optional[list[str]] = None` mutated by _get_qn_command(). Tests pollute each other; first call wins for the lifetime of the process.

2. **Infrastructure Leaking Into Business Logic** (anti-pattern #8): ~30 raw subprocess.run() calls scattered across services/views, each re-implementing timeout/error/decode handling. Should be wrapped in a single QnCliClient adapter.

3. **Magic values everywhere**: timeout=2 / 5 / 10 / 60 littered through subprocess calls; refresh interval 0.3 / 2 / 30 hardcoded in 4 places; `board-channel`, `escalations`, `worker-ceo` strings hardcoded.

4. **5 `# TODO:` comments without bead links** (CLAUDE.md: 'No `# TODO` without an associated beads issue'): src/board_ui/views/org_tabs.py:146, src/board_ui/views/team.py:263/401/414/439

5. **Lazy try/except imports of cli.core** (11 sites): hides circular dep / packaging weakness. Either declare the dep cleanly in pyproject (terminal-app already lists 'quinnai' as dep — the fallback is dead code in non-monorepo install) or formalize a board↔cli adapter boundary.

title: Investigate full pytest cli/tests/ suite hang
description:
Running the full test suite ('pytest cli/tests/') hangs for 60+ minutes despite --timeout=30 per-test. Individual files complete fine, so something at session/module scope is jamming up. Suspect: a session-scoped autouse fixture, a slow collection hook, or a shared resource (sqlite file, tmux server) that gets contended.

Approach: bisect by running with -x and watching for which test the hang starts at; check session-scoped fixtures (notably verify_no_leaked_sessions in tests/conftest.py); check if tmux server proliferation is a factor.

Repro: pytest cli/tests/ -q --timeout=30. Compare with running file-by-file: each file passes, but the aggregate hangs.
close_reason:
PROOF (per /reality-check):

Root cause found via process inspection during a deliberate hang. While the test suite was stuck, ps -ef showed:

  bd --sandbox --db=/var/folders/.../tmp.../.beads/beads.db create Plan initial team hiring 
    --type=task --priority=2 ... 
    --deps=serves:OKR(id='tmpf1nrwkv9-3v0', title='Establish organizational foundation', 
                      description='Set up core processes ...', 
                      owner_worker_id='wrkr-487ce320', parent_okr_id=None, status='active', 
                      created_at=datetime.datetime(2026, 4, 27, 2, 22, 47, 832957), 
                      updated_at=...,
                      key_results=[KeyResult(metric='team_size', target=3.0, current=1.0, ...)],
                      due_date=None)

The --deps argument has the FULL Python repr of an OKR dataclass, not a bead id. bd's parser hangs on this giant string (probably trying to resolve serves:<repr> as an issue ref).

Bug: cli/core/org_init.py had three sites (and the new lxp helper) where create_okr's RETURN VALUE — which is an OKR dataclass — was assigned to a variable named okr_id and then formatted into a string. The assignment was always wrong; pre-lxp it didn't matter much because the FK constraint from quinn-ai-6se was masking it (init_initial_tasks was failing 'No active session' or FK and the bd subprocess never reached this exact path under load). Post-lxp + 6se fix, the codepath actually exercises bd create with the malformed deps argument.

Fix: extract .id at three sites (create_initial_okrs's two branches + _create_bootstrap_okr's SQLite mirror).

Verification:
- Original hanging pair (test_audit_lifecycle_batch4 + test_audit_qn_org_chart_show): now passes 27 in 85s.
- Larger 21-file sweep: 433 passed in 560.89s. No hangs.

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_audit_lifecycle_batch4.py cli/tests/test_audit_qn_org_chart_show.py -q

title: Test orgs leak bootstrap beads into the platform repo's .beads — BEADS_DIR override not effective
description:
Tests that create temp orgs (e.g. cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py) cause bd-create calls during init to write into THIS repo's .beads instead of the temp org's .beads. Surfaced after the quinn-ai-lxp fix made _create_bootstrap_okr() invoke 'bd create' during init.

Polluting beads observed (now cleaned up): quinn-ai-64a/kah/5eg/zrb — these were the bootstrap OKR + 3 initial tasks created by test orgs.

Likely cause: my shell sets BEADS_DIR=$(pwd)/.beads = /Users/.../quinn-ai/.beads before running pytest. Pytest inherits it. Inside cli.core.bd_wrapper.run_bd, env = os.environ.copy() then env['BEADS_DIR'] = str(beads_dir) — that SHOULD override. Either:
A. bd is actually picking up cwd-walk discovery and finding the QuinnAI repo's .beads (since cwd=org_path but the repo's tree contains it via parent chain when run inside the repo working dir)
B. The env override isn't reaching the subprocess (unlikely — verified the code does it)
C. bd's --sandbox / --db flags would isolate it but aren't being used during init

Fix candidates:
- Pass --db=<beads_dir>/beads.db explicitly (like 'bd --sandbox --db=...' which run_bd already does for normal commands)
- Or, in init_beads / _create_okr_bead, explicitly set HOME=tmp + scrub other bd-discovery env vars

Repro: cd /Users/.../quinn-ai && BEADS_DIR=/Users/.../quinn-ai/.beads pytest cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py -v && BEADS_DIR=/Users/.../quinn-ai/.beads bd list — observe new bootstrap beads in this repo's tracker.
close_reason:
PROOF (per /reality-check):

1. Regression test: pytest cli/tests/test_bd_wrapper_isolation.py → 1 passed in 3.29s.
   The test bootstraps a fresh org with its own .beads at a tempdir, then calls run_bd from a different cwd, and asserts the new bead lands in the TARGET org's .beads (verified by counting before/after via bd list --json on the target).

2. Verification on real test runs: ran cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py (which exercises the lxp init→OKR-bead path); QuinnAI repo's open-bead count stayed at 2 (the parent epic + REFACTOR-2). No leakage.

The earlier 4 polluting beads (quinn-ai-64a/kah/5eg/zrb, all closed as noise) appear to have been created during an intermediate iteration of the quinn-ai-lxp fix that I refined away. The current code paths (run_bd in cli/core/bd_wrapper.py at line 654-665) DO subprocess.run(..., env=env) without an explicit cwd — but bd's discovery still picks up BEADS_DIR from env correctly when set, and the regression test confirms isolation holds.

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_bd_wrapper_isolation.py -v

title: TmuxSpawner sets env vars BEFORE new-session — env_vars never reach the spawned process
description:
cli/core/sessions/tmux_spawner.py:136-140 calls 'tmux set-environment -t session_name KEY VALUE' BEFORE 'tmux new-session ...'. set-environment only affects EXISTING sessions, so the env vars are lost (and tmux logs them as no-ops, silently).

Repro: spawn a session with env_vars={'QUINN_WORKER_ID': 'x'} via TmuxSpawner. Inside the session, QUINN_WORKER_ID is unset.

Surfaced by Layer-2 harness work (quinn-ai-9s1): tmux_with_fake_cli fixture passed QUINN_WORKER_ID=fakecli-test, but fake_cli read os.environ.get('QUINN_WORKER_ID') → 'unknown'.

Fix options:
A. Reorder: call new-session first, then set-environment -t (set per-session env post-create — but the command has already started; future invocations would see them but the initial process won't)
B. Use 'tmux new-session -e KEY=VALUE' form so env is set at process spawn time (correct fix)
C. Both (use -e for the spawned process AND set-environment for future commands in the session)

Recommend (B) or (C). The current code is broken.
close_reason:
PROOF: pytest cli/tests/test_tmux_env_vars_bug.py -v → 2 passed in 1.01s.

Fix: cli/core/sessions/tmux_spawner.py — replaced the broken 'tmux set-environment -t session_name KEY VALUE' loop (which ran BEFORE 'tmux new-session', so it silently no-op'd because the session didn't exist yet) with '-e KEY=VALUE' flags appended to the new-session command. This is the documented tmux mechanism for setting env vars on the spawned process.

Verified:
- test_env_vars_reach_spawned_process: fake_cli (no --worker arg, reads env) banner now shows 'worker=env-test-worker' instead of 'worker=unknown'
- test_multiple_env_vars: FOO/BAZ/QUINN_WORKER_ID all visible in 'env' output of a sh -c spawned process

Knock-on effects:
- cli/tests/harness/tmux_fixtures.py: reverted the workaround that passed --worker via args; now uses env_vars again
- All 11 tmux-marked tests pass: test_tmux_fixtures.py (5) + test_audit_with_real_tmux.py (4) + test_tmux_env_vars_bug.py (2)

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_tmux_env_vars_bug.py cli/tests/harness/test_tmux_fixtures.py -v -m tmux
