title: SessionConfig missing welcome_message field — broke spawn_worker_session
description:
spawn_worker_session in cli/commands/org/session_utils.py:36 passes welcome_message=... to SessionConfig(), but cli/core/session.py:65's SessionConfig didn't declare that field. Caller would crash with: TypeError: SessionConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'welcome_message'.

Note shared/core/session.py:123 has welcome_message; the cli SessionConfig is a parallel/duplicate definition that drifted.

FIX (in working tree, uncommitted): added 'welcome_message: Optional[str] = None' field to cli/core/session.py SessionConfig. Verified: hire flow now gets past this point.

Followup architectural question: should cli/core/session.py:SessionConfig and shared/core/session.py:SessionConfig be deduplicated? Two separate definitions for the same concept smells. test_worker.py:908 references config.welcome_message so we know callers expect it.
close_reason: Already fixed in working tree alongside l3o: added 'welcome_message: Optional[str] = None' to cli/core/session.py SessionConfig dataclass. Verified: hire now proceeds past the SessionConfig kwarg error (reaches the budget-allocation check, which is a separate issue tracked as quinn-ai-41v). Architectural dedupe of cli/core/session.py:SessionConfig vs shared/core/session.py:SessionConfig still worth doing as a separate effort.

title: Provider selection rejects claude_code: 'No provider can satisfy cost=50, capabilities=[]'
description:
After hiring alice with --cost 50, the post-hire session start fails:
  Warning: Failed to start session: No provider can satisfy cost=50, capabilities=[]

Repro:
  qn --org-path /tmp/test org hire --name alice --role engineer --manager <ceo-id> --cost 50

Default providers.yaml has claude_code enabled (api_key: not-needed-uses-system-auth), and 'qn org provider list' shows claude_code's capabilities (shell, file_edit, ...). So a provider IS available, but selection logic rejects it.

Suspect: select_provider_for_worker() in cli/providers/registry/selection.py expects a 'cost' field in providers.yaml that the default template doesn't set. With cost=50 (mid-tier 'standard'), and no provider declaring its tier, no provider matches.

Either: (a) default claude_code to satisfy any cost/capability when no constraints are set, (b) add explicit cost/tier fields to default providers.yaml template, (c) make selection fall back to first enabled provider when nothing else matches.
close_reason:
Fixed cli/commands/org/hire.py _start_workday_for_hire(): when registry.select_for_worker() raises ValueError (no enabled API providers), fall back to the org's session default by reading providers.yaml directly (load_providers_config().default).

Root cause: providers.yaml's 'default: claude_code' wasn't picked up by the API ProviderRegistry because claude_code is a session-CLI adapter (not registered as an API Provider class). The default template ships with anthropic/openai both 'enabled: false', so the registry was empty and select_for_worker() always raised. Verified at /tmp/quinn-test: hire now picks claude_code as fallback and proceeds (eve, frank were hired successfully).

Surfaced two cascading bugs in the next phases of session spawn: (1) SessionConfig missing welcome_message field — filed and fixed; (2) hire auto-spawn fails when no budget allocation exists — filed as UX gap.

Architectural followup (not in scope): the providers.yaml file conflates two concepts — session-CLI adapters (claude_code, codex, gemini) and API providers (anthropic, openai). Cost/capability selection is meaningful only for the latter. Future cleanup should either split the config or unify the registries.

title: qn org hire --manager accepts only worker ID, not name (docs say either)
description:
Running 'qn org hire --name alice --role engineer --manager ceo' crashes with WorkerNotFound: 'ceo'. The lookup at cli/commands/org/hire.py:102 calls Worker.get(db, manager) which only resolves by id; passing a role/name fails.

Help text and README claim '--manager TEXT  Manager name or ID (required)'. Either:

title: qn org init logs FOREIGN KEY constraint failed when creating initial tasks
description:
On a fresh init (qn --org-path /tmp/foo org init --ceo-name=X --skip-okrs), the output includes:
  Failed to create initial tasks: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
  CEO will need to create tasks manually from OKRs

Init still completes and the org is usable, but the seeding step is broken. Likely the initial-task creator references a row that hasn't been written yet (OKR? worker?). With --skip-okrs there's no OKR record to FK against, which would explain it. Either (a) skip task seeding when --skip-okrs is set, or (b) FK against the bootstrap OKR that --skip-okrs is supposed to create.
notes:
## Root cause

`create_initial_okrs()` (cli/core/org_init.py:344) writes the OKR to the SQLite `okrs` table only — the id is generated as 'okr-xxx' via generate_id().

`create_initial_tasks()` (org_init.py:489) then runs `bd create --deps=serves:okr-xxx` which expects 'okr-xxx' to be an existing bead. It isn't — it's only an SQLite row. bd's FK constraint (in the dolt issue graph) fails.

This is true on EVERY init regardless of --skip-okrs (with --skip-okrs the bootstrap OKR is still created at org_init.py:444 `_create_bootstrap_okr()`, then the task seeding hits the same FK).

## Design question

Per CLAUDE.md: 'OKRs are beads with label okr (not a type); work items link via serves dependency'. So the design intent IS that OKRs live in beads. The SQLite okrs table appears to be a parallel denormalized cache (queryable progress, KR JSON). `qn org okr link <task> <okr>` (commands/org/okr.py:730) runs `bd dep add task okr --type serves` — confirming OKRs are expected to exist as beads.

## Fix options
A. Drop `--deps=serves:` from create_initial_tasks args. Tasks are created but orphaned (no link to OKR). Smallest change, loses the link.
B. Also create OKR as a bead in create_initial_okrs (and use the bead id as the SQLite okr_id). Correct but touches two store layers.
C. Move OKRs to beads-only and treat the SQLite okrs table as a derived view. Largest change, cleanest architecture.

Recommend B for this bug; track C as a follow-up architecture decision.
## Additional repro from quinn-ai-l3h walk-through

Running 'qn org okr set --title "Q2 Beta launch" --owner ceo' against /tmp/quinn-test produced:

  ✓ Created issue: quinn-test-epv — Q2 Beta launch
  Failed to store OKR in database (ignored): FOREIGN KEY constraint failed

So the FK problem is pervasive:
- qn org okr set: bd create succeeds, SQLite write fails (ignored)
- qn org init: SQLite write succeeds, bd dep references fail (warned)

After 'qn org okr set':
- 'qn org okr list' (reads beads) — shows quinn-test-epv (the new OKR)
- 'qn org okr list --from-db' (reads SQLite) — shows okr-082f4304 (bootstrap from init)

The two stores hold disjoint sets of OKRs. This is worse than 'broken init' — it means OKR data integrity is lost on every write. Recommendation: pick one store as authoritative. Option B from earlier note (store both, share id) is the right minimal fix. Option C (beads-only, kill the okrs table) would resolve this entire class of bug.
close_reason:
Found and fixed the actual FK violator — it was NOT about OKR/bd dual-store as the bead title implied. Root causes:

1. cli/core/org_init.py:540 (init flow): create_initial_tasks passed worker_id='system' to run_bd, which then tried to insert an activity_signals row with worker_id='system'. activity_signals.worker_id has FK to workers.id; 'system' is not a worker. Fix: use ceo_id instead. The CEO exists in the workers table, so the audit trail FK now holds.

2. cli/commands/org/okr.py:306 (qn org okr set): the --owner flag's default value 'ceo' fell through the resolver as a literal string 'ceo' which was used as okrs.owner_worker_id — fails FK to workers.id. Fix: resolution chain now tries get_worker_by_name → Worker.get(by id) → Org(db).ceo_worker_id (when literal == 'ceo'), and skips the SQLite mirror with a warning instead of attempting the FK-doomed insert.

Both verified at /tmp/6se-verify: fresh init clean, no warnings; 'qn org okr set --owner ceo' creates the bead AND the SQLite row in the same id. Stores now agree on user-created OKRs.

Filed as separate followup: bootstrap OKR (created during init via _create_bootstrap_okr) still exists only in SQLite, not beads — different gap.

title: qn init: bd init deadlocks on macOS without coreutils (FIXED — verify and close)
description:
init_beads() in cli/core/org_init.py was calling bare 'bd init', which (a) installs a pre-commit hook, then (b) makes a git commit that triggers it, (c) the hook calls 'bd hooks run pre-commit' which deadlocks on the dolt db lock held by the parent bd init. The hook script's timeout(1) fallback isn't on macOS by default, so there's no escape.

FIX (in working tree, uncommitted): pass --skip-hooks --non-interactive to bd init. See cli/core/org_init.py:302.

Fresh init at /tmp/aa3-verify completed cleanly; .beads/hooks/ is absent (skip-hooks worked); bd list inside the new org returns OK. Patch is in working tree, will land with the broader cleanup commit.

title: [BUG] Workers treat explicit 'please pick up X' DMs as suggestions, ask CEO for confirmation instead of acting
description:
Live observation, StartSimpli canary 2026-04-29.

CEO sent frontend-eng a clear directive DM:
  'Great work on raise-simpli-3er! Next up — please pick up raise-simpli-epe (useCalendarEvents auto-paginate via next URL). It's marked P2 but it's the last KR on OKR quinnai-nkr.'

After being nudged to check inbox, frontend-eng read the DM, summarized the situation accurately, then ENDED with:
  'Want me to proceed with raise-simpli-epe (auto-paginate hook) per the CEO's directive?'

Then went idle waiting for an answer. Net effect: 0 progress on raise-simpli-epe, blocking the last KR on OKR quinnai-nkr until the CEO is nudged AGAIN to read the inbox AGAIN to answer.

This compounds quinn-ai-srwt: the CEO doesn't auto-poll, and now even when nudged, the cycle re-blocks because the worker asks for confirmation instead of executing the direction.

Real-world equivalent: a direct report who treats every assignment as 'should I really do this?' rather than executing.

Fix options:
  (a) BRIEFING.md instruction strengthening: 'when your manager DMs you a directive starting with verbs like please/take/pick-up/start, EXECUTE it; do NOT respond with a confirmation question. Confirmation Q's are for ambiguous direction or scope changes.'
  (b) Route 'directive' DMs through a different channel that prompts the worker to act vs. discuss.
  (c) Train via repeated runs (model behavior; no code change).

Recommend (a) — a few-shot example in BRIEFING.md showing a directive DM and the correct 'started' confirmation reply rather than a 'should I?' question.

Same pattern was NOT exhibited by backend-eng on the same nudge — they Acked + acted immediately. Behavior is per-worker / per-task ambiguity, not deterministic, but plausible enough to harden against.
close_reason: BRIEFING.md.jinja2 + INITIAL_TASK.md: added explicit 'Want me to proceed?' anti-pattern with before/after example. Workers now get concrete negative example of the org-stalling confirmation question at both boot and in briefing.

title: [BUG] SQLite uses Python 3.12-deprecated default datetime adapter — floods test output with DeprecationWarning
description:
Every test run emits hundreds of:
  /Users/qosha/Repos/ai/quinn-ai/cli/core/db/connection.py:183: DeprecationWarning: The default datetime adapter is deprecated as of Python 3.12; see the sqlite3 documentation for suggested replacement recipes

cli/core/db/connection.py:74 uses 'detect_types=sqlite3.PARSE_DECLTYPES | sqlite3.PARSE_COLNAMES' which activates Python's legacy default datetime/date adapter+converter. Python 3.12+ deprecated those in favor of explicit registration.

Fix: register custom adapters in cli/core/db/connection.py module init:
  - sqlite3.register_adapter(datetime, lambda v: v.isoformat())
  - sqlite3.register_adapter(date, lambda v: v.isoformat())
  - sqlite3.register_converter('DATETIME', lambda b: datetime.fromisoformat(b.decode()))
  - sqlite3.register_converter('DATE', lambda b: date.fromisoformat(b.decode()))

The codebase runs Python 3.14 so this warning will become an error in a future release.
close_reason: Fixed in b374b703b4daad83b68e1597f7c05f4940e7e7cc: registered explicit datetime/date adapters and DATETIME/TIMESTAMP/DATE converters in cli/core/db/connection.py module init. 245 tests pass with -W error::DeprecationWarning (was emitting hundreds of warnings per run).

title: [BUG] State name drift: code has 'offboarding' / 'working' / 'blocked' but spec STATEMACHINES.md doesn't
description:
State-machine validation gap (still failing as of 2026-04-28 sweep).

Code (shared/state_machines.py):
  LIFECYCLE_STATES = {'pending', 'onboarding', 'active', 'offboarding', 'suspended', 'terminated'}
  RUNTIME_STATES = {'starting', 'running', 'idle', 'working', 'blocked', 'crashed', 'stopped'}

Spec (STATEMACHINES.md):
  Worker lifecycle: pending, onboarding, active, suspended, terminated  (NO 'offboarding')
  Session runtime: documented states don't include 'working'/'blocked' transition machinery

So:
- 'offboarding' exists in code as a real intermediate state (mid-termination), but the spec doesn't mention it. Spec is incomplete.
- 'working' and 'blocked' exist in RUNTIME_STATES but no automatic transition machinery — assign_task() / mark_blocked() methods don't exist.

Repro covered by 2 xfailed tests:
  cli/tests/test_worker_lifecycle_state_machine.py::TestWorkerStates::test_states_match_specification
    asserts LIFECYCLE_STATES == {'pending', 'onboarding', 'active', 'suspended', 'terminated'} (no 'offboarding')

  cli/tests/test_session_lifecycle_state_machine.py::TestSessionT4RunningToWorking::test_t4_transition_to_working
    expects worker.assign_task(task_id) which doesn't exist; expects auto-transition to 'working'

Decision needed:
A. **Spec wins**: remove 'offboarding' from LIFECYCLE_STATES, remove 'working'/'blocked' from RUNTIME_STATES if they have no machinery.
B. **Code wins**: update STATEMACHINES.md to document 'offboarding' (as part of termination flow) and either implement the working/blocked transitions or document them as 'reserved-for-future'.

Recommend B for offboarding (it's a real state, spec is just incomplete). For working/blocked, recommend removing them from RUNTIME_STATES until there's a use case — they're unused.

From docs/validation/state-machine-validation-2026-01-25.md (still applicable).
close_reason: Fixed in e9df25d0b343d852e9feec0ab9f983577353d67c: code wins for offboarding (real state — spec updated to document it); spec wins for working/blocked (vestigial — stripped from RUNTIME_STATES). 87 state-machine tests pass / 4 xfail; full state_sequences suite (49 tests) passes; broader regression suite green at 4294 passed.

title: [BUG] Org.start() resume (T4) doesn't spawn CEO session — inconsistent with first-start (T2)
description:
State-machine validation gap (still failing as of 2026-04-28 sweep).

The Python API Org.start() updates org status but doesn't spawn any CEO session — session spawning happens only in the CLI orchestrator (cli/core/org_start_controller.py). This means:

- First-start (T2: initialized → running): works because CLI orchestrator runs after Python state transition.
- Resume (T4: stopped → running): if invoked via Python API directly, ends in 'running' state with no CEO session.

Repro covered by 2 xfailed tests:
  cli/tests/test_org_lifecycle_state_machine.py::TestOrgT4StoppedToRunning::test_t4_consistent_with_t2
  cli/tests/test_state_machine_dependencies.py::TestConsistencyC1OrgResumeBehavior::test_c1_resume_spawns_ceo_session_like_first_start

Decision needed:
A. Move session spawning into Org.start() Python API so any caller (CLI, scripts, tests) gets consistent behavior.
B. Document that Org.start() is just a state transition; session spawning is the CLI orchestrator's responsibility. Update STATEMACHINES.md spec accordingly.
C. Add a separate Org.resume() method that handles session spawning while Org.start() stays minimal.

Recommend B (matches current architecture) — but require the spec update.

From docs/validation/state-machine-validation-2026-01-25.md (still applicable).
close_reason: Fixed in ed9eb72cf5d95c5bc550f85f790e2f211656684b: documented the Python-API-vs-orchestrator layering in STATEMACHINES.md and inverted the 2 xfailed tests to pin the deliberate Python-API contract (no session spawn). Result: 91 pass / 0 xfail across all 4 state-machine test files.

title: [BUG] Org.start() has no rollback if CEO activation fails — leaves inconsistent state
description:
State-machine validation gap (still failing as of 2026-04-28 sweep).

If Org.start() / Org.start() flow encounters a failure between mid-transition states (e.g., CEO.complete_onboarding() raises), the org's status may already be 'running' but the CEO is still 'pending'. No rollback / try-except / transaction wrapping.

A. Add transaction wrapper around the Org.start() Python API (begin → commit | rollback on exception).
B. Document that Org.start() is not transactional and rely on the CLI orchestrator (org_start_controller) to handle phase failures (which it already does to some extent).

Recommend B + tighten the orchestrator: less code change, the CLI is already the canonical orchestration layer. Spec (STATEMACHINES.md) would need updating to reflect this.

title: Worker runtime_status='crashed' when tmux session is actually alive
description:
After 'tmux kill-server' (and presumably any other tmux-server-level event),
worker_state.runtime_status is set to 'crashed' but the worker's actual
tmux session may have been recreated by a subsequent 'qn org start'.

Repro:
  qn org init/start, hire Bob
  tmux kill-server  # simulates external event
  qn org start --worker Bob   # respawns tmux session
  qn org status              # shows CEO crashed even though tmux exists

Concretely seen in /tmp/qn-dogfood-5:
  $ tmux ls
  qn-wrkr-cc875efb (Quinn): present
  qn-wrkr-f2e6366c (Bob): present
  $ sqlite3 quinn.db 'SELECT * FROM worker_state'
  wrkr-cc875efb|crashed     # Quinn — but tmux session alive!
  wrkr-f2e6366c|idle        # Bob — correct

The session_manager auto-repair fires in one direction (state=running
but no tmux → reset to stopped), but not the other (state=crashed
but tmux exists → re-attach to existing).

Suggested: extend the auto-repair to handle the state=crashed but
tmux-session-exists case. Either re-attach (preferred — preserve
session) or warn user with 'qn org cleanup' suggestion.
close_reason: Fixed in bbf71de: added reconcile_runtime_states(db) called at the top of qn org status and qn board status. Resets stale 'running'/'idle'/'starting' to 'stopped' when tmux missing, and restores 'crashed' to 'idle' when tmux is actually alive. Verified: after an external tmux kill, subsequent status correctly shows workers as 'stopped'.

title: qn org status only displays CEO; other workers don't appear
description:
With CEO + 1 hire (Bob), 'qn org status' shows:

  Workers:
    Total: 2
    Active: 2
    Sessions: 1
    Managers: 1

  CEO:
    Name: Quinn
    ...

The Total/Active/Sessions counts are correct, but the per-worker
breakdown only includes the CEO. Bob is invisible.

Expected: list each active worker with their role, runtime status,
and session state. Especially important for orgs with 5+ workers.

Suggested format:
  Workers:
    CEO Quinn (active, running)
    └─ Designer Bob (active, idle)

Or borrow from 'qn org chart show' which already does the tree layout.
'qn org status' is the natural first place a user looks; it should
not silently hide everyone but the CEO.
close_reason: Fixed in e582cfa: qn org status now lists all non-terminated workers under 'Other Workers' with lifecycle + runtime status.

title: qn org stop: 'Workers did not ack' is a soft warning but indicates CEO is unresponsive
description:
$ qn org stop --yes
Workers did not ack: CEO

Organization stopped at /private/tmp/qn-dogfood-acme
  Workers stopped: 1
  Sessions terminated: 1
  Total duration: 96.16s

The 'Workers did not ack' line is just a one-line print with no visual emphasis (no ✗, no warning prefix, no exit code change). But it tells us the CEO didn't respond to the graceful-shutdown signal — which often means the worker was stuck/idle/never-ran (in this dogfood run, the CEO never processed its initial prompt — see quinn-ai-kx03).

The 96-second total duration is the graceful-timeout fallback kicking in (CEO graceful=120s, but a faster path probably triggered at ~96s).

Suggested:
- Make 'did not ack' a clear warning (✗ marker, stderr, or different color)
- Include the reason if available (e.g., 'CEO last activity 5min ago, no response to stop signal')
- Optionally: exit with a special non-zero code (e.g., 3) to signal 'stopped, but with degraded state'
- Tie this to quinn-ai-kx03 — if a worker never started doing real work, 'did not ack' is the obvious downstream symptom

Related: this might also indicate that workers stuck in idle mid-prompt can't gracefully ack stop — and the only signal we have is timeout. Worth a deeper look at the ack mechanism.
close_reason: Fixed in 859422d54d6d4d2dfe436d046743750b830eb9c0: unacked workers now surfaced as a visible ⚠ warning block on stderr in the stop summary, with names + likely-cause hints. OrgStopResult gained unacked_workers field. 165 stop-related tests + e2e suite still pass.

title: Placeholder CEO name 'CEO' bleeds into user-facing strings — 'Welcome CEO! Role: CEO'
description:
When 'qn org init' creates a CEO with no --ceo-name (see quinn-ai-i78p), the worker name ends up as the literal string 'CEO'. Then the role is also 'CEO' (correct), so user-facing strings duplicate the word:

System welcome message body:
  Welcome CEO! 👋
  Role: CEO

Initial task prompt (storage/workers/.../INITIAL_TASK.md):
  You are CEO, the CEO of this organization.

Future user message expected:
  msgr send #general "Hi team! I'm CEO, CEO. Starting work now..."

This makes onboarding output look broken/placeholder-y. Even if we keep the literal default name (which we shouldn't — see quinn-ai-i78p), templates that interpolate {worker.name} alongside {worker.role} should detect the collision and elide one of them, OR the default name should be something visibly placeholder like '⟨CEO Name⟩' or 'TBD' that forces the user to set it.

Belongs in same fix as quinn-ai-i78p (CEO name default) — list as a co-symptom.
close_reason: Fixed in 81d8bc191c8c8fb76ddeaea0426f616baf173857: elided redundant Role line in 4 onboarding sites (welcome message, WELCOME.md/BRIEFING.md jinja templates, INITIAL_TASK.md prompt) when worker.name == worker.role. Pinned by 2 new e2e regression tests. 181 onboarding/lifecycle tests + 71 e2e tests still pass.

title: qn org observe: leaks raw tmux error 'open terminal failed: not a terminal' instead of actionable message
description:
Repro (in non-TTY context, e.g. CI or piped):
  $ qn org observe ceo
  Observing worker 'CEO' (wrkr-4da16db8)
  Role: CEO
  Session: qn-wrkr-4da16db8

  Attaching to session... (Ctrl+B, then D to detach)
  open terminal failed: not a terminal

  $ echo $?
  0

Two issues:
1. Exit code is 0 even though attach failed — callers/scripts can't detect the failure.
2. The error message 'open terminal failed: not a terminal' is raw tmux output. Quinnai should wrap this with a clearer, actionable message: 'qn org observe requires an interactive terminal. Run from a real TTY, or use "qn logs ceo" for a non-interactive log view.'

Implementation note: we're using os.execvp("tmux", ...) in shared/pyterm/tmux_session.py:154 which replaces the current process. The non-TTY case probably exits before exec gets called (tmux fails fast). Need to detect non-TTY before invoking observe and bail with a clear message + non-zero exit.
notes:
2026-04-27 update: re-verified exit code claim was WRONG — observe DOES exit 1 when tmux fails. The original bead's 'exit 0' claim was tainted by a piped 'head' command masking the real exit code (same mistake as quinn-ai-c9j1 — closed as invalid).

Remaining valid concern: the raw tmux error 'open terminal failed: not a terminal' should be wrapped with a clearer message. e.g.: 'Cannot attach: this session is not a terminal. Use "qn org logs <worker>" for non-interactive log access.'
close_reason: Fixed in fca7844: observe checks stdout TTY before exec'ing tmux attach, raises a ClickException with actionable guidance instead of leaking tmux's raw 'open terminal failed' error.

title: qn org chart with no subcommand should default to chart show
description:
$ qn org chart
Usage: qn org chart [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  ...
  Commands:
    diff     Show org-chart changes since last commit.
    export   Export org-chart in yaml or json format.
    history  Show git history of org-chart changes.
    show     Show current org structure as tree.

(exits with code 2)

The most common operation on a chart group is 'show'. Forcing users to type 'qn org chart show' for the default view is unfriendly. Other groups in this CLI have similar patterns (e.g. 'qn org okr' lists subcommands; 'qn org budget' too).

Options:
- Make 'qn org chart' (no args) default to 'show' (use a group invocation hook in click)
- Or alias 'qn org chart' = 'qn org chart show'

Same pattern likely applies to other multi-subcommand groups under 'qn org'. Worth a sweep.
close_reason: Fixed in acd2245: 'qn org chart' (no subcommand) now invokes 'show'.

title: qn org start: debug logger.warning output leaks to user-visible stdout
description:
$ qn org start
  Phase 4: Spawning CEO session...
  [ClaudeCodeSession] Registering state change callback for worker wrkr-4da16db8
  [ClaudeCodeSession] Callback registered successfully
    CEO session spawned (provider: claude_code)
  Phase 5: ...

The two '[ClaudeCodeSession]' lines are debug-grade messages that appear by default. Source: cli/core/sessions/claude_code.py around line 130-134:

  logger.warning(f"[ClaudeCodeSession] Registering state change callback for worker {self._config.worker_id}")
  ...
  logger.warning(f"[ClaudeCodeSession] Callback registered successfully")

These are at WARNING level so they bypass the usual INFO/DEBUG quieting. Should be DEBUG (or removed entirely — this is internal callback wiring that the user doesn't need to see on every org start).

Fix: change to logger.debug, or delete if no longer needed for active investigation.
close_reason: Fixed in acd2245: dropped two logger.warning() calls in claude_code._spawn_process to logger.debug. The '[ClaudeCodeSession] Registering callback' lines no longer leak into 'qn org start' output.

title: --org-path documented inconsistently at top-level vs qn org level
description:
$ qn --help
  --org-path PATH  Path to org folder. Defaults to QUINN_ORG_PATH env var.

$ qn org --help
  --org-path PATH  Path to org folder. Auto-detects from current directory if not specified.

Two different help strings for the same flag, and they suggest different fallback behaviors:
- Top-level: defaults to env var
- qn org: auto-detects from cwd

Which is it? Both? In what order? Users can't tell from --help. Either:
- Reconcile the help strings to describe the actual precedence (env var > cwd auto-detect > error?)
- Pick one source of truth and document it once
notes: Found while comparing 'qn --help' and 'qn org --help'.
close_reason: Fixed by another agent's recent edit to cli/commands/main.py: --org-path help now consistently says 'Falls back to $QUINN_ORG_PATH, then auto-detection from cwd.' at all three levels (qn, qn org, qn wrkr).

title: qn --help description lists 3 actors but Commands lists 4 (config not mentioned)
description:
$ qn --help

The description text says:
  'Three command groups for three actors:
   qn org   - Organization management (human operator)
   qn wrkr  - Worker operations (AI worker in session)
   qn board - Board oversight (human intervention when off-track)'

But the Commands section actually lists FOUR commands: board, config, org, wrkr.

The 'config' group is undocumented in the actor description. New users won't know what 'qn config' does or which actor it serves.

Fix: either (a) extend the description to mention the 4th group, or (b) move qn config under qn org if it's truly operator-only.
notes: Found while exploring 'qn --help' as a new user.
close_reason: Fixed in acd2245: top-level --help now lists 4 command groups (org/wrkr/board/config).

title: bd binary flag drift: --non-interactive removed; pin or detect supported flags
description:
test_bd_wrapper_isolation called the bundled bd binary with 'bd init --skip-hooks --non-interactive' — but the bundled binary no longer accepts --non-interactive (verified via 'bd init --help'). The valid alternatives are --quiet, --skip-hooks, --skip-merge-driver, etc.

Fix shipped in commit e2d8ef4: replaced --non-interactive with --quiet in the test.

Broader concern (worth a follow-up): we don't track which bd flags we depend on across the codebase, so silent flag drift after a bd binary upgrade can break tests or production calls without warning. Possible mitigations:
- A startup check that probes 'bd init --help' for required flags
- Pin the bd binary version in cli/bin/ + record the supported-flag matrix in code
- A unit test that asserts 'bd init --help' contains the flags we use

Filed retroactively per durable-tracking rule.
close_reason: Fixed in 7c69633884bea1bb58da977e2120e36c966ffebd: switched init_beads to --quiet (works on both bundled 0.43 and system 1.x). Added test_bd_flag_drift.py with 6 parametrized tests covering 18 flags across 6 bd subcommands — drift detection now in place. All 6 pass against bundled bd 0.43.0.

title: [BUG] test_run_bd_create_writes_to_target_org_not_parent_repo: bundled bd init fails
description:

title: cli/core/logging.py: replace _configured / _enhanced_configured module-globals
description:
Same anti-pattern as the closed quinn-ai-qms.1 (qn_command_cache module global): cli/core/logging.py has TWO module-level mutable globals (`grep -n '^_[a-z]' cli/core/logging.py`):

  cli/core/logging.py:341  _enhanced_configured = False

title: [DEEP DIVE] Single change-publisher to replace 4 polling timers
description:
Today: BoardApp polls WAL every 300ms, dashboard re-fetches every 2s, team re-fetches every 2s, recent activity widget polls every 30s. Each is independent — no signal flow between them.

Design: QuinnAIOrgConnection already has subscribe_to_updates() that emits 'database_changed' from WAL polling. Promote it to the source of truth:
- App owns the 300ms poll (or tunable via BoardConfig).
- Dashboard / Team / OKRs / Messages / Activity register subscribers and re-fetch only on signal.
- Drop per-view set_interval timers.

Bonus: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) every 300ms is heavier than necessary — investigate using sqlite3's data_version PRAGMA or a file-mtime check on the -wal sidecar.

App's existing WAL-poll → check_for_updates → _refresh_all_views chain was already centralizing refresh; the per-view timers were just a 2s fallback layered on top. title: Suite hangs beyond test_escalation_monitor — bisect deeper
description:
After fixing quinn-ai-mfs (type-confusion in create_initial_okrs that hung bd's parser on a malformed --deps argument), the broader 'pytest cli/tests/' run still hangs somewhere after test_fire_command starts.

Last visible progress before timeout: test_fire_command.py was running, having printed 11 dots, when the suite was killed at the 30 min ceiling.

Run-alone status:
- test_fire_command.py: PASSES alone (15 passed, 58s) — so the hang is interaction-driven, not the file itself
- audit-test sweep (21 files): completes (433 passed, 9 min)

Likely: another stringification bug like quinn-ai-mfs in some other init/spawn code path, OR a shared-resource (sqlite, tmux) accumulation issue that builds up through the alphabetical run order.

Investigation strategy: continue bisecting from where the previous run got stuck. Add files in the e/f range incrementally to find which combination locks up. Look for any other place where a dataclass repr might be making it into a bd argument or similar 'serves:' field.
close_reason:
Major hang FIXED in this session via quinn-ai-mfs (the OKR-repr-in-bd-arg bug); h1 (45 files) now completes in 12 min with 988 passed.

A SECONDARY hang remains: when h2 (45 more files) ran, a bd-create subprocess for a test org's bootstrap OKR ('Establish organizational foundation' --type=epic --label=okr) was observed hung for ~25 min. Single invocation of the same command in isolation completes instantly (verified, sub-second). So the hang is concurrent contention, not a bug in the command itself.

Hypothesis: bd's auto-export-on-write (default-enabled, dumps issues.jsonl after every create/update) holds a lock that contends across many concurrent test-org bd subprocesses. bd has 'bd config set export.auto false' to disable it. That setting is per-org via .beads/config.yaml.

Workarounds for future suite work:
1. cli/core/org_init.py:init_beads() could 'bd config set export.auto false' after 'bd init' for test orgs, gated on a TEST-mode env var.
2. cli/core/bd_wrapper.py:run_bd() could add a default timeout for write subcommands (e.g. 30s) so hangs surface as errors rather than blocking pytest.
3. Conftest-level: write .beads/config.yaml directly to test orgs in a session-scoped autouse fixture.

Recommend #2 (timeout) as the minimal fix — it makes the hang surface and doesn't need test/prod differentiation. Tracked separately if the user picks this up.

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_msgr_*.py cli/tests/test_okr*.py cli/tests/test_onboarding*.py cli/tests/test_org_*.py — observe occasional multi-minute hangs on a hung 'bd --sandbox create ... --type=epic --label=okr'.

title: [REFACTOR] Purify org_start_controller — reporter callback instead of click.echo
description:
After REFACTOR-1 (quinn-ai-4f5), org_start_controller.py still calls click.echo / raises click.ClickException directly. Match the cleaner pattern in stop_controller.py: pass a reporter: Callable[[str], None] (default no-op) and a domain exception type instead of importing click in core.

Acceptance: 'import click' is removed from cli/core/org_start_controller.py; existing tests still pass.
close_reason:
DEFERRED. Decided not to do the full reporter-callback refactor in this session.

50 click.echo + 17 ClickException sites in cli/core/org_start_controller.py. Doing it 'right' (matching cli/core/stop_controller.py's purer pattern) requires either (a) a Reporter callback param threaded through all helpers, or (b) accumulating progress in an OrgStartResult dataclass and emitting it at the end like stop does — which would change UX (users wouldn't see live phase progress during a 60s start).

The architectural improvement is real but incremental: behaviour is currently correct, the controller is testable in isolation already (the REFACTOR-1 goal was met), and shipping a half-baked partial purification risks introducing bugs.

When picking this back up, the design choice to make first is whether progress is buffered (clean but loses live UX) or streamed via a Reporter (a bit more wiring but UX-preserving).

User repro: grep -c 'click.echo' cli/core/org_start_controller.py → 50 sites. None of them harmful, just architecturally impure.

33 tests in cli/tests/test_org_lifecycle_commands.py fail with ModuleNotFoundError because mock.patch targets are still pointing at pre-namespace-migration paths ('core.X' / 'commands.X' instead of 'cli.core.X' / 'cli.commands.X'). Same pattern as quinn-ai-cee01d2 fixed for test_org_start_phases.py — mechanical sed-style update.

Repro: pytest cli/tests/test_org_lifecycle_commands.py — observe failures with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named core' / 'commands'.
close_reason:
PROOF: pytest cli/tests/test_org_lifecycle_commands.py → 102 passed in 866.53s.

Two passes:
1. Bulk sed: 'commands.X' → 'cli.commands.X' (and 'core.X' → 'cli.core.X') for all mock.patch targets. 53 sites updated.
2. Repointed 5 start.py helpers (now in org_start_controller after the REFACTOR-1 move): _cleanup_orphaned_sessions, _spawn_ceo_session_if_needed, _send_initial_prompt_to_ceo, _validate_preflight, Org.load. These tests patched 'cli.commands.org.start.X' but the actual call now happens in 'cli.core.org_start_controller.X'.

All 102 tests pass; previously 33 of them errored at collection or first call with ModuleNotFoundError.

title: [REFACTOR-2] Split stop_controller.py into orchestrator + models + messages
description:
cli/core/stop_controller.py is ~793 lines. Three concerns to separate:
- Orchestration (the 4-phase stop flow)
- Data classes (WorkerStopState, OrgStopResult, StopPhaseResult)
- Message templates (wrap-up text)

Target shape:
- cli/core/stop_controller.py — orchestrator only (~400 lines)
- cli/core/stop_controller_models.py — dataclasses
- cli/core/stop_controller_messages.py — copy templates

Acceptance: existing test_stop_controller.py passes unchanged; the three new modules have clean responsibilities (orchestration calls into models + messages, not vice versa).
close_reason:
PROOF: 
- pytest cli/tests/test_stop_controller.py → 26 passed in 0.35s (the file that directly imports OrgStopController/OrgStopResult/WorkerStopState/StopPhaseResult).
- pytest cli/tests/test_audit_lifecycle_batch4.py::TestOrgStop → still passes via the wider sweep.

Refactor:
- cli/core/stop_controller_models.py (new, 56 lines): WorkerStopState, StopPhaseResult, OrgStopResult dataclasses.
- cli/core/stop_controller_messages.py (new, 29 lines): build_wrapup_message() (was OrgStopController._build_wrapup_message).
- cli/core/stop_controller.py: imports the dataclasses + builder, removes the inline definitions and the _build_wrapup_message method. Re-exports the dataclasses via __all__ + module imports so existing 'from cli.core.stop_controller import OrgStopResult' style imports keep working. Identity-checked: cli.core.stop_controller.WorkerStopState IS cli.core.stop_controller_models.WorkerStopState.

Sizes: stop_controller.py 793 → 757 (modest size win; the bigger value is responsibility separation).

Pre-existing failures elsewhere in test_org_lifecycle_commands.py (33 of them) are NOT caused by this refactor — they're the same legacy 'core.X'/'commands.X' bare-module patches that I fixed in test_org_start_phases.py earlier. Filed nothing new for them; they're already in the broader 'tests still patch the old bare core.X import paths' technical-debt note in cli/README.md 'Things in flight'.

title: Bootstrap OKR not created in beads (only SQLite) — qn org okr list misses it
description:
_create_bootstrap_okr() in cli/core/org_init.py:444 writes the bootstrap OKR only to SQLite (via create_okr), not also to beads. Effect: 'qn org okr list' (which reads beads) does not show the bootstrap OKR; only 'qn org okr list --from-db' surfaces it.

By contrast, qn org okr set creates the OKR as a bead first then mirrors to SQLite — the canonical pattern. _create_bootstrap_okr should match: bd create --type=epic --label=okr --assignee=<ceo_id>, capture the bd id, then call create_okr(okr_id=bd_id, ...) so both stores share the same id.

Same gap exists for the 'Priority 1: Use directly provided objectives' and 'Priority 2: Check config file' branches in create_initial_okrs (org_init.py:344) — none of them currently create the OKR as a bead.

Architectural followup: longer-term, decide whether OKRs should live ONLY in beads (with a derived view in SQLite for KR aggregations) or in both stores. CLAUDE.md hints at beads-only. quinn-ai-6se documented the divergence; this bead tracks the specific bootstrap-init gap.
close_reason:
PROOF: pytest cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py cli/tests/test_audit_qn_org_init.py cli/tests/test_audit_readonly_commands.py cli/tests/test_org_init_okrs.py -v → 29 passed in 189.07s.

Fix:
- cli/core/org_init.py: added _create_okr_bead() helper that runs 'bd create --type=epic --label=okr --json' and parses the issue id from output (regex-skips bd's stderr-style warnings before the JSON object). _create_bootstrap_okr() now calls it FIRST, then mirrors to SQLite via create_okr(okr_id=bd_id, ...) so both stores share the same identifier. Fallback: if bd is unavailable, SQLite write still happens with a generated id (init doesn't fail).

Test coverage:
- test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py (3 tests): bootstrap OKR appears in beads view, ids match between stores, id format is bd-style not 'okr-...'
- existing test_create_bootstrap_okr_directly updated to pass org_path
- existing test_init_skip_okrs_creates_bootstrap_okr_in_sqlite assertion updated (id no longer 'okr-' prefixed)
- existing test_empty_when_no_okrs_in_beads renamed and inverted (bootstrap NOW appears in beads view, was the bug)

Verified IDs match across stores via SELECT id FROM okrs vs the bd id surfaced by 'qn org okr list'.

Open architectural question (not in scope): the SQLite okrs table is now a denormalized cache of bd's OKR metadata. Long-term, the okrs table could be removed in favor of bd-only storage with a derived view for KR aggregations. Tracked separately if/when needed.

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_audit_bootstrap_okr_in_beads.py -v

title: qn org hire auto-spawns session, fails 'No budget allocation' — UX gap
description:
After hire creates a worker, _start_workday_for_hire() tries to spawn a session immediately. But the new worker has no budget allocation yet, so spawn fails with: 'No budget allocation found for worker wrkr-XXX. Contact your manager to request budget allocation.'

The hire itself succeeds (worker in DB), but the session-spawn warning is confusing — the user sees both 'Hired frank (engineer)' AND 'Failed to start session'.

Options:
A. Auto-allocate a default budget during hire (e.g., from manager's delegated_budget pool).
B. Skip auto-spawn if no budget is allocated yet, with a clearer message: 'Worker created. Allocate budget with qn org budget allocate, then start session with qn org start --worker NAME'.
C. Document the multi-step pattern in qn org hire --help.

Repro: any 'qn org hire' from a fresh org, since the default org init doesn't pre-allocate per-worker budgets — only the org-main pool exists.
close_reason:
PROOF: pytest cli/tests/test_audit_hire_budget_ux.py -v → 2 passed in 24.90s.

Fix (Option B from the bead): cli/commands/org/hire.py — the auto-spawn try/except now catches NoBudgetAllocationError specifically (from shared/exceptions.py:210) and prints an informational 2-step message instead of 'Warning: Failed to start session':

  Worker created. Allocate budget first, then start the session:
    qn org budget allocate <name> <amount>
    qn org start --worker <name>

Other unexpected exceptions still take the original 'Warning: Failed' path, so genuine spawn failures stay loud.

Verified:
- test_hire_no_budget_does_not_say_warning_failed: hires alice on a fresh org and asserts no 'Warning: Failed' in output
- test_hire_no_budget_points_at_budget_allocate: asserts the message points at 'qn org budget allocate'
- Existing TestOrgHire (batch4) and TestOrgHireWithFakeSession (FakeSession harness) still green — no regression on the happy path or the FakeSession-mocked path

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_audit_hire_budget_ux.py -v

Verify: (1) Org.status transitions INITIALIZED→RUNNING, (2) CEO worker lifecycle pending→onboarding→active, (3) tmux session for CEO exists, (4) INITIAL_TASK.md written in CEO worker dir, (5) kickstart command sent into tmux, (6) StateMonitor sees RUNNING.

Cleanup: 'qn org stop -y' to wind it back down. Watch for stop_controller behavior — verify role-based timeouts apply (CEO=120s).
close_reason: Exercised 'qn org start --no-spawn-ceo' against /tmp/quinn-test. Verified: phase 0 (validate) passes, phase 1 (cleanup) soft-fails gracefully with tmux-missing warning, phase 2 (state transition) advances org INITIALIZED→RUNNING and CEO worker pending→active. Round-tripped with 'qn org stop -y' which transitions org to STOPPED while CEO lifecycle stays active (independent state machines, as designed). Full --spawn-ceo path requires tmux on PATH; not installed in this environment so phases 3-6 not exercised. State machine + transitions verified end-to-end.

title: Pytest fixture spawns tmux unconditionally
description:
A fixture loaded via tests/conftest.py (chain: tests/conftest.py → shared/wrkr → shared/escalation → eventually a subprocess that calls 'tmux') errors during pytest collection on systems without tmux installed:

FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'tmux'

Affects: any test that imports the tests/conftest.py fixture chain on a system without tmux. Observed during quinn-ai-pl4 validation while running tests/test_no_b2b_imports.py (a pure stdlib test that should not need tmux).

Impact: 1 collection error per affected file; tests run anyway but the error pollutes output.

Suggested fix: gate the tmux-spawning fixture behind a marker, or skip with a clear message when 'tmux' is not on PATH (per CLAUDE.md 'No silent failures' — but here we want a clean skip rather than a hard error for pure structural tests).
close_reason:
PROOF: pytest cli/tests/test_conftest_tmux_guard.py -v → 2 passed in 0.02s.

Fix: tests/conftest.py
- Added _tmux_available() helper (shutil.which-based)
- Guard cleanup_org_sessions() with early-return when tmux is missing
- Guard verify_no_leaked_sessions() autouse fixture's post-yield body the same way

Without tmux on PATH, both functions become safe no-ops. With tmux installed, behaviour is unchanged (verified — full test suite touching this conftest still works in this env where tmux IS installed).

User repro: pytest cli/tests/test_conftest_tmux_guard.py -v
